claims.statement: Dormarch, or possibly Dormarth, is a hound; in Welsh mythology Dormarch's master is Gwynn ap Nudd, though it was formerly owned by Maelgwn Gwynedd, a 6th-century king of Gwynedd.
claims.statement_id: Dormarch atau mungkin Dormarth adalah seekor anjing pemburu; dalam mitologi Welsh tuannya adalah Gwynn ap Nudd, walau dulu dimiliki Maelgwn Gwynedd, raja Gwynedd abad ke-6.
claims.quote: Dormarch or possibly Dormarth is a hound, normally used to assist hunters by tracking or chasing the animal that is being hunted, however in Welsh mythology Dormarch's master is Gwynn ap Nudd although formerly owned by Maelgwn Gwynedd, a 6th-century king of Gwynedd.

claims.statement: As king of the Tylwyth Teg (fairy folk), Gwynn ap Nudd ruled Annwn and is closely associated with the Wild Hunt, escorting the newly deceased souls of British warriors from the battlefield to the afterlife.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai raja Tylwyth Teg (bangsa peri), Gwynn ap Nudd menguasai Annwn dan erat dengan Wild Hunt, tempat ia mengantar arwah prajurit Britania (British) yang baru gugur dari medan perang ke alam baka.
claims.quote: As king of the Tylwyth Teg or fairy folk, Gwynn ap Nudd was the ruler of Annwn ... he is closely associated with the Wild Hunt where he is responsible for escorting newly deceased souls of British warriors from the battlefield to the afterlife.

claims.statement: Dormarch has a single head, two front legs, and a body that narrows rapidly from the chest and ends in three fish-like tails.
claims.statement_id: Dormarch berkepala satu, berkaki depan dua, dan tubuhnya cepat menyempit dari dada lalu berakhir pada tiga ekor mirip ekor ikan.
claims.quote: Dormarch has a single head, two front legs, and a body that narrows rapidly from the chest and terminates in three fish-like tails.

claims.statement: The Dormarch's natural habitat is described in Welsh as 'ar wybir', 'riding on the clouds' that haunt the mountain peaks.
claims.statement_id: Habitat alami Dormarch dilukiskan dalam bahasa Welsh sebagai 'ar wybir', yaitu 'menunggang awan' yang menyelimuti puncak-puncak gunung.
claims.quote: The Dormarch's natural habitat is described in Welsh as being 'ar wybir', that is 'riding on the clouds' which haunt the mountain peaks.

claims.statement: Gwyn gathers the souls of fallen British warriors with the help of his hounds, making Dormarch a member of the Cŵn Annwn, the 'Hounds of Annwn'.
claims.statement_id: Gwyn mengumpulkan arwah prajurit Britania yang gugur dengan bantuan anjing-anjingnya, sehingga Dormarch tergolong Cŵn Annwn, 'Anjing-Anjing Annwn'.
claims.quote: gathering the souls of fallen British warriors with the help of his hounds, thereby making Dormarch a member of the Cŵn Annwn, the 'Hounds of Annwn'.

claims.statement: The Dialogue of Gwyn ap Nudd and Gwyddno Garanhir is found in the Black Book of Carmarthen.
claims.statement_id: Dialog antara Gwyn ap Nudd dan Gwyddno Garanhir terdapat dalam naskah Black Book of Carmarthen.
claims.quote: The Dialogue of Gwyn ap Nudd and Gwyddno Garanhir is found in the Black Book of Carmarthen

claims.statement: Dormarch is pictured on page 97 of Evans' Black Book of Carmarthen in a Christianised form that reduces its canine traits and draws on whales of Biblical legend, typically that of Jonah.
claims.statement_id: Dormarch digambarkan di halaman 97 edisi Black Book of Carmarthen karya Evans dalam bentuk yang dikristenkan: ciri anjingnya dikurangi dan mengambil pengaruh paus dalam kisah Alkitab, terutama kisah Yunus (Jonah).
claims.quote: Dormarch is shown as a pictorial representation on page 97 of Evans' Black Book of Carmarthen in a Christianised form that reduces the canine attributes and instead draws from influences such as whales in Biblical legends, typically that of Jonah.

claims.statement: The form 'Dormarth' has been interpreted as 'Death's door', though contradictory evidence exists, and the word 'mach' translates as 'a bail or surety'.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk 'Dormarth' pernah ditafsirkan sebagai 'Pintu Maut' (Death's door), meski ada bukti yang bertentangan; kata 'mach' berarti 'jaminan'.
claims.quote: The form "Dormarth" has been interpreted as 'Death's door' although contradictory evidence exists and the word "mach" translates as 'a bail or surety'.

claims.statement: Similar Wild Hunt hounds are found in other traditions, such as the Gabriel Hounds, Ratchets, Yell Hounds (Isle of Man) and Herne the Hunter's hounds.
claims.statement_id: Anjing Wild Hunt serupa ada dalam tradisi lain, misalnya Gabriel Hounds, Ratchets, Yell Hounds (Isle of Man), dan anjing-anjing Herne the Hunter.
claims.quote: Similar Wild Hunt hounds are found in other traditions, such as the Gabriel Hounds, Ratchets, Yell Hounds (Isle of Man), Herne the Hunter's hounds, etc.

claims.statement: In one translation of the poem the dog is called Dormath, which belonged to Maelgwyn.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu terjemahan syair, anjing itu disebut Dormath, yang dahulu milik Maelgwyn.
claims.quote: Dormath was he, which belonged to Maelgwyn.

claims.statement: Evans compares it with Cerberus, a bodiless three-headed monster with a serpent's tail; Dormarch differs in having two front legs and but one head.
claims.statement_id: Evans membandingkannya dengan Cerberus, monster tak bertubuh berkepala tiga dengan ekor ular; Dormarch berbeda karena memiliki dua kaki depan dan hanya satu kepala.
claims.quote: Cerberus was a bodiless three-headed monster, with a serpent's tail. Dormarch differs in having two front legs, and but one head.

claims.statement: According to Evans, his body is attenuated into a sort of forked tail ending in fan-like ends.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Evans, tubuhnya meruncing menjadi semacam ekor bercabang yang ujungnya berbentuk kipas.
claims.quote: His body, however, is attenuated into a sort of forked tail, terminating in fan-like ends.

claims.statement: The text informs us that he moved 'ar wybir', i.e. rode on the clouds which haunt mountain-tops.
claims.statement_id: Menurut teks naskah itu, ia bergerak 'ar wybir', yakni menunggang awan yang menyelimuti puncak gunung.
claims.quote: our text informs us that he moved ar wybir, i.e. rode on the clouds which haunt mountain-tops.

claims.statement: The form and meaning of the dog's name are uncertain; the scribe wrote Dormarch twice, but the r has been erased, probably by a later hand.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk dan arti nama anjing itu tidak pasti; penyalin menulis Dormarch dua kali, tetapi huruf r-nya kemudian dihapus, mungkin oleh tangan yang lebih kemudian.
claims.quote: The form and meaning of the dog's name are uncertain. The scribe wrote Dormarch twice, but the r has been erased, probably by a later hand.

claims.statement: Mach, the amended syllable, means 'a bail, a surety'.
claims.statement_id: Mach, suku kata hasil perbaikan itu, berarti 'jaminan'.
claims.quote: Mach, the amended syllable, means 'a bail, a surety.'

claims.statement: In the poem the speaker calls himself Gwyn, the son of Nud, the lover of Creurdilad, the daughter of Llud.
claims.statement_id: Dalam syair itu penutur memperkenalkan diri sebagai Gwyn, putra Nud, kekasih Creurdilad putri Llud.
claims.quote: Whilst I am called Gwyn, the son of Nud, The lover of Creurdilad, the daughter of Llud.

claims.statement: In Skene's translation the dog is praised as handsome, round-bodied and truly the best of dogs; it belonged to Maelgwn.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Skene, anjing itu dipuji tampan, bertubuh bulat, dan terbaik di antara anjing; dahulu ia milik Maelgwn.
claims.quote: Handsome my dog and round-bodied, And truly the best of dogs ; Dorraach was he, which belonged to Maelgwn.

claims.statement: The poem calls Dormach the one with the ruddy nose, a gazer upon the speaker, and notices his wanderings on Gwibir Vynyd.
claims.statement_id: Syair itu menyebut Dormach berhidung kemerahan, yang menatap penutur, dan menyinggung pengembaraannya di Gwibir Vynyd.
claims.quote: Dormach with the ruddy nose ! what a gazer Thou art upon me ! because I notice Thy wanderings on Gwibir Vynyd.

claims.statement: In Welsh mythology (walisischen Mythologie) Drudwyn is one of the Cŵn Annwn, the hounds of Annwn (Hunde Annwns).
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Welsh (walisischen Mythologie), Drudwyn adalah salah satu Cŵn Annwn, anjing-anjing Annwn (Hunde Annwns).
claims.quote: ist in der walisischen Mythologie einer der Cŵn Annwn, der Hunde Annwns.

claims.statement: According to the German Wikipedia article, he is the young dog (junge Hund) of Greid and a son of Eri (Sohn von Eri).
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel Wikipedia Jerman, ia anjing muda (junge Hund) milik Greid dan putra Eri (Sohn von Eri).
claims.quote: Er ist der junge Hund von Greid und ein Sohn von Eri.

claims.statement: Drudwyn has red ears (rote Ohren) and a white body (weißen Körper).
claims.statement_id: Drudwyn bertelinga merah (rote Ohren) dan bertubuh putih (weißen Körper).
claims.quote: Drudwyn hat rote Ohren und einen weißen Körper.

claims.statement: He could be controlled only by Mabon ap Modron and caught the wild boar (wilden Eber) Twrch Trwyth for him, so that Mabon could snatch the comb and scissors (Kamm und Schere) from it.
claims.statement_id: Ia hanya dapat dikendalikan oleh Mabon ap Modron dan menangkap babi hutan liar (wilden Eber) Twrch Trwyth untuknya, sehingga Mabon bisa merebut sisir dan gunting (Kamm und Schere) darinya.
claims.quote: Er war nur durch Mabon ap Modron zu kontrollieren und fing für ihn den wilden Eber Twrch Trwyth ... so dass Mabon ihm Kamm und Schere entreißen konnte.

claims.statement: A Dunnie is a small Brownie-like being in the folklore of the Anglo-Scottish borders, specifically Northumberland; the most famous is the Hazlerigg Dunnie of Hazlerigg in the parish of Chatton.
claims.statement_id: Dunnie adalah makhluk kecil mirip Brownie dalam cerita rakyat perbatasan Inggris-Skotlandia (Anglo-Scottish borders), khususnya Northumberland; yang paling terkenal adalah Dunnie dari Hazlerigg di paroki Chatton.
claims.quote: A Dunnie is a small Brownie-like being in the folklore of the Anglo-Scottish borders, specifically Northumberland, the most famous being that of the Hazlerigg Dunnie of Hazlerigg in the parish of Chatton, Northumberland.

claims.statement: The Dunnie has been known to take the form of a horse to trick a rider into mounting him, then disappear and leave them in the muddiest part of the road.
claims.statement_id: Dunnie dikenal mengambil wujud kuda untuk memperdaya penunggang agar menaikinya, lalu menghilang dan meninggalkan mereka di bagian jalan yang paling berlumpur.
claims.quote: The Dunnie has been known to take the form of a horse in order to trick a rider into mounting him before disappearing and leaving them in the muddiest part of the road.

claims.statement: He is also said to disguise himself as plough-horses, only to vanish when the ploughman takes him into the stalls.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga dikatakan menyamar sebagai kuda bajak, lalu lenyap ketika pembajak membawanya ke kandang.
claims.quote: He also is said to disguise as plough-horses only to vanish when the ploughman takes him into the stalls.

claims.statement: The Dunnie was also said to wander the crags and dales of the Cheviots singing.
claims.statement_id: Dunnie juga dikatakan berkeliaran di tebing dan lembah Cheviots sambil bernyanyi.
claims.quote: The Dunnie was also said to wander the crags and dales of the Cheviots singing

claims.statement: His song says there is gear enough at Cockenheugh and more at Collierheugh, for he has lost the key o' the Bounders.
claims.statement_id: Lagunya menyebut harta (gear) di Cockenheugh dan lebih banyak lagi di Collierheugh, sementara ia kehilangan kunci 'the Bounders'.
claims.quote: Cockenheugh there's gear enough, Collierheugh there's mair, For I've lost the key o' the Bounders

claims.statement: The Dunnie is thus thought to be the ghost of a reiver who hoarded his loot in the fells and guards his ill-gotten gains to this day.
claims.statement_id: Karena itu Dunnie dianggap hantu seorang perampok perbatasan (reiver) yang menimbun jarahannya di perbukitan dan menjaga harta haramnya sampai sekarang.
claims.quote: The Dunnie is thus thought to be a ghost of a reiver who hoarded his loot in the fells and guards his ill-gotten gains to this day.

claims.statement: Henderson says this sprite is called the Dunnie, appears to be of the Brownie type, and is located at Haselrigg, in the parish of Chatton, in Northumberland.
claims.statement_id: Henderson menyebut sprite ini Dunnie, tampaknya dari jenis Brownie, dan bertempat di Haselrigg, paroki Chatton, Northumberland.
claims.quote: sprite is called the Dunnie ; he appears to be of the Brownie type, and is located at Haselrigg, in the parish of Chatton, in Northumberland.

claims.statement: Like others of his race, he is much addicted to mischievous, troublesome tricks.
claims.statement_id: Seperti makhluk sejenisnya, ia sangat gemar melakukan tipu daya yang jahil dan merepotkan.
claims.quote: Like others of his race, he is much addicted to mischievous, troublesome tricks

claims.statement: When a farmer's family wants the midwife and the master goes out to saddle his horse to fetch her, the Dunnie will take its form.
claims.statement_id: Ketika keluarga petani membutuhkan bidan dan sang tuan keluar untuk memasang pelana kudanya, Dunnie akan mengambil wujud kuda itu.
claims.quote: When the midwife is wanted in a farmer's family, and the master goes out to saddle his horse that he may fetch her, the Dunnie will take its form.

claims.statement: On the way back he will suddenly vanish and leave the unhappy pair floundering in the mud.
claims.statement_id: Dalam perjalanan pulang ia tiba-tiba menghilang dan meninggalkan petani serta bidan itu menggelepar di lumpur.
claims.quote: he will suddenly vanish, and leave the unhappy pair floundering in the mud.

claims.statement: A ploughman who thinks he has harnessed his horse will see the harness come 'slap to the ground' while the steed kicks up his heels and starts across the country like the wind.
claims.statement_id: Pembajak yang mengira sudah memasang tali kekang pada kudanya akan melihat tali itu jatuh ke tanah, sementara kuda itu menendang dan berlari melintasi daerah itu secepat angin.
claims.quote: see the harness come " slap to the ground," while the steed kicks up his heels and starts across the country like the wind.

claims.statement: Some years ago the Dunnie was often seen wandering among the crags of the Cheviots and heard repeating a verse again and again in a melancholy voice.
claims.statement_id: Beberapa tahun sebelumnya, Dunnie sering terlihat berkeliaran di antara tebing Cheviots dan terdengar mengulang-ulang sebuah bait dengan suara sedih.
claims.quote: Some years ago, the Dunnie was often seen wandering among the crags of the Cheviots, and heard repeating the following verse again and again, in a melancholy voice

claims.statement: Hence it has been thought that the Dunnie is really the ghost of a 'reiver' who hoarded his ill-gotten pelf in those crags and therefore haunts them constantly.
claims.statement_id: Karena itu Dunnie diduga sebenarnya hantu seorang 'reiver' yang menimbun harta haramnya di tebing-tebing itu dan karenanya terus menghantuinya.
claims.quote: Hence it has been thought that the Dunnie is really the ghost of a " reiver," who had hoarded his ill-gotten pelf in those crags, and therefore haunts them constantly.

claims.statement: A friend pointed to the steepest part of the rocks and said it was there that Dunnie used to hang his legs over when he sat on the crags at night.
claims.statement_id: Seorang kawan menunjuk bagian batu paling curam di sebuah tambang di Haselrigg dan berkata di situlah Dunnie biasa menjuntaikan kakinya saat duduk di tebing pada malam hari.
claims.quote: a friend pointed to the steepest part of the rocks, and said it was there that Dunnie used to hang over his legs when he sat on the crags at night.

claims.statement: According to Henderson's footnote, the Dunnie, Brag and Hedley Kow are probably the same as the Nick or Nippeu.
claims.statement_id: Menurut catatan kaki Henderson, Dunnie, Brag, dan Hedley Kow mungkin sama dengan Nick atau Nippeu.
claims.quote: The Dunnie, Brag, and Hedley Kow are probably the same as the Nick or Nippeu.

claims.statement: Dyrnwch, nicknamed 'the Giant' (der Riese), also Diwrnach, nicknamed 'the Irishman' (der Ire), Dyrnog, Tyrnog, Irish Diugurach, is a figure of legend (Sagengestalt) from Welsh mythology (walisischen Mythologie).
claims.statement_id: Dyrnwch, berjuluk 'sang Raksasa' (der Riese), juga Diwrnach berjuluk 'orang Irlandia' (der Ire), Dyrnog, Tyrnog, dalam bahasa Irlandia Diugurach, adalah tokoh legenda (Sagengestalt) dari mitologi Welsh (walisischen Mythologie).
claims.quote: Dyrnwch, Beiname „der Riese“, auch Diwrnach, Beiname „der Ire“, Dyrnog, Tyrnog, irisch Diugurach, ist eine Sagengestalt aus der walisischen Mythologie.

claims.statement: In the tale Kulhwch ac Olwen, Olwen's father, the giant (Riese) Ysbaddaden, sets the suitor Kulhwch several hard tasks (schwere Aufgaben).
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Kulhwch ac Olwen, ayah Olwen, raksasa (Riese) Ysbaddaden, memberi pelamar Kulhwch sejumlah tugas berat (schwere Aufgaben).
claims.quote: In der Erzählung Kulhwch ac Olwen („Die Geschichte von Kulhwch und Olwen“) wird berichtet, dass Olwens Vater, der Riese Ysbaddaden, dem Freier Kulhwch einige schwere Aufgaben stellt

claims.statement: One of the tasks is to win the cauldron (Kessel) of the Irish giant (irischen Riesen) Dyrnwch, called Diwrnach in the text, for the wedding feast (Hochzeitsmahl).
claims.statement_id: Salah satu tugasnya adalah merebut kuali (Kessel) milik raksasa Irlandia (irischen Riesen) Dyrnwch, yang dalam teks disebut Diwrnach, untuk jamuan pernikahan (Hochzeitsmahl).
claims.quote: Eine der Aufgabe ist, den Kessel des irischen Riesen Dyrnwch, im Text Diwrnach genannt, für das Hochzeitsmahl zu erringen.

claims.statement: The cauldron (Kessel) can tell bad people (böse) from good people (guten Menschen): for bad people it cooks no food (Essen), for the others it readies a dish very quickly.
claims.statement_id: Kuali (Kessel) itu dapat membedakan orang jahat (böse) dari orang baik (guten Menschen): bagi orang jahat ia tidak memasak makanan (Essen), bagi yang lain ia cepat sekali menyiapkan hidangan.
claims.quote: Dieser Kessel hat die mythische Bedeutung, böse von guten Menschen unterscheiden zu können. Für schlechte Menschen kocht er kein Essen, bei den anderen ist er schnellstens mit einer Speise fertig.

claims.statement: Diwrnach refuses (weigert sich) to hand over the cauldron (Kessel).
claims.statement_id: Diwrnach menolak (weigert sich) menyerahkan kuali (Kessel) itu.
claims.quote: Diwrnach weigert sich, den Kessel herzugeben.

claims.statement: So Bedwyr fab Bedrawg takes the cauldron (Kessel) and has it carried away; his companions kill (töten) Diwrnach and all the Irish (Iren) who want to fight for it.
claims.statement_id: Karena itu Bedwyr fab Bedrawg mengambil kuali (Kessel) itu dan menyuruh membawanya pergi; rekan-rekannya membunuh (töten) Diwrnach dan semua orang Irlandia (Iren) yang hendak memperebutkannya.
claims.quote: Deshalb entwendet Bedwyr fab Bedrawg den Kessel und lässt ihn wegbringen. Seine Gefährten töten Diwrnach und alle Iren, die um den Kessel kämpfen wollen.

claims.statement: This cauldron (Kessel) is one of the Tri Thlws ar Ddeg Ynys Prydain, 'the Thirteen Treasures of the Island of Britain' (dreizehn Schätze der Insel Britannien).
claims.statement_id: Kuali (Kessel) ini termasuk Tri Thlws ar Ddeg Ynys Prydain, 'Tiga Belas Pusaka Pulau Britania' (dreizehn Schätze der Insel Britannien).
claims.quote: Dieser Kessel zählt zu den Tri Thlws ar Ddeg Ynys Prydain („Die dreizehn Schätze der Insel Britannien“).

claims.statement: The Welsh name (kymrische Name) Diwrnach derives from Irish Diugurach (irischen Diugurach), emphasising the Irish origin of the cauldron's owner.
claims.statement_id: Nama Welsh (kymrische Name) Diwrnach diturunkan dari bahasa Irlandia Diugurach (irischen Diugurach), sehingga asal Irlandia pemilik kuali itu ditekankan.
claims.quote: Der kymrische Name Diwrnach wird vom irischen Diugurach abgeleitet, damit wird die irische Herkunft des Kesselbesitzers betont.

claims.statement: Originally the tales of Dyrnwch's cauldron and Diwrnach's cauldron were separate (getrenntes Erzählgut); in Culhwch ac Olwen they were merged over time into a single myth (einzigen Mythos).
claims.statement_id: Semula kisah kuali Dyrnwch dan kisah kuali Diwrnach adalah cerita terpisah (getrenntes Erzählgut); dalam Culhwch ac Olwen keduanya lambat laun disatukan menjadi satu mitos (einzigen Mythos).
claims.quote: Ursprünglich waren die Sagen vom Kessel Dyrnwchs und vom Kessel Diwrnachs getrenntes Erzählgut, in Culhwch ac Olwen wurden sie im Laufe der Zeit zu einem einzigen Mythos vereinigt.

claims.quote: The Cauldron of Dyrnwch the Giant (Pair Dyrnwch Gawr ... "if meat for a coward were put in it to boil, it would never boil; but if meat for a brave man were put in it, it would boil quickly (and thus the brave could be distinguished from the cowardly)".

claims.statement_id: Ia tinggal di celah-celah batu (còsan nan creag) dan di tebing-tebing (bruaichean) di Dataran Tinggi Skotlandia (Gàidhealtachd).
claims.quote: Tha e a' còmhnaidh ann an còsan nan creag agus anns na bruaichean air a' Ghàidhealtachd.

claims.statement: It lives on the same food (lòn) as people, and so depends on people (dhaoine) for its sustenance.
claims.statement_id: Ia hidup dari makanan (lòn) yang sama dengan manusia, sehingga bergantung pada manusia (dhaoine) untuk penghidupannya.
claims.quote: Tha e a' tighinn beò air an aon lòn ri sluagh an t-saoghail; mar sin, tha e an eisimeil dhaoine airson theachd-an-tìr.

claims.statement: Crumbs of food (spruilleach bìdh) used to be left for it on a knoll (cnoc).
claims.statement_id: Orang dulu meninggalkan remah makanan (spruilleach bìdh) untuknya di atas bukit kecil (cnoc).
claims.quote: Bhite a' fàgail spruilleach bìdh dha air cnoc an gorma.

claims.statement: Frid or fride is glossed as gnome, pigmy, elf or rock elfin.
claims.statement_id: Frid atau fride diartikan sebagai gnome, pigmi, elf, atau peri batu (rock elfin).
claims.quote: Frid, fride,' gnome, pigmy, elf, rock elfin.

claims.statement: The term is applied to creatures alleged to dwell inside the rocks and in the innermost parts of the earth.
claims.statement_id: Istilah itu dipakai untuk makhluk yang diyakini tinggal di dalam batu dan di bagian terdalam bumi.
claims.quote: to creatures which they allege dwell in the internal rocks and in the innermost parts of the earth.

claims.statement: People say these gnomes eat and drink like men, and that it is not right to deprive them of crumbs that fall to the ground.
claims.statement_id: Orang berkata makhluk kecil ini makan dan minum seperti manusia, dan tidak patut merampas remah yang jatuh ke tanah dari mereka.
claims.quote: They say that these gnomes eat and drink like men, and that it is not right to deprive them of the crumbs that fall to the ground.

claims.statement: When crumbs of food or drops of milk fall on the floor, the old people object to removing them, saying many needy mouths are awaiting it.
claims.statement_id: Bila remah makanan atau tetes susu jatuh ke lantai, orang tua melarang membersihkannya sambil berkata bahwa banyak mulut yang membutuhkan sedang menunggunya.
claims.quote: When crumbs of food or drops of milk fall on the floor, the old people deprecate removing them, saying ... let it be, many are the needy mouths awaiting it.

claims.quote: never again remove the fragments of food from the floor, they are the rightful dues of " fridich nan creag," the gnomes of the rocks

claims.quote: lose his kine or his sheep or his horses.

claims.statement: Glen Liadail in South Uist was much inhabited by these gnomes, friendly to the people of the glen but resentful of strangers.
claims.statement_id: Glen Liadail di South Uist banyak dihuni makhluk kecil ini, yang ramah kepada warga lembah tetapi tidak suka didatangi orang asing.
claims.quote: Glen Liadail in South Uist was much inhabited by gnomes who, while friendly to the people of the glen, resented the intrusion of strangers.

claims.statement: The fridich are said to go about in clouds like midges, but invisible to mortal eyes.
claims.statement_id: Fridich dikatakan bergerak berkelompok seperti awan agas, tetapi tidak terlihat oleh mata manusia.
claims.quote: who go about in clouds like midges, but invisible to mortal eyes.

claims.statement_id: Karena sangat peka terhadap pujian, mereka tidak mencelakai perempuan yang sendirian itu maupun anaknya.
claims.quote: They, being intensely sensitive to flattery, did no harm to the lonely woman nor to the helpless child

claims.statement: The Girt Dog of Ennerdale was a dog believed to have killed between 300 and 400 sheep in the fells of Cumberland, England, from May to September 1810.
claims.statement_id: Girt Dog of Ennerdale adalah seekor anjing yang diyakini membunuh 300 sampai 400 domba di perbukitan Cumberland, Inggris, dari Mei sampai September 1810.
claims.quote: was a dog believed to have killed between 300 and 400 sheep in the fells of Cumberland, England, from May to September 1810.

claims.statement: It is also known as the Vampire Dog of Ennerdale or the Demon Dog of Ennerdale.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga dikenal sebagai Vampire Dog of Ennerdale atau Demon Dog of Ennerdale.
claims.quote: also known as the Vampire Dog of Ennerdale or Demon Dog of Ennerdale

claims.statement: The adjective "girt" is Cumbrian for "great".
claims.statement_id: Kata sifat "girt" dalam dialek Cumbria berarti "besar" (great).
claims.quote: The adjective "girt" is Cumbrian for "great".

claims.statement: The dog was first seen by Mr Mossop of Thornholme on 10 May 1810 and soon began killing and eating local sheep.
claims.statement_id: Anjing itu pertama kali dilihat oleh Mr Mossop dari Thornholme pada 10 Mei 1810, lalu segera mulai membunuh dan memakan domba setempat.
claims.quote: The dog was first observed by Thornholme resident Mr Mossop on 10 May 1810, and began killing and eating local sheep shortly afterwards.

claims.statement: Its origins are uncertain, though it was speculated that the dog had escaped from "some gipsy troop."
claims.statement_id: Asal-usulnya tidak pasti, tetapi ada dugaan anjing itu kabur dari sebuah rombongan gipsi.
claims.quote: Its origins are uncertain, although it was speculated that the dog had escaped from "some gipsy troop."

claims.statement: Some suggested it may have been a cross between a mastiff and a greyhound.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang menduga ia hasil persilangan mastiff dan greyhound.
claims.quote: Some suggested it may have been a cross between a mastiff and a greyhound.

claims.statement: The Girt Dog usually killed livestock at night.
claims.statement_id: Girt Dog biasanya membunuh ternak pada malam hari.
claims.quote: The Girt Dog of Ennerdale would usually kill livestock at night.

claims.statement: According to one account, the dog drank the sheep's blood directly from the jugular vein.
claims.statement_id: Menurut satu cerita, anjing itu meminum darah domba langsung dari pembuluh leher.
claims.quote: According to one account, the dog would drink the sheep's blood directly from the jugular vein.

claims.statement: Throughout its killing spree the dog was "never known to utter a vocal sound".
claims.statement_id: Selama masa pembantaiannya, anjing itu tidak pernah diketahui mengeluarkan suara.
claims.quote: Throughout its killing spree, the dog was "never known to utter a vocal sound".

claims.statement: John Russell, owner of a brewery in Whitehaven and a sheep farm in Ennerdale, offered a £10 reward for the dog's capture, dead or alive.
claims.statement_id: John Russell, pemilik pabrik bir di Whitehaven dan peternakan domba di Ennerdale, menawarkan hadiah £10 untuk anjing itu, hidup atau mati.
claims.quote: John Russell, who owned a brewery in Whitehaven and a sheep farm in Ennerdale, offered a £10 reward for the dog's capture, dead or alive.

claims.statement: On 12 September 1810 the dog was finally shot dead by John Steel of Asby; its carcass weighed 8 imperial stones (51 kg).
claims.statement_id: Pada 12 September 1810 anjing itu akhirnya ditembak mati oleh John Steel dari Asby; bangkainya seberat 8 stone (51 kg).
claims.quote: On 12 September 1810, the dog was finally shot and killed by John Steel, a resident of Asby. Its carcass weighed 8 imperial stones (51 kg).

claims.statement: Until the late 1800s its taxidermied skin was displayed in Hutton's Museum at Keswick, Cumbria, and was later discarded as it began to rot.
claims.statement_id: Sampai akhir 1800-an kulit awetannya dipamerkan di Hutton's Museum di Keswick, Cumbria, lalu dibuang karena mulai membusuk.
claims.quote: Until the late 1800s, the animal's taxidermied skin was on display in the Hutton's Museum at Keswick, Cumbria; it was discarded at some point due to the corpse beginning to rot.

claims.statement: The smooth-haired dog of a tawny mouse-colour with dark tiger-like streaks over his coat began his murderous career; he weighed eight stones.
claims.statement_id: Anjing berbulu licin berwarna cokelat tikus kekuningan dengan belang gelap seperti harimau itu memulai pembantaiannya; beratnya delapan stone.
claims.quote: smooth-haired dog of a tawny mouse-colour, with dark streaks in tiger fashion over his coat, started his murderous career. He weighed eight stones

claims.statement: Seven or eight sheep were frequently found destroyed in one night.

claims.statement: 'Caer Ogyrfan' is an old name for the hillfort (bryngaer) 'Hen Ddinas' near Croesoswallt.
claims.statement_id: 'Caer Ogyrfan' adalah nama lama benteng bukit (bryngaer) 'Hen Ddinas' dekat Croesoswallt.
claims.quote: Ceir 'Caer Ogyrfan' yn hen enw ar fryngaer 'Hen Ddinas' ger Croesoswallt.

claims.statement: Rachel Bromwich suggests that this Og(y)rfan was an early hero (arwr) of Powys (Bowys).
claims.statement_id: Rachel Bromwich berpendapat bahwa Og(y)rfan ini adalah pahlawan (arwr) awal dari Powys (Bowys).
claims.quote: Awgryma Rachel Bromwich mai arwr cynnar o Bowys oedd yr Og(y)rfan hwn.

claims.statement: It seems likely that the tradition mixes two different characters: a hero from Powys and the Gororau (Marches), and a giant (cawr) who is father of Gwenhwyfar.
claims.statement_id: Tampaknya dalam tradisi terjadi percampuran dua tokoh: seorang pahlawan dari Powys dan daerah Gororau, dan seorang raksasa (cawr) ayah Gwenhwyfar.
claims.quote: Ymddengys yn debygol felly fod cymysgedd yn y traddodiad rhwng dau gymeriad gwahanol, un yn arwr o Bowys a'r Gororau a'r llall yn gawr sy'n dad i Wenhwyfar.

claims.statement: To the cywydd poets (cywyddwyr) the element -fran in the name was clearly "brân" (crow).
claims.statement_id: Bagi para penyair cywydd (cywyddwyr), unsur -fran dalam nama itu jelas dipahami sebagai "brân" (gagak).
claims.quote: Daw'n amlwg mai "brân" oedd yr elfen -fran yn yr enw i'r cywyddwyr.

claims.statement: There is a stream (ffrwd) called Ogran in Sir Fynwy, on which basis the element ogr- is suggested to mean "llym" (sharp), if the form Ogrfan is accepted.
claims.statement_id: Ada sungai kecil bernama Ogran di Sir Fynwy; atas dasar itu diduga unsur ogr- berarti "llym" (tajam) bila bentuk Ogrfan diterima.
claims.quote: Ceir ffrwd o'r enw Ogran yn Sir Fynwy, ac ar sail hynny awgrymir mai "llym" yw ystyr yr elfen ogr-, os derbynnir y ffurf Ogrfan.

claims.statement: Siôn Dafydd Rhys refers to the giant (cawr) as Gogfran Gawr and says he dwelt near Aberhonddu in Brycheiniog.
claims.statement_id: Siôn Dafydd Rhys menyebut raksasa (cawr) itu Gogfran Gawr dan mengatakan ia tinggal dekat Aberhonddu di Brycheiniog.
claims.quote: cyfeiria Siôn Dafydd Rhys at y cawr dan yr enw Gogfran Gawr a dweud ei fod yn trigo ger Aberhonddu ym Mrycheiniog.

claims.statement: In one Welsh Triad there are three Gwenhwyfars married to Arthur; the third is the daughter of (G)og(y)rfan Gawr ("the Giant").
claims.statement_id: Dalam salah satu Triad Wales ada tiga Gwenhwyfar yang menikah dengan Arthur; yang ketiga adalah putri (G)og(y)rfan Gawr ("Sang Raksasa").
claims.quote: The first is the daughter of Cywryd of Gwent, the second of Gwythyr ap Greidawl (a supernatural figure), and the third of (G)og(y)rfan Gawr ("the Giant").

claims.statement: In a variant of another Welsh Triad (Trioedd Ynys Prydein, no. 54), only the daughter of Gogfran Gawr is mentioned.
claims.statement_id: Dalam varian Triad Wales lain (Trioedd Ynys Prydein no. 54), hanya putri Gogfran Gawr yang disebut.
claims.quote: In a variant of another Welsh Triad (Trioedd Ynys Prydein ... only the daughter of Gogfran Gawr is mentioned.

claims.statement: There was once a popular folk rhyme in Wales about Gwenhwyfar: "Gwenhwyfar, daughter of Ogrfan Gawr, bad when little, worse when great."
claims.statement_id: Dulu ada sajak rakyat populer di Wales tentang Gwenhwyfar: "Gwenhwyfar putri Ogrfan Gawr, nakal waktu kecil, lebih buruk waktu besar."
claims.quote: There was once a popular folk rhyme known in Wales concerning Gwenhwyfar: "Gwenhwyfar ferch Ogrfan Gawr / Drwg yn fechan, gwaeth yn fawr

claims.statement: Welsh adaptations of Geoffrey, such as Brut y Brenhinedd, portray her as a daughter of the giant Og[y]vran by a mother of Roman ancestry.
claims.statement_id: Adaptasi Wales atas karya Geoffrey, seperti Brut y Brenhinedd, menggambarkan Gwenhwyfar sebagai putri raksasa Og[y]vran dari ibu keturunan Romawi.
claims.quote: Welsh adaptations of Geoffrey, such as Brut y Brenhinedd, portray her as a daughter of the giant Og[y]vran from a mother of Roman ancestry.

claims.statement: The 14th-century Welsh poet Dafydd ap Gwilym calls her Ogfran the Giant's daughter in one of his poems.
claims.statement_id: Penyair Wales abad ke-14, Dafydd ap Gwilym, menyebut Gwenhwyfar putri Ogfran sang raksasa dalam salah satu puisinya.
claims.quote: The 14th-century Welsh poet Dafydd ap Gwilym alludes to it in one of his poems, calling her Ogfran the Giant's daughter.

claims.statement: In the land of Brycheiniog near the town of Aber Hodni, Gogfran Gawr lived in Aber Ysgyr in the caer above the river.
claims.statement_id: Di tanah Brycheiniog dekat kota Aber Hodni, Gogfran Gawr tinggal di Aber Ysgyr, di benteng (caer) di atas sungai.
claims.quote: In the land of Brycheiniog near to the town of Aber Hodni: Gogfran Gawr lived in Aber Ysgyr in the caer above the river.

claims.statement: Some brothers of Gwenhwyfar, daughter of Gogyrfan Gawr, were imprisoned by some of the giants at Bron Wrgan.
claims.statement_id: Beberapa saudara laki-laki Gwenhwyfar, putri Gogyrfan Gawr, dikisahkan dipenjara oleh raksasa-raksasa di Bron Wrgan.
claims.quote: there were some brothers to Gwenhwyfar, the daughter of Gogyrfan Gawr, who were imprisoned by some of these giants.

claims.statement: Arthur saved each one of them, killing the giants.
claims.statement_id: Arthur menyelamatkan mereka semua dan membunuh para raksasa itu.
claims.quote: But Arthur saved them each one, killing the giants

claims.statement: This list of giants was compiled by Sion Dafydd Rhys around 1600.
claims.statement_id: Daftar raksasa ini disusun Sion Dafydd Rhys sekitar tahun 1600.
claims.quote: Sion Dafydd Rhys, ca. 1600 Peniarth MS 118 f.829-837

claims.statement: In Welsh mythology the father of Gwenhwyfar (Guinevere) is a giant named Ogyruan/Ogyrvan, or Gogyrfan, mentioned in Middle Welsh texts.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Wales, ayah Gwenhwyfar (Guinevere) adalah raksasa bernama Ogyruan/Ogyrvan atau Gogyrfan yang disebut dalam teks-teks Welsh Tengah.
claims.quote: In Welsh mythology, the father of Gwenhwyfar (Guinevere) is instead a giant named Ogyruan/Ogyrvan, or Gogyrfan, mentioned in Middle Welsh texts.

claims.statement: In Arthurian legend Leodegrance is Guinevere's father; when his daughter marries Arthur, he gives the young king the table as a dowry.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda Arthur, Leodegrance adalah ayah Guinevere; ketika putrinya menikah dengan Arthur, ia memberikan meja itu sebagai mas kawin.
claims.quote: When his daughter, Princess Guinevere, marries Arthur, Leodegrance gives the young king the table in dowry.

claims.statement: Joan the Wad is a mythological character in Cornish folklore; she is the Queen of the Pixies, tiny mythical creatures usually associated with the counties of Cornwall and Devon in England.
claims.statement_id: Joan the Wad adalah tokoh mitologis dalam cerita rakyat Cornwall; ia Ratu para Pixie, makhluk mitos mungil yang biasanya dikaitkan dengan county Cornwall dan Devon di Inggris (England).
claims.quote: Joan the Wad is a mythological character in Cornish folklore. She is the Queen of the Pixies, which are tiny mythical creatures usually associated with the counties of Cornwall and Devon in England.

claims.statement: Wad is an Eastern Cornwall colloquial term for a torch or a bundle of straw.
claims.statement_id: Wad adalah istilah sehari-hari di Cornwall Timur untuk obor atau seikat jerami.
claims.quote: Wad is an Eastern Cornwall colloquial term for torch or bundle of straw.

claims.statement: Joan the Wad has been associated with Jack o' the Lantern, King of the Pixies; both may be considered will-o'-the-wisp type characters who lead travellers astray on lonely moors.
claims.statement_id: Joan the Wad dikaitkan dengan Jack o' the Lantern, Raja para Pixie; keduanya dapat dianggap tokoh sejenis will-o'-the-wisp yang menyesatkan pelancong di padang sunyi (moors).
claims.quote: Joan the Wad has been associated with Jack o' the Lantern, the King of the Pixies. ... The two may also be considered will-o'-the-wisp type characters who lead travellers astray on lonely moors

claims.statement: Joan is also thought to use her Wad (torch) to light the way to safety and good luck.
claims.statement_id: Joan juga dipercaya memakai Wad (obor) miliknya untuk menerangi jalan menuju keselamatan dan keberuntungan.
claims.quote: Joan is also thought to use her Wad (Torch) to light the way to safety and good luck

claims.statement: Joan the Wad is often depicted naked and associated with fire and water elements.
claims.statement_id: Joan the Wad sering digambarkan telanjang dan dikaitkan dengan unsur api dan air.
claims.quote: Joan the Wad is often depicted naked and associated with fire and water elements.

claims.statement: In the last century there was a thriving cottage industry in Joan the Wad lucky charms; people carried small figures of her for good luck.
claims.statement_id: Pada abad lalu terdapat industri rumahan yang ramai membuat jimat keberuntungan Joan the Wad; orang membawa figur kecilnya untuk keberuntungan.
claims.quote: In the last century, there was a thriving cottage industry in Joan the Wad lucky charms. ... People carried small figures of Joan the Wad for good luck

claims.statement: A small collection of such antique figures is housed at the Museum of Witchcraft in Boscastle; her image also appears on door knockers as a protective spirit.
claims.statement_id: Sekumpulan kecil figur antik semacam itu disimpan di Museum of Witchcraft di Boscastle; gambarnya juga muncul pada pengetuk pintu sebagai roh pelindung.
claims.quote: a small collection of such antique figures is housed at the Museum of Witchcraft in Boscastle. ... Her image also appears on door knockers to serve as a protective spirit.

claims.statement: A brass good luck charm shows Joan the Wad, Queen of the Cornish Piskies, seated with one arm curved over her head, inscribed "Joan the Wad" and with a hanging ring.
claims.statement_id: Jimat keberuntungan dari kuningan menggambarkan Joan the Wad, Ratu para Piskie Cornwall, duduk dengan satu lengan melengkung di atas kepala, bertuliskan "Joan the Wad" dan bercincin gantungan.
claims.quote: Brass good luck charm - Joan the Wad, Queen of the Cornish Piskies. Joan is seated with one arm curved over her head, with an inscription "Joan the Wad" and a ring for hanging above her.

claims.statement: 'Wad' means 'torch', perhaps linking Joan the Wad to Jack O'Lantern as another spirit who leads travellers astray with a mysterious light.
claims.statement_id: 'Wad' berarti 'obor', yang mungkin menghubungkan Joan the Wad dengan Jack O'Lantern sebagai roh lain yang menyesatkan pelancong dengan cahaya misterius.
claims.quote: 'Wad' means 'torch', perhaps linking Joan the Wad to Jack O'Lantern as another spirit who leads travellers astray with a mysterious light.

claims.statement: However, it could also indicate a connection with Hecate, Goddess of the Witches, one of whose symbols is a flaming torch.
claims.statement_id: Namun, nama itu juga bisa menunjukkan hubungan dengan Hecate, Dewi para Penyihir, yang salah satu lambangnya obor menyala.
claims.quote: However, it could also indicate a connection between her and Hecate, Goddess of the Witches, one of whose symbols is a flaming torch.

claims.statement: These Joan the Wad charms seem to have been devised by F.T. Nettleinghame, who registered them in 1932.
claims.statement_id: Jimat Joan the Wad ini tampaknya dirancang oleh F.T. Nettleinghame, yang mendaftarkannya pada tahun 1932.
claims.quote: These Joan the Wad charms seem to have been devised by F.T. Nettleinghame, who registered them in 1932.

claims.statement: Joan the Wad is the name of an elf or pisky.
claims.statement_id: Joan the Wad adalah nama seorang elf atau pisky.
claims.quote: Joan the Wad, the name of an elf or pisky.

claims.statement: In Celtic mythology a Joint-eater, Just-halver or Alp-luachra (Ireland) is a type of fairy that sits invisibly and consumes half of its victim's food.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Kelt, Joint-eater, Just-halver, atau Alp-luachra (Irlandia/Ireland) adalah sejenis peri yang duduk tanpa terlihat dan memakan separuh makanan korbannya.
claims.quote: In Celtic mythology, a Joint-eater, Just-halver or Alp-luachra (Ireland) is a type of fairy who sits invisibly and consumes half of their victim's food.

claims.statement: When a person falls asleep beside a spring or stream, the Alp-luachra appears as a newt and crawls down the person's mouth, feeding off the food they have eaten.
claims.statement_id: Ketika seseorang tertidur di tepi mata air atau sungai kecil, Alp-luachra muncul dalam wujud kadal air (newt) dan merayap masuk lewat mulutnya, lalu memakan makanan yang telah dimakan orang itu.
claims.quote: When a person falls asleep by the side of a spring or stream, the Alp-luachra appears in the form of a newt and crawls down the person's mouth, feeding off the food that they had eaten.

claims.statement: A man haunted by a joint-eater never grows fat, because the fairy consumes the pith or quintessence of his food; people who consume newts are thought to be plagued this way.
claims.statement_id: Orang yang dihantui joint-eater tidak akan pernah gemuk karena sari makanan (pith or quintessence) dihabiskan peri itu; orang yang menelan kadal air (newt) dipercaya terkena gangguan ini.
claims.quote: A man haunted by a joint-eater will never grow fat, because the pith or quintessence of the food is consumed by the fairy. ... People who consume newts are thought to be plagued in this way.

claims.statement: To rid oneself of an Alp-luachra one should eat a large quantity of salt beef without drinking, then lie by a running stream with the mouth wide open.
claims.statement_id: Untuk menyingkirkan Alp-luachra, orang harus makan banyak daging sapi asin tanpa minum, lalu berbaring di tepi aliran air dengan mulut terbuka lebar.
claims.quote: to rid one's self of an Alp-Luachra, one should eat a large quantity of salt beef, without drinking anything, and then lie by a running stream with their mouth wide open

claims.statement: After a long wait the Alp-luachra becomes thirsty and jumps into the stream to drink.
claims.statement_id: Setelah lama menunggu, Alp-luachra akan kehausan dan melompat ke sungai untuk minum.
claims.quote: after a long wait, the Alp-Luachra will become thirsty, and will jump into the stream to drink.

claims.statement: In Scottish folklore the lavellan (làbh-allan, la-mhalan, la-bhallan) is a rodent- or lizard-like creature with a venomous bite.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skotlandia, lavellan (làbh-allan, la-mhalan, la-bhallan) adalah makhluk mirip hewan pengerat atau kadal dengan gigitan berbisa.
claims.quote: In Scottish folklore, the lavellan, làbh-allan, la-mhalan, or la-bhallan is a rodent- or lizard-like creature with a venomous bite.

claims.statement: It reportedly lives in bodies of water and features in tales from both Sutherland and Caithness.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini dikabarkan hidup di perairan dan muncul dalam kisah-kisah dari Sutherland maupun Caithness.
claims.quote: It reportedly lives in bodies of water. ... It features in tales from both Sutherland and Caithness.

claims.statement: Robert Sibbald's Scotia Illustrata described the lavellan as an animal common in Caithness that stays in water, with a head and colouring like a weasel, whose breath does harm.
claims.statement_id: Robert Sibbald dalam Scotia Illustrata menggambarkan lavellan sebagai hewan yang umum di Caithness, tinggal di air, berkepala dan berwarna seperti musang (weasel), dan napasnya mencelakakan.
claims.quote: The lavellan was described in Robert Sibbald's Scotia Illustrata as "an animal common in Caithness, it stays in water, it has a head similar to the weasel, and is a beast of the same colouring. The breath from these beasts does harm."

claims.statement: At the settlement of Ausdale Thomas Pennant asked local people about the lavellan; they believed it was particularly harmful to cattle.
claims.statement_id: Di permukiman Ausdale, Thomas Pennant menanyai penduduk tentang lavellan; mereka percaya lavellan sangat berbahaya bagi ternak sapi (cattle).
claims.quote: In the settlement of Ausdale, Thomas Pennant asked the local people about the lavellan. They reportedly believed that the lavellan was particularly harmful to cattle

claims.statement: Pennant posited that the lavellan was actually a water shrew (Neomys fodiens); according to researcher Lee Raye, this view is now generally accepted.

claims.quote: Pennant posited that the mythical lavellan was, in actuality, a water shrew (Neomys fodiens). According to researcher Lee Raye, Pennant's view is now generally accepted as accurate.

claims.statement: Lazy Laurence is a pixie and nature spirit in English folklore who inhabits the New Forest area of Hampshire and Dorset.
claims.statement_id: Lazy Laurence adalah pixie dan roh alam dalam cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore) yang mendiami kawasan New Forest di Hampshire dan Dorset.
claims.quote: Lazy Laurence is a pixie and nature spirit in English folklore who inhabits the New Forest area of Hampshire and Dorset.

claims.statement: He is traditionally associated with protecting orchards and cider, and is known to send people to sleep beneath fruit trees, make them lazy or dithering, or give them stomach cramps.
claims.statement_id: Secara tradisional ia dikaitkan dengan perlindungan kebun buah dan sari apel (cider), dan dikenal membuat orang tertidur di bawah pohon buah, menjadi malas, ragu-ragu, atau kram perut.
claims.quote: He is traditionally associated with the protection of orchards and of cider, and known to send people to sleep beneath fruit trees, make them lazy, make them dither, or to give them stomach cramps.

claims.statement: Lazy Laurence is most associated with the New Forest, where he gives apple scrumpers and rude tourists indigestion and sends people into a dreaming, dithery state.
claims.statement_id: Lazy Laurence paling erat dikaitkan dengan New Forest, tempat ia membuat pencuri apel dan wisatawan kurang ajar sakit perut serta membuat orang melamun dan ragu-ragu.
claims.quote: Lazy Laurence is most prominently associated with the New Forest, where he regularly gives apple scrumpers and rude tourists indigestion, and sends people into a dreaming, dithery state.

claims.statement: Laurence was once also known in the neighbouring counties of Sussex and Somerset, where he was used as a bogeyman to scare children.
claims.statement_id: Laurence dulu juga dikenal di county tetangga Sussex dan Somerset, tempat ia dijadikan momok untuk menakut-nakuti anak-anak.
claims.quote: Laurence was once also known of in the neighbouring counties of Sussex and Somerset, where he was used as a bogeyman to scare children

claims.statement: He was also known in the dialects of Devon and Cornwall, where his laziness was emphasised.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga dikenal dalam dialek Devon dan Cornwall, yang menekankan kemalasannya.
claims.quote: as well as in the dialects of Devon and Cornwall, where his laziness was emphasised.

claims.statement: An early literary reference to the figure is a small pamphlet from the 1770s titled "The Pleasant history of lazy Laurence".
claims.statement_id: Rujukan sastra awal tentang tokoh ini terdapat dalam pamflet kecil dari tahun 1770-an berjudul "The Pleasant history of lazy Laurence".
claims.quote: An early literary reference to the figure is in a small pamphlet from the 1770s titled "The Pleasant history of lazy Laurence"

claims.statement: Brewer's Dictionary of Phrase and Fable notes the suggestion that the name alludes to the heat prevalent around the feast of St Lawrence (10 August).
claims.statement_id: Brewer's Dictionary of Phrase and Fable mencatat dugaan bahwa namanya menyinggung panas yang lazim di sekitar hari raya St Lawrence (10 Agustus).
claims.quote: it has been suggested that there is an allusion to the heat prevalent around the time of the feast of St Lawrence (10 August).

claims.statement: Another conjecture is a joke that when the martyr St Lawrence told his torturers to turn him on his gridiron, he was too lazy to move himself.
claims.statement_id: Dugaan lain berasal dari lelucon bahwa ketika martir St Lawrence meminta penyiksanya membaliknya di atas panggangan, itu karena ia terlalu malas bergerak sendiri.
claims.quote: Another conjecture is that there was a joke to the effect that when the martyr St Lawrence told his torturers to turn him round on his gridiron, it was because he was too lazy to move by himself.

claims.statement: The earthwork where Lazy Laurence is believed to live, Laurence's Barrow, is a small bell barrow on Beaulieu Heath near two other barrows (Watt's Parlour and Cold Pixies' Cave).
claims.statement_id: Gundukan tanah yang dipercaya menjadi kediaman Lazy Laurence, Laurence's Barrow, adalah bell barrow kecil di Beaulieu Heath, dekat dua barrow lain (Watt's Parlour dan Cold Pixies' Cave).
claims.quote: The earthwork where Lazy Laurence is traditionally believed to reside, Laurence's Barrow, is a small bell barrow situated on Beaulieu Heath, near to two other barrows (Watt's Parlour and Cold Pixies' Cave)

claims.statement: Wise writes that fairies still dwell in the Forest; the mischievous sprite Laurence still holds men by his spell and makes them idle.
claims.statement_id: Wise menulis bahwa di Forest masih tinggal para peri; makhluk jahil Laurence masih memikat orang dengan mantranya dan membuat mereka malas.
claims.quote: Here in the Forest still dwell fairies. The mischievous sprite, Laurence, still holds men by his spell and makes them idle.

claims.statement: The Ly Erg is a fairy from Scottish folklore, particularly associated with the area in and around Glenmore Forest, part of the present-day Cairngorms National Park.
claims.statement_id: Ly Erg adalah peri dari cerita rakyat Skotlandia (Scottish folklore), terutama dikaitkan dengan kawasan di dalam dan sekitar Glenmore Forest, bagian dari Cairngorms National Park saat ini.
claims.quote: The Ly Erg is a fairy from Scottish folklore, particularly associated with the area in and around the Glenmore Forest, part of the present-day Cairngorms National Park.

claims.statement: It is dressed as a soldier, distinguishable from a real one only by its red right hand, said to be stained with its victims' blood.
claims.statement_id: Ia berpakaian seperti prajurit dan hanya dapat dibedakan dari prajurit sungguhan oleh tangan kanannya yang merah, yang konon ternoda darah korban-korbannya.
claims.quote: It is dressed as a soldier, distinguishable from a real soldier only by its red right hand, said to be stained with the blood of its victims.

claims.statement: While walking it stops near water and, raising its right hand, challenges passersby to fight.
claims.statement_id: Saat berjalan, ia berhenti di dekat air dan, dengan mengangkat tangan kanannya, menantang orang yang lewat untuk bertarung.
claims.quote: While out walking it will stop near water, and by raising its right hand challenge passersby to fight.

claims.statement: Anyone who fights the Ly Erg will be dead within a fortnight, win or lose.
claims.statement_id: Siapa pun yang bertarung dengan Ly Erg akan mati dalam dua minggu (a fortnight), menang ataupun kalah.
claims.quote: But anyone who engages in combat with the Ly Erg will be dead within a fortnight, win or lose.

claims.statement: Writing in 1847, the antiquarian Joseph Robertson told of three brothers who fought the Ly Erg, each dying immediately after the encounter.
claims.statement_id: Pada tahun 1847, antikuarian Joseph Robertson menulis tentang tiga bersaudara yang bertarung dengan Ly Erg dan masing-masing mati segera setelah pertemuan itu.
claims.quote: Writing in 1847, the antiquarian Joseph Robertson tells of three brothers who fought the Ly Erg, each of them dying immediately after their encounter.

claims.statement: The archive holds a story of the Ly Erg and three brothers: the Ly Erg, dressed as a soldier with one red hand, challenged three brothers to a fight, after which they all died.
claims.statement_id: Arsip memuat kisah Ly Erg dan tiga bersaudara: Ly Erg, berpakaian prajurit dan bertangan merah sebelah, menantang tiga bersaudara bertarung, dan segera setelah itu mereka semua mati.
claims.quote: Story about the Ly Erg and three brothers in which Ly Erg, dressed as a soldier and with one red hand, challenged three brothers to a fight immediately after which they all died.

claims.statement: The story of the Ly Erg and three brothers was recorded in July 1909 in the Carmichael-Watson Collection, University of Edinburgh Library Heritage Collections.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Ly Erg dan tiga bersaudara tercatat pada Juli 1909 (July 1909) dalam Carmichael-Watson Collection di University of Edinburgh Library Heritage Collections.
claims.quote: Story about the Ly Erg and three brothers, July 1909, Coll-97/CW117/16. The Carmichael-Watson Collection, Coll-97. University of Edinburgh Library Heritage Collections.

claims.statement: Madam Pigott or Madam Piggott is a ghost said to haunt Chetwynd Park and the nearby market town of Newport, Shropshire; she resembles other White Ladies in British folklore.
claims.statement_id: Madam Pigott atau Madam Piggott adalah hantu yang konon menghantui kawasan Chetwynd Park dan kota pasar Newport, Shropshire, di sekitarnya; ia mirip dengan White Lady lain dalam cerita rakyat Britania.
claims.quote: Madam Pigott or Madam Piggott is a ghost supposed to haunt the area of Chetwynd Park and the surrounding market town of Newport, Shropshire. She bears similarities to other White Ladies in British folklore.

claims.statement: If a rider passed, Madam Pigott would leap onto the horse behind him; her spirit could not cross water, so she let go when the rider crossed a stream.
claims.statement_id: Bila seorang penunggang kuda melintas, Madam Pigott melompat ke punggung kuda di belakangnya; arwahnya tidak dapat menyeberangi air, sehingga ia melepaskan diri saat penunggang menyeberangi sungai kecil.
claims.quote: If a rider passed through the area, Madam Pigott would leap onto the horse behind him. Her spirit was unable to cross water, so when the rider crossed a stream, she would let go.

claims.statement: Sightings of "Madame Piggott" have been recorded as recently as 2014.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan "Madame Piggott" tercatat hingga tahun 2014.
claims.quote: "Madame Piggott" sightings have been recorded as recently as 2014.

claims.statement: She has been said to appear around the A41 road between Newport and Market Drayton.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikatakan muncul di sekitar jalan A41 antara Newport dan Market Drayton.
claims.quote: She has been said to appear around the A41 road between Newport and Market Drayton.

claims.statement: The Silky of Black Heddon is a similar White Lady, with a favourite tree known as the Silky's Chair.
claims.statement_id: Silky dari Black Heddon adalah White Lady yang serupa; ia punya pohon kesukaan yang dikenal sebagai Silky's Chair.
claims.quote: The Silky of Black Heddon is a similar White Lady. She had a preferred tree known as the Silky's Chair.

claims.statement: Burne calls Madam Pigott a far more appalling 'Madam', the ancient terror of Chetwynd and Edgmond.
claims.statement_id: Burne menyebut Madam Pigott sebagai sosok 'Madam' yang jauh lebih mengerikan, teror lama bagi Chetwynd dan Edgmond.
claims.quote: A far more appalling ‘Madam’ is Madam Pigott, the ancient terror of Chetwynd and Edgmond.

claims.statement: Her husband said 'one should lop the root to save the branch'; neither mother nor child survived, and because he had so cruelly willed her death, Madam Pigott's spirit could find no rest.
claims.statement_id: Suaminya berkata 'one should lop the root to save the branch'; ibu dan anak sama-sama tidak selamat, dan karena suaminya begitu kejam menghendaki kematiannya, arwah Madam Pigott tidak dapat beristirahat.
claims.quote: ‘one should lop the root to save the branch.’ Neither mother nor child survived, but after her husband had thus cruelly willed her death, Madam Pigott’s spirit could find no rest.

claims.statement: Night after night, exactly at twelve o'clock, she came out of a trap-door in the roof of Chetwynd (old) Rectory.
claims.statement_id: Malam demi malam, tepat pukul dua belas, ia keluar dari pintu kolong di atap Chetwynd (old) Rectory.
claims.quote: Night after night, exactly at twelve o'clock, she issued from a trap-door in the roof of Chetwynd (old) Rectory

claims.statement: Her favourite haunt was the steep, dark, high-banked lane properly called Cheney Hill.
claims.statement_id: Tempat kesukaannya adalah jalan sempit yang curam, gelap, dan bertebing tinggi bernama Cheney Hill.
claims.quote: Her favourite haunt was the steep, dark, high-banked lane, properly called Cheney Hill

claims.statement: On a tree-root called Madam Pigott's Armchair, or on the old stone wall of Chetwynd Park above it, Madam Pigott used to sit on a moonlit night combing her baby's hair.
claims.statement_id: Di akar pohon yang disebut Madam Pigott's Armchair, atau di tembok batu tua Chetwynd Park di atasnya, Madam Pigott biasa duduk pada malam terang bulan sambil menyisir rambut bayinya.
claims.quote: tree-root, called Madam Pigott’s Armchair. On this, or else on the old stone wall of Chetwynd Park just above it, Madam Pigott used to sit, ‘on a moonshiny night,’ combing her baby’s hair

claims.statement: She and her black cat would spring up behind the rider and cling fast until they came to running water, beyond which she could go no farther.
claims.statement_id: Ia dan kucing hitamnya melompat ke belakang penunggang dan berpegangan erat, sampai tiba di air mengalir (running water), lalu ia tidak bisa lebih jauh.
claims.quote: she and her black cat would spring up behind him and cling fast, notwithstanding all his efforts, till she came to a ‘ running water,’ then she could go no farther.

claims.statement: Twelve local clergy were summoned to lay her by incessantly reading Psalms until they made her obedient to their power.
claims.statement_id: Dua belas rohaniwan setempat dipanggil untuk menenangkan (lay) arwahnya dengan terus-menerus membaca Mazmur (Psalms) sampai ia tunduk pada kuasa mereka.
claims.quote: were summoned to lay her, by incessantly reading Psalms till they made her obedient to their power.

claims.statement: One clergyman succeeded because he continued to 'read' after all the others were exhausted.
claims.statement_id: Satu rohaniwan berhasil karena terus 'membaca' setelah semua yang lain kelelahan.
claims.quote: for he continued to ‘read ’ after all the others were exhausted.

claims.statement: This wild and gruesome myth is familiar to poor folk for miles around Chetwynd.
claims.statement_id: Mitos yang liar dan mengerikan ini dikenal rakyat kecil hingga bermil-mil di sekitar Chetwynd.
claims.quote: This wild and gruesome myth is familiar to the poor folk for miles around Chetwynd.

claims.statement: The version told by Dimiti and recorded by Groome: at Chetwynd End near Newport a young lady, Miss Pigott, was out hunting when her horse ran up a big sandy bank, threw her off and killed her.
claims.statement_id: Versi yang dituturkan Dimiti dan dicatat Groome: di Chetwynd End dekat Newport, seorang wanita muda, Miss Pigott, sedang berburu ketika kudanya berlari menaiki tebing pasir besar, melemparkannya, dan menewaskannya.
claims.quote: It was at Chetwynd End, near Newport, just by the parson's house ; and there was a young lady. Miss Pigott, out hunting; and the horse run up a great big sandy bank, and threw her off his back, and killed her.

claims.statement: She was laid and thrown into Chetwynd Pool, but the bottle holding her broke (someone skating, it was thought), and she returned as bad as before, jumping onto men's horses.
claims.statement_id: Arwahnya ditenangkan dan dilemparkan ke Chetwynd Pool, tetapi botol tempatnya dikurung pecah (kemungkinan karena orang berseluncur), sehingga ia kembali mengganggu dan melompat ke kuda-kuda orang.
claims.quote: then they laid her, threw her into Chetwynd Pool. And somehow the bottle they'd put her in got broken (somebody skating, I think it was); and she come as bad again after that, and got jumping on the men's horses.

claims.statement: Groome notes that Dimiti then began a legend which, in his view, certainly has no claim to Gipsy origin, though it recalls the Fisherman in the Arabian Nights.
claims.statement_id: Groome mencatat bahwa Dimiti mulai menuturkan sebuah legenda yang menurutnya jelas tidak berasal dari kaum Gipsy, meski mengingatkan pada kisah Nelayan dalam Arabian Nights.
claims.quote: the priest in it started Dimiti off on a legend, that certainly has no claim to Gipsy origin, though it reminds one of the Fisherman in the Arabian Nights

claims.statement: The Metheringham Lass is the name given to an apparition reported at RAF Metheringham.
claims.statement_id: Metheringham Lass adalah nama penampakan (apparition) yang dilaporkan di RAF Metheringham.
claims.quote: The Metheringham Lass is the name given to an apparition which has been reported at RAF Metheringham.

claims.statement: Reports state that the woman, wearing a jacket bearing RAF insignia, approaches cars as they pass the old airfield, sometimes even physically interacting with the car.
claims.statement_id: Menurut laporan, perempuan itu memakai jaket berlambang RAF dan mendekati mobil yang melintasi bekas lapangan terbang, kadang bahkan menyentuh mobil secara fisik.
claims.quote: Reports have stated that the woman, wearing a jacket bearing RAF insignia, approaches cars as they pass the old airfield, sometimes even physically interacting with the car.

claims.statement: She begs the driver to help her boyfriend, injured in a motorcycle accident, but vanishes when the driver exits the car to help.
claims.statement_id: Ia memohon pengemudi menolong pacarnya yang terluka dalam kecelakaan sepeda motor, tetapi ia lenyap ketika pengemudi keluar dari mobil.
claims.quote: She begs the driver to help her boyfriend who has been injured in a motorcycle accident. However, when the driver exits the car to help, she vanishes.

claims.statement: The apparition is said to be accompanied first by the smell of lavender, followed by the smell of decomposing flesh.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan itu konon disertai mula-mula bau lavender, lalu bau daging membusuk.
claims.quote: The apparition is said to be accompanied first by the smell of lavender, followed by the smell of decomposing flesh.

claims.statement: It has been speculated that the apparition is Catherine Bystock, who died aged nineteen when her flight sergeant boyfriend crashed the motorcycle carrying them both after a dance.
claims.statement_id: Ada dugaan bahwa penampakan itu adalah Catherine Bystock, yang meninggal pada usia sembilan belas tahun ketika pacarnya, seorang flight sergeant, menabrakkan sepeda motor yang mereka tumpangi berdua sepulang dari pesta dansa.
claims.quote: It has been speculated that the reported apparition is of Catherine Bystock, who died at the age of nineteen when her flight sergeant boyfriend crashed his motorcycle after a dance with them both on board.

claims.statement: This is a variant of the 'phantom hitchhiker' legend, common in twentieth-century and contemporary ghost folklore.
claims.statement_id: Kisah ini adalah varian legenda 'phantom hitchhiker' (penumpang hantu), yang umum dalam cerita rakyat hantu abad ke-20 dan masa kini.
claims.quote: This is a variant of the ‘phantom hitchhiker’ legend, common in twentieth-century and contemporary folklore concerning ghosts.

claims.statement: The ghost of a young woman is said to flag down motorists at night on a road beside the former RAF Metheringham, saying her boyfriend has fallen off his motorbike.
claims.statement_id: Hantu seorang perempuan muda konon menghentikan pengendara pada malam hari di jalan di samping bekas RAF Metheringham, sambil berkata pacarnya jatuh dari sepeda motor.
claims.quote: The ghost of a young woman is said to flag down unsuspecting motorists at night, on a road adjacent to the former RAF Metheringham, saying her boyfriend has fallen off his motorbike.

claims.statement: In some versions or alleged sightings she wears a green mac and a grey headscarf, and the last thing people see before she vanishes is her skull facing them from beneath her scarf.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian versi atau kesaksian, ia memakai jas hujan hijau dan kerudung abu-abu, dan yang terakhir terlihat sebelum ia lenyap adalah tengkoraknya yang menghadap orang dari balik kerudung.
claims.quote: In some versions, or alleged sightings, she is wearing a green mac and a grey headscarf, and the last people see of her before she vanishes is her skull facing them from beneath her scarf.

claims.statement: Bruce Barrymore Halpenny's rendition in his book Ghost Stations (1986) is the main source of the tale.
claims.statement_id: Versi Bruce Barrymore Halpenny dalam bukunya Ghost Stations (1986) adalah sumber utama kisah ini.
claims.quote: Bruce Barrymore Halpenny, whose rendition of this story in his book Ghost Stations (1986) is the main source of the tale.

claims.statement: Halpenny claims that nineteen-year-old Catherine Bystock was killed here in 1945 when her Flight Sergeant boyfriend, stationed at RAF Metheringham, lost control of his motorcycle.
claims.statement_id: Halpenny mengklaim bahwa perempuan sembilan belas tahun bernama Catherine Bystock tewas di sini pada 1945, ketika pacarnya, seorang Flight Sergeant yang bertugas di RAF Metheringham, kehilangan kendali atas sepeda motornya.
claims.quote: He claims that a nineteen-year-old woman called Catherine Bystock was killed here in 1945, when her Flight Sergeant boyfriend, stationed at RAF Metheringham, lost control of his motorcycle.

claims.statement: There is, however, no evidence to support this sad backstory.
claims.statement_id: Namun, tidak ada bukti yang mendukung latar kisah sedih itu.
claims.quote: There is no evidence to support this sad backstory, though.

claims.statement: In 2022 a group called Retford Ghost Hunters claimed to have photographed her, and national and international media picked this up.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2022, kelompok Retford Ghost Hunters mengaku telah memotretnya, dan klaim itu diberitakan media nasional dan internasional.
claims.quote: In 2022, a group called Retford Ghost Hunters claimed to have taken a photograph of her, and this was picked up by national and international media.

claims.statement: Rory Waterman includes a modernised adaptation in Come Here to This Gate (Carcanet, 2024), where the apparition is a young man's delusion.
claims.statement_id: Rory Waterman memuat adaptasi modern kisah ini dalam Come Here to This Gate (Carcanet, 2024), dengan penampakan itu sebagai delusi seorang pemuda.
claims.quote: Rory Waterman includes a modernised adaptation of the story in Come Here to This Gate (Carcanet, 2024), in which the apparition is a young man’s delusion.

claims.statement: The tale now has its own episode of the BBC's 'Secret Lincolnshire' (2024).
claims.statement_id: Kisah ini kini punya episode sendiri dalam 'Secret Lincolnshire' (2024) dari BBC.
claims.quote: This tale now has its own episode of the BBC’s ‘Secret Lincolnshire’ (2024), narrated by Rory.

claims.statement: A lonely lane now crosses the site of the base (operational 1942-5), atop its only partly remaining runway.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah jalan sepi kini melintasi bekas pangkalan itu (beroperasi 1942-5), di atas landasan pacu yang hanya tersisa sebagian.
claims.quote: A lonely lane now crosses the site of the base (operational 1942-5), atop its only partly-remaining runway.

claims.statement: There are several broadly similar anecdotes of ghost sightings in this part of Lincolnshire.
claims.statement_id: Ada beberapa anekdot penampakan hantu yang mirip di bagian Lincolnshire ini.
claims.quote: There are several broadly similar anecdotes of ghost sightings in this part of Lincolnshire.

claims.statement: The figure allegedly appearing is a young woman named Catherine Bystock, a member of the Women's Auxiliary Air Force engaged to a Flight Sergeant.
claims.statement_id: Konon yang muncul adalah sosok perempuan muda bernama Catherine Bystock, anggota Women's Auxiliary Air Force yang bertunangan dengan seorang Flight Sergeant.
claims.quote: The figure of a young woman named Catherine Bystock, a member of the Women's Auxiliary Air Force who had been engaged to a Flight Sergeant, allegedly appears.

claims.statement: The ghost appears in the summer months at around 9:30 pm, the time she was supposedly killed, and always after dusk starts to fall.
claims.statement_id: Hantu itu muncul pada bulan-bulan musim panas sekitar pukul 9.30 malam, waktu ia konon tewas, dan selalu setelah senja mulai turun.
claims.quote: The ghost appears in the summer months at around 9:30 pm – the time she was supposedly killed and always after dusk starts to fall.

claims.statement: She then disappears, leaving behind the smells of rotting meat and, in some accounts, lavender.
claims.statement_id: Ia lalu menghilang, meninggalkan bau daging busuk dan, menurut sebagian kisah, lavender.
claims.quote: She then disappears, leaving behind the smells of rotting meat and, in some accounts, lavender.

claims.statement: She is said to have haunted the spot for more than 60 years.
claims.statement_id: Ia konon telah menghantui tempat itu lebih dari 60 tahun.
claims.quote: She is said to have haunted the spot for more than 60 years.

claims.statement: In Irish folklore, Muckie is the name given to an alleged mysterious creature said to inhabit the Lakes of Killarney in Ireland.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Irlandia, Muckie adalah nama makhluk misterius yang konon menghuni Danau-danau Killarney (Lakes of Killarney) di Irlandia.
claims.quote: In Irish folklore, Muckie is the name given to an alleged mysterious creature said to inhabit the Lakes of Killarney in Ireland.

claims.statement: In 2003, scientists conducted a series of sonar scans to determine local fish populations.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2003, para ilmuwan melakukan serangkaian pemindaian sonar untuk mengetahui populasi ikan setempat.
claims.quote: In 2003, scientists conducted a series of sonar scans to determine local fish populations.

claims.statement: A large solid object in the water was recorded, which led to the theory that the lake is inhabited by some form of lake monster, similar to the famed "Nessie" of Loch Ness.
claims.statement_id: Pemindaian itu merekam benda padat besar di air, sehingga muncul teori bahwa danau itu dihuni semacam monster danau, mirip "Nessie" dari Loch Ness.
claims.quote: However, a large solid object in the water was recorded, which has led to the theory that the lake is inhabited by some form of lake monster, similar to the famed "Nessie" of Loch Ness.
