claims.statement_id: Kisah worm ini mungkin terilhami kapal panjang Viking yang mengukir kepala worm (Ormr) di haluannya.
claims.quote: The tale of the worm may be inspired by the longships of marauding Vikings, who carved the heads of Worms (Ormr) on the bow

claims.statement: However, this does not account for the commonness of dragons in Germanic folklore including Northumbria (see the Laidly and Lambton Worms and the Worm of Linton).
claims.statement_id: Namun dugaan itu tidak memperhitungkan banyaknya naga dalam cerita rakyat Jermanik, termasuk Northumbria (seperti Laidly Worm, Lambton Worm, dan Worm of Linton).
claims.quote: however, this does not take into account the commonness of dragons in Germanic folklore including that of Northumbria (see the Laidly and Lambton Worms as well as the Worm of Linton).

claims.statement: The tradition lapsed from 1771, the sword was given to Durham Cathedral in 1947, and the ceremony was revived by Bishop David Jenkins in 1984.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi itu terhenti sejak 1771, pedangnya diserahkan ke Katedral Durham pada 1947, dan upacaranya dihidupkan kembali oleh Uskup David Jenkins pada 1984.
claims.quote: The tradition lapsed from 1771 and the sword was given to Durham Cathedral in 1947. The ceremony was revived by bishop David Jenkins in 1984

claims.statement: The Sockburn Worm, with the falchion embedded in it, appears on the district badge of the Darlington & District Scout Association.
claims.statement_id: Sockburn Worm dengan falchion tertancap padanya muncul di lencana distrik Darlington & District Scout Association.
claims.quote: The Sockburn Worm, with the falchion embedded in it, appears on the district badge of the local Darlington & District Scout Association.

claims.statement: According to legend, in 1063 the head of the family, Sir John Conyers, killed a fearsome dragon terrorising the area, known as the Sockburn Worm.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, pada 1063 kepala keluarga, Sir John Conyers, membunuh naga menakutkan yang meneror wilayah itu, yang dikenal sebagai Sockburn Worm.
claims.quote: According to legend, this was because in 1063 the head of the family, Sir John Conyers, had killed a fearsome dragon which had been terrorising the area, known as the Sockburn Worm.

claims.statement: The ceremonial speech: this falchion is the one with which the champion Conyers slew the worm, dragon or fiery flying serpent that destroyed man, woman and child; in memory of which the king gave him the manor of Sockburn.
claims.statement_id: Pidato upacara: falchion ini dipakai sang juara Conyers membunuh worm, naga, atau ular terbang berapi yang membinasakan laki-laki, perempuan, dan anak-anak; untuk mengenangnya raja memberinya manor Sockburn.
claims.quote: My Lord Bishop. I hereby present you with the falchion wherewith the champion Conyers slew the worm, dragon or fiery flying serpent which destroyed man, woman and child; in memory of which the king then reigning gave him the manor of Sockburn

claims.statement: The custom fell out of use in 1771, the sword was given to the Cathedral in 1947, and the ceremony was revived in 1984, with the Mayor of Darlington now presenting the sword to the Bishop.
claims.statement_id: Kebiasaan itu terhenti pada 1771, pedangnya diserahkan ke katedral pada 1947, dan upacara dihidupkan kembali pada 1984 dengan Wali Kota (Mayor) Darlington sebagai penyerah pedang kepada Uskup.
claims.quote: The custom fell out of use in 1771, and the sword was given to the Cathedral in 1947. The tenure ceremony was revived in 1984, the sword now being presented to the Bishop by the Mayor of Darlington

claims.statement: The Sockburn Worm story was almost certainly the inspiration for Lewis Carroll's nonsense poem Jabberwocky; Carroll lived in Croft-on-Tees as a boy.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Sockburn Worm hampir pasti mengilhami puisi nonsens Jabberwocky karya Lewis Carroll, yang semasa kecil tinggal di Croft-on-Tees.
claims.quote: The story of the Sockburn Worm was almost certainly the inspiration for Lewis Carroll’s famous nonsense poem ‘Jabberwocky’. Carroll lived in nearby Croft-on-Tees as a boy

claims.statement: In the poem the hero wields a vorpal blade to kill the monster, a weapon probably based on the falchion.
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi itu sang pahlawan memakai 'vorpal blade' untuk membunuh monster, senjata yang mungkin terilhami falchion.
claims.quote: In the poem, the hero wields a ‘vorpal blade’ to kill the monster, a weapon probably based on the falchion.

claims.statement: The story tells of a young knight, Sir John Conyers, who fought to save his lands from a great dragon that had haunted the region for seven years.
claims.statement_id: Kisahnya tentang ksatria muda Sir John Conyers yang bertarung menyelamatkan tanahnya dari naga besar yang telah menghantui wilayah itu selama tujuh tahun.
claims.quote: telling the story of a young knight named Sir. John Conyers, who fought to save his lands from a great dragon who had haunted the region for seven years.

claims.statement: After praying at a nearby chapel, Sir John slew the foul-breathed serpent with his falchion, left its body in the River Tees, and buried what remained under the Grey Stone still visible today.
claims.statement_id: Setelah berdoa di kapel terdekat, Sir John membunuh ular berbau busuk itu dengan falchion-nya, membiarkan tubuhnya di Sungai Tees, dan mengubur sisanya di bawah Grey Stone yang masih terlihat sekarang.
claims.quote: After offering his prayers at a nearby chapel, Sir John slew the foul-breathed serpent with his trusty falchion, letting its decimated body rest in the River Tees. He buried what was left of the beast under the great ‘Grey Stone’ still visible today

claims.statement: Heraldry book: Sir John Conyers of Storkburn slew the monstrous, venomous (venoms) and poisonous wyvern (wiverns) or worme that overthrew and devoured (Devourd) many people.
claims.statement_id: Buku heraldik: Sir John Conyers dari Sockburn (ditulis Storkburn) membunuh wyvern (wiverns) atau worme yang mengerikan, berbisa (venoms), dan beracun, yang menjatuhkan dan melahap (Devourd) banyak orang.
claims.quote: Sr. Jo. Conyers of Storkburn [sic] Knt who slew [th]e monstrous venoms and poysons wiverns Ask or worme which overthrew and Devourd many people in fight

claims.statement: A book of heraldry dating from the early seventeenth century recalls the legend.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah buku heraldik dari awal abad ke-17 mencatat legenda ini.
claims.quote: A book of heraldry dating from the early seventeenth century recalls the legend

claims.statement: In the North East, tales of dragons (known as worms) seem to have dominated the popular imagination, with at least twenty separate stories recorded in Northumbria, Co. Durham and Yorkshire alone.
claims.statement_id: Di Timur Laut, kisah naga (disebut worms) tampaknya mendominasi imajinasi rakyat, dengan sedikitnya dua puluh kisah tercatat di Northumbria, Co. Durham, dan Yorkshire.
claims.quote: In the North East, tales of dragons (known as ‘worms’) seem to have dominated the popular imagination, with at least twenty separate stories recorded in Northumbria, Co. Durham and Yorkshire alone.

claims.statement: During these tumultuous times of religious and social upheaval, the story of the Sockburn Worm reigned supreme.
claims.statement_id: Pada masa pergolakan agama dan sosial itu, kisah Sockburn Worm paling unggul (reigned supreme).
claims.quote: During these tumultuous times of religious and social upheaval, the story of the Sockburn Worm reigned supreme

claims.statement: Bishop Cosin records the pomp and excitement of the ceremony in 1661.
claims.statement_id: Uskup Cosin mencatat kemeriahan dan kegembiraan upacara itu pada 1661.
claims.quote: Bishop Cosin records the pomp and excitement associated with the ceremony in 1661

claims.statement: Sockburn was a village under siege from the ferocious Sockburn Worm, which terrorised locals, devoured livestock and laid waste to the land.
claims.statement_id: Sockburn adalah desa yang dikepung Sockburn Worm yang ganas, yang meneror penduduk, melahap ternak, dan menghancurkan tanah.
claims.quote: Sockburn was a village under siege from the ferocious Sockburn Worm, who terrorised locals, devoured livestock and lay waste to the land.

claims.statement: A worm is the name given to a wyvern, a winged dragon with an arrow-tipped tail and two legs instead of four.
claims.statement_id: Worm adalah sebutan untuk wyvern, naga bersayap dengan ekor berujung mata panah dan dua kaki, bukan empat.
claims.quote: A worm is the name given to a wyvern, a winged dragon sporting a tail with an arrow-shaped tip and has two legs instead of four.

claims.statement: From that time to the present day, whenever a new Bishop of Durham first enters the Diocese by crossing the River Tees at Croft on Tees, a welcoming ceremony is held on the bridge.
claims.statement_id: Sejak saat itu hingga kini, setiap Uskup Durham baru yang pertama kali memasuki keuskupan dengan menyeberangi Sungai Tees di Croft on Tees disambut dengan upacara di jembatan.
claims.quote: From that time on to the present day, whenever a new Bishop of Durham enters the Diocese for the first time by crossing the River Tees at Croft on Tees, a welcoming ceremony is conducted on the bridge.

claims.statement: The reputation and pedigree of the Conyers family was firmly linked to the dragon their ancestor slew, and the Sockburn Worm was tied to the ceremonial ritual of the Palatinate.
claims.statement_id: Reputasi dan silsilah keluarga Conyers terikat erat pada naga yang dibunuh leluhurnya, dan Sockburn Worm terikat pada ritual upacara Palatinate.
claims.quote: The reputation and pedigree of the Conyers family was firmly linked to the dragon their ancestor had slayed. The Sockburn Worm was tied to the ceremonial ritual of the Palatinate.

claims.statement: For his efforts he received the lands of Sockburn from the Bishop of Durham.
claims.statement_id: Atas jasanya, Sir John menerima tanah Sockburn dari Uskup Durham.
claims.quote: and received the lands of Sockburn for his efforts from the Bishop of Durham.

claims.statement: Each newly appointed Bishop of Durham, on crossing the River Tees and entering the bishopric for the first time at Croft-on-Tees, received the sword.
claims.statement_id: Setiap Uskup Durham yang baru diangkat, saat menyeberangi Sungai Tees dan pertama kali memasuki keuskupan di Croft-on-Tees, menjadi penerima pedang itu.
claims.quote: Each newly appointed Bishop of Durham, on crossing the River Tees and entering the bishopric for the first time at Croft-on-Tees

claims.statement: Dyrnwch Gawr (variant: Dyrnhwch Gawr) is a Welsh giant (cawr Cymreig) associated with the Hen Ogledd and with Gwent.
claims.statement_id: Dyrnwch Gawr (varian: Dyrnhwch Gawr) adalah raksasa Welsh (cawr Cymreig) yang dikaitkan dengan Hen Ogledd dan Gwent.
claims.quote: Cawr Cymreig a gysylltir â'r Hen Ogledd ac â Gwent yw Dyrnwch Gawr (amrywiad, Dyrnhwch Gawr).

claims.statement: Dyrnwch Gawr is named in the list Tri Thlws ar Ddeg Ynys Prydain as the owner (perchennog) of a special cauldron (pair).
claims.statement_id: Dyrnwch Gawr disebut dalam daftar Tri Thlws ar Ddeg Ynys Prydain sebagai pemilik (perchennog) kuali (pair) istimewa.
claims.quote: Enwir Dyrnwch Gawr yn y rhestr Tri Thlws ar Ddeg Ynys Prydain fel perchennog pair arbennig

claims.statement: If meat (cig) for a coward (llwfr) were put in to boil, it would never boil (ni ferwai fyth); if meat for a brave man (dewr), it would boil (berwi) quickly.
claims.statement_id: Jika daging (cig) untuk orang pengecut (llwfr) dimasukkan untuk direbus, daging itu tidak akan pernah mendidih (ni ferwai fyth); jika daging untuk orang pemberani (dewr), ia cepat mendidih (berwi).
claims.quote: pe rhoid ynddo gig i ŵr llwfr i ferwi, ni ferwai fyth; o rhoid iddo gig i ŵr dewr, berwi a wnâi yn ebrwydd

claims.statement: A similar virtue is attributed to the Pair Pen Annwn mentioned in the poem 'Preiddiau Annwn' in Llyfr Taliesin, which does not boil (berwi) a coward's (llwfrgi) food.
claims.statement_id: Sifat serupa dikenakan pada Pair Pen Annwn yang disebut dalam puisi 'Preiddiau Annwn' di Llyfr Taliesin, yang tidak merebus (berwi) makanan pengecut (llwfrgi).
claims.quote: Priodolir rhinwedd cyffelyb i'r Pair Pen Annwn y cyfeirir ato yn y gerdd 'Preiddiau Annwn' yn Llyfr Taliesin, sydd ddim yn berwi bwyd llwfrgi.

claims.statement: It is almost certain that the story of the cauldron (pair) is based on a reference in the tale Culhwch ac Olwen to 'bair Diwrnach Wyddel' (the cauldron of Diwrnach Wyddel).
claims.statement_id: Hampir pasti kisah tentang kuali (pair) itu didasarkan pada rujukan dalam kisah Culhwch ac Olwen tentang 'bair Diwrnach Wyddel' (kuali Diwrnach Wyddel).
claims.quote: Mae hi bron yn sicr fod y stori am y pair yn seiliedig ar gyfeiriad yn y chwedl Culhwch ac Olwen am "bair Diwrnach Wyddel".

claims.statement: The Tri Thlws ar Ddeg are associated with the Hen Ogledd, but Dyrnwch (Ddyrnwch) is not mentioned in the genealogies (achau), e.g. Bonedd Gwŷr y Gogledd.
claims.statement_id: Tri Thlws ar Ddeg dikaitkan dengan Hen Ogledd, tetapi Dyrnwch (Ddyrnwch) tidak disebut dalam silsilah (achau), misalnya Bonedd Gwŷr y Gogledd.
claims.quote: Cysylltir y Tri Thlws ar Ddeg â'r Hen Ogledd, ond ni cheir cyfeiriad at Ddyrnwch yn yr achau (e.e. Bonedd Gwŷr y Gogledd).

claims.statement: The name Dyrn(h)wch is given by Siôn Dafydd Rhys at the end of the 16th century (16g) in his list (rhestr) of the giants of Cymru (gewri Cymru).
claims.statement_id: Nama Dyrn(h)wch tercantum dalam daftar (rhestr) raksasa Cymru (gewri Cymru) karya Siôn Dafydd Rhys pada akhir abad ke-16 (16g).
claims.quote: ceir enw Dyrn(h)wch gan Siôn Dafydd Rhys ar ddiwedd y 16g yn ei restr o gewri Cymru

claims.statement: Dyrnhwch Gawr in the land (gwlad) of Ewias.
claims.statement_id: Dyrnhwch Gawr di negeri (gwlad) Ewias.
claims.quote: Dyrnhwch Gawr yng ngwlad Ewias.

claims.statement: Because the names (enwau) Dyrnwch and Diwrnach are so alike, the former is probably a later form (ffurf ddiweddar) of the latter.
claims.statement_id: Karena nama (enwau) Dyrnwch dan Diwrnach sangat mirip, kemungkinan yang pertama adalah bentuk lebih muda (ffurf ddiweddar) dari yang kedua.
claims.quote: Am fod yr enwau Dyrnwch a Diwrnach mor debyg i'w gilydd mae'n debygol fod y cyntaf yn ffurf ddiweddar ar yr ail

claims.statement: There may be a link (cysylltiad) between Wrnach Gawr and Diwrnach Wyddel, and Dyrnwch Gawr may be a later development (datblygiad diweddarach) of those characters, but this cannot be proven conclusively.
claims.statement_id: Mungkin ada hubungan (cysylltiad) antara Wrnach Gawr dan Diwrnach Wyddel, dan Dyrnwch Gawr mungkin perkembangan lebih kemudian (datblygiad diweddarach) dari tokoh-tokoh itu, tetapi tidak dapat dibuktikan secara pasti.
claims.quote: Efallai fod cysylltiad rhwng Wrnach Gawr a Diwrnach Wyddel, er bod yr hanesion amdanynt yn wahanol, a bod Dyrnwch Gawr yn ddatblygiad diweddarach seiliedig ar y cymeriadau hynny, ond nid oes modd profi hynny'n derfynol.

claims.statement: The cauldron (pair) of Dyrnwch the Giant is said to discriminate between cowards and brave men: it would not boil meat for a coward but would boil quickly meat belonging to a brave man.
claims.statement_id: Kuali (pair) Dyrnwch sang Raksasa dikatakan membedakan pengecut dari pemberani: ia tidak merebus daging untuk pengecut, tetapi cepat merebus daging milik orang pemberani.
claims.quote: The cauldron (pair) of Dyrnwch the Giant is said to discriminate between cowards and brave men: whereas it would not boil meat for a coward, it would boil quickly if that meat belonged to a brave man.

claims.statement: Although Dyrnwch is not himself described as an Irishman, his name probably goes back to Diwrnach.
claims.statement_id: Walaupun Dyrnwch sendiri tidak disebut orang Irlandia (Irishman), kemungkinan besar namanya berasal dari Diwrnach.
claims.quote: Although Dyrnwch is not himself described as an Irishman, it is probable that his name goes back to Diwrnach.

claims.statement: The extant manuscripts of Tri Thlws ar Ddeg also give the variant spellings Dyrnog and Tyrnog, without the Irish-sounding ending.
claims.statement_id: Naskah-naskah Tri Thlws ar Ddeg yang masih ada juga memuat ejaan varian Dyrnog dan Tyrnog, tanpa akhiran yang berbunyi Irlandia.
claims.quote: The extant manuscripts of Tri Thlws ar Ddeg also present such variant spellings as Dyrnog and Tyrnog, without the Irish-sounding ending

claims.statement: Pair Dyrnwch Gawr means The Cauldron of Dyrnwch the Giant.
claims.statement_id: Pair Dyrnwch Gawr berarti Kuali Dyrnwch sang Raksasa (The Cauldron of Dyrnwch the Giant).
claims.quote: Pair Dyrnwch Gawr: The Cauldron of Dyrnwch the Giant

claims.statement: These treasures are ancient magical items of Welsh tradition mentioned in 15th and 16th century manuscripts; most of them are from 'The North' of the Island of Britain.
claims.statement_id: Pusaka-pusaka (treasures) ini adalah benda ajaib kuno tradisi Welsh yang disebut dalam naskah abad ke-15 dan ke-16; kebanyakan berasal dari 'The North' (Utara) Pulau Britania.
claims.quote: These treasures are ancient magical items of Welsh tradition that are mentioned in 15th and 16th Century manuscripts. Most of the treasures are from and in ‘The North’ of the Island of Britain.

claims.statement: The Thirteen Treasures of the Island of Britain (Welsh: Tri Thlws ar Ddeg Ynys Prydain) are a series of items in late-medieval Welsh tradition.
claims.statement_id: Tiga Belas Pusaka Pulau Britania (Thirteen Treasures of the Island of Britain; Welsh: Tri Thlws ar Ddeg Ynys Prydain) adalah serangkaian benda dalam tradisi Welsh akhir Abad Pertengahan.
claims.quote: The Thirteen Treasures of the Island of Britain (Welsh: Tri Thlws ar Ddeg Ynys Prydain) are a series of items in late-medieval Welsh tradition.

claims.statement: The Hampton Court ghost refers to a figure seen in CCTV footage near Hampton Court Palace in October 2003.
claims.statement_id: Hantu Hampton Court merujuk pada sosok yang terlihat dalam rekaman CCTV di dekat Istana Hampton Court pada Oktober 2003.
claims.quote: Hampton Court ghost refers to a figure seen in a CCTV footage/image near Hampton Court Palace in October 2003.

claims.statement: The figure was seen in a long robe-like cloth, allegedly haunting the place for a couple of days or months.
claims.statement_id: Sosok itu terlihat mengenakan kain panjang mirip jubah dan diduga menghantui tempat itu selama beberapa hari atau bulan.
claims.quote: The figure was seen in a long robe-like cloth allegedly haunting the place for a couple of days or months.

claims.statement: The figure was first reported in early 2001; a similar incident in 2015 was later debunked.
claims.statement_id: Sosok itu pertama kali dilaporkan pada awal 2001; kejadian serupa pada 2015 kemudian dibantah.
claims.quote: The figure was first reported in early-2001. A similar incident happened in 2015 but was later debunked.

claims.statement: Security guards noticed fire doors kept opening in an exhibition area, checked the footage and saw a figure in period dress.
claims.statement_id: Petugas keamanan mendapati pintu darurat di area pameran terus terbuka, lalu memeriksa rekaman dan melihat sosok berpakaian zaman dahulu.
claims.quote: Security guards spotted that fire doors kept opening in an exhibition area, and on one occasion checked the footage and saw a figure in period dress.

claims.statement: Warder James Faukes said it was spooky because the face just didn't look human.
claims.statement_id: Penjaga James Faukes berkata wajah sosok itu tidak tampak seperti wajah manusia.
claims.quote: It was incredibly spooky because the face just didn't look human," he said.

claims.statement: Warder Ian Franklin described someone in a full cloak walking forward, bringing in both doors and closing them behind them.
claims.statement_id: Penjaga Ian Franklin menggambarkan sosok bermantel penuh yang menarik kedua daun pintu lalu menutupnya di belakangnya.
claims.quote: State apartment warder Ian Franklin added: "Someone who appears to be in a full cloak walks forward, brings one door in, another door in and then closes it behind them.

claims.statement: CCTV cameras picked up the vision at the 16th-century Surrey palace, which has a reputation for being haunted.
claims.statement_id: Kamera CCTV menangkap penampakan itu di istana abad ke-16 di Surrey yang punya reputasi berhantu.
claims.quote: CCTV cameras picked up the vision at the 16th Century Surrey palace, which has a reputation for being haunted.

claims.statement: The first footage showed the doors flying open with no evidence why; the second time a ghostly figure in period dress appeared on screen and closed the doors.
claims.statement_id: Pertama kali rekaman menunjukkan pintu terbuka lebar tanpa sebab; kedua kalinya sosok seperti hantu berpakaian zaman dahulu muncul dan menutup pintu.
claims.quote: On the first occasion the footage showed the doors flying wide open, but no evidence of why they had. On the second, the guards were stunned when a ghostly figure in period dress suddenly appeared on the screen and closed the doors.

claims.statement: The same happened on a third day with no figure appearing; a visitor had also noted in the palace visitor book that she thought she had seen a ghost in that area.
claims.statement_id: Hal serupa terjadi pada hari ketiga tanpa sosok yang tampak; seorang pengunjung juga menulis di buku tamu istana bahwa ia merasa melihat hantu di area itu.
claims.quote: The same thing happened on a third day, but again no figure appeared. Stranger still was that a visitor had noted in the palace's visitor book that she thought she had seen a ghost in that area.

claims.statement: The area around the man is somewhat blurred, and his face appears unnaturally white compared with his outstretched hand.
claims.statement_id: Area di sekitar pria itu agak buram dan wajahnya tampak putih tidak wajar dibandingkan tangannya yang terjulur.
claims.quote: The area around the man is somewhat blurred, and his face appears unnaturally white compared with his outstretched hand.

claims.statement: In the still photograph, a man in a robelike garment is shown stepping from the shadowy doorway, one arm reaching for the door handle.
claims.statement_id: Dalam foto diam, sosok pria berpakaian mirip jubah tampak melangkah dari ambang pintu yang gelap sambil meraih gagang pintu.
claims.quote: In the still photograph, the figure of a man in a robelike garment is shown stepping from the shadowy doorway, one arm reaching out for the door handle.

claims.statement: A dark, distorted figure appeared in a picture taken by a 12-year-old girl while visiting the palace.
claims.statement_id: Sosok gelap yang terdistorsi muncul dalam foto yang diambil seorang anak perempuan berumur 12 tahun saat mengunjungi istana.
claims.quote: A dark, distorted figure popped up in a picture recently taken by a 12-year-old girl while she and a cousin were visiting the tourist-friendly palace.

claims.statement: Mick West says the 2015 photo looks like the effect created when someone walks through your line of sight while taking an iPhone panorama.
claims.statement_id: Mick West menilai foto 2015 itu mirip efek yang muncul ketika seseorang lewat di depan kamera saat mengambil panorama iPhone.
claims.quote: Metabunk.org's Mick West says it looks like the weird effect that's created when someone walks through your line of sight while you're taking an iPhone panorama.

claims.statement: The warder first thought someone was having a laugh, but the costumed guides don't own a costume like that.
claims.statement_id: Penjaga itu semula mengira ada yang bercanda, tetapi pemandu berkostum di istana tidak memiliki kostum seperti itu.
claims.quote: I thought someone was having a laugh but our costumed guides don't own a costume like that.

claims.statement: The 2015 picture purported to show the Grey Lady, the shade of a servant said to have nursed Queen Elizabeth I and died of smallpox in 1562.
claims.statement_id: Foto tahun 2015 itu diklaim menunjukkan Grey Lady, arwah seorang pelayan yang konon mengasuh Ratu Elizabeth I dan meninggal karena cacar pada 1562.
claims.quote: This time, it's about a picture purporting to show the "Grey Lady," the shade of a servant who is said to have nursed Queen Elizabeth I and died of smallpox in 1562.

claims.statement: Searrach Uisge is the name of a 'monster' from Scottish mythology (Schotse mythologie) said to live (zou leven) in the Scottish Loch Suainbhal.
claims.statement_id: Searrach Uisge adalah nama sebuah 'monster' (monster) dari mitologi Skotlandia (Schotse mythologie) yang dikatakan hidup di Loch Suainbhal di Skotlandia.
claims.quote: Searrach Uisge is de naam van een 'monster' uit de Schotse mythologie dat zou leven in het Schotse Loch Suainbhal.

claims.statement: The existence (bestaan) of this creature (wezen), like that of its compatriots Nessie and Morag, has never been proven (nooit aangetoond).
claims.statement_id: Keberadaan makhluk ini (wezen), seperti halnya Nessie dan Morag, tidak pernah dibuktikan (nooit aangetoond).
claims.quote: Het bestaan van dit wezen is evenals dat van landgenoten Nessie en Morag nooit aangetoond.

claims.statement: The Searrach Uisge is said to have the shape (vorm) of a capsized boat (gekapseisde boot) and be ten to thirteen metres (tien tot dertien meter) long.
claims.statement_id: Searrach Uisge dikatakan berbentuk perahu terbalik (gekapseisde boot) dan panjangnya sepuluh hingga tiga belas meter (tien tot dertien meter).
claims.quote: Searrach Uisge zou de vorm hebben van een gekapseisde boot en tien tot dertien meter lang zijn.

claims.statement: The first testimonies (eerste getuigenissen) of having seen the creature date from the early second half of the 19th century (19e eeuw).
claims.statement_id: Kesaksian pertama (eerste getuigenissen) tentang makhluk ini berasal dari awal paruh kedua abad ke-19 (19e eeuw).
claims.quote: De eerste getuigenissen die verklaren het wezen gezien te hebben, dateren uit de vroege tweede helft van de 19e eeuw.

claims.statement: According to tradition (overlevering), the local population once offered lambs (lammeren) to the Searrach Uisge once a year (eens per jaar).
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi (overlevering), penduduk setempat dahulu mempersembahkan anak domba (lammeren) kepada Searrach Uisge setahun sekali (eens per jaar).
claims.quote: Volgens de overlevering offerde vroeger de lokale bevolking eens per jaar lammeren aan Searrach Uisge.

claims.statement: The creature referred to as the Searrach Uisge is possibly a water horse of Loch Suainbhal.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk yang disebut Searrach Uisge mungkin adalah kuda air dari Loch Suainbhal.
claims.quote: The creature, possibly a water horse of Loch Suainbhal is referred to as the Searrach Uisge.

claims.statement: The creature was said to have inhabited the loch for over a century, and in the nineteenth century it was described as like a capsized boat when seen swimming around.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini dikatakan menghuni danau itu lebih dari satu abad, dan pada abad ke-19 ia digambarkan seperti perahu terbalik saat terlihat berenang.
claims.quote: The creature was said to inhabit the loch for over a century and in the nineteenth century it was described as being like an capsized boat when it was seen swimming around.

claims.statement: Another description has it forty feet long and eel-like.
claims.statement_id: Gambaran lain menyebutnya sepanjang empat puluh kaki dan mirip belut.
claims.quote: Another description has it being forty foot long and eel like.

claims.statement: It is said that locals offered lambs to the creature as an annual sacrifice to appease the beast.
claims.statement_id: Konon penduduk setempat mempersembahkan anak domba kepada makhluk ini sebagai korban tahunan untuk menenangkannya.
claims.quote: It is said that lambs would be offered to the creature by the locals as an annual sacrifice to appease the beast.

claims.statement: Segeta or Segesta is a goddess (déesse) of Celtic mythology (mythologie celtique), goddess of the Loire and eponymous deity of the Segusiavi people (peuple ségusiave).
claims.statement_id: Segeta atau Segesta adalah dewi (déesse) dalam mitologi Kelt (mythologie celtique), dewi Sungai Loire, dan dewi eponim suku Segusiavi (peuple ségusiave).
claims.quote: Segeta ou Segesta est une déesse de la mythologie celtique, déesse de la Loire et divinité éponyme du peuple ségusiave.

claims.statement: Associated with thermal waters (eaux thermales), she was also a healing goddess (déesse guérisseuse).
claims.statement_id: Ia dikaitkan dengan air panas alami (eaux thermales) dan juga merupakan dewi penyembuh (déesse guérisseuse).
claims.quote: Associée aux eaux thermales, c'était également une déesse guérisseuse.

claims.statement: Her name (nom) is thought to be based on the Gaulish (gaulois) Sego-, 'force, victory' (force, victoire).
claims.statement_id: Namanya (nom) diduga berasal dari kata Galia (gaulois) Sego- yang berarti 'kekuatan, kemenangan' (force, victoire).
claims.quote: Son nom serait basé sur le gaulois Sego- « force, victoire ».

claims.statement: She was celebrated (célébrée) particularly at Moingt, then a Gallo-Roman spa (station thermale gallo-romaine) attested under the name Aquis Segeta.
claims.statement_id: Ia terutama dipuja (célébrée) di Moingt, yang saat itu merupakan tempat pemandian Galia-Romawi (station thermale gallo-romaine) bernama Aquis Segeta.
claims.quote: Elle était célébrée plus particulièrement à Moingt, alors station thermale gallo-romaine attestée sous le nom d’Aquis Segeta

claims.statement: Aquis Segeste is identified with Sceaux-du-Gâtinais, one of the fifty-two spa towns (villes d'eau) of the Roman Empire (Empire romain) that were important places of pilgrimage (pèlerinage).
claims.statement_id: Aquis Segeste diidentifikasi dengan Sceaux-du-Gâtinais, salah satu dari lima puluh dua kota air (villes d'eau) Kekaisaran Romawi (Empire romain) yang menjadi tempat ziarah (pèlerinage) penting.
claims.quote: On identifie Aquis Segeste à Sceaux-du-Gâtinais, l’une des cinquante-deux villes d’eau de l’Empire romain qui ont été un lieu de pèlerinage important.

claims.statement: A circular plaque (plaque circulaire) of pink marble (marbre rose), 0.60 m in diameter, found at Sceaux-du-Gâtinais/Aquis Segeste in 1973, bears an inscription (inscription).
claims.statement_id: Sebuah lempeng bundar (plaque circulaire) dari marmer merah muda (marbre rose) berdiameter 0,60 m ditemukan di Sceaux-du-Gâtinais/Aquis Segeste pada tahun 1973 dan memuat sebuah prasasti (inscription).
claims.quote: Une plaque circulaire en marbre rose d'un diamètre de 0,60 m, trouvée sur le site de Sceaux-du-Gâtinais/Aquis Segeste en 1973, porte l'inscription suivante

claims.statement: Translation of the inscription: to the august goddess (déesse) Segeta, T. Marius Priscinus fulfilled his vow (vœu) willingly; Maria Sacra, his daughter (sa fille), saw to its making.
claims.statement_id: Terjemahan prasasti: kepada dewi (déesse) Segeta yang agung, T. Marius Priscinus telah memenuhi nazarnya (vœu); Maria Sacra, putrinya (sa fille), mengurus pembuatannya.
claims.quote: « À l'auguste déesse Segeta, T. Marius Priscinus s'est acquitté de son vœu de bonne grâce : Maria Sacra, sa fille, a pris soin de le réaliser »

claims.statement: Segeta had at least two important sanctuaries (sanctuaires), both thermal establishments (établissements thermaux): at Aquis Segeste, Sceaux-du-Gâtinais, and at Moingt.
claims.statement_id: Segeta memiliki sedikitnya dua tempat suci (sanctuaires) penting, keduanya pemandian air panas (établissements thermaux): di Aquis Segeste, Sceaux-du-Gâtinais, dan di Moingt.
claims.quote: Segeta avait au moins deux sanctuaires importants où elle était honorée, tous deux des établissements thermaux, le premier à Aquis Segeste, à Sceaux-du-Gâtinais, le deuxième à Moingt.

claims.statement: It seems that many of the pilgrims (pèlerins) were women (femmes) coming to implore or thank the goddess over problems of sterility (stérilité) or after childbirth (postnataux).
claims.statement_id: Tampaknya sebagian besar peziarah (pèlerins) adalah perempuan (femmes) yang datang untuk memohon atau berterima kasih kepada dewi itu atas masalah kemandulan (stérilité) atau pascapersalinan (postnataux).
claims.quote: Il semblerait qu'une grande partie des pèlerins étaient des femmes venant implorer ou remercier la déesse pour des problèmes de stérilité ou postnataux.

claims.statement: Segeta has many similarities (similitudes) with other Gaulish goddesses (déesses gauloises) of springs or thermal waters, such as Sirona and Damona.
claims.statement_id: Segeta memiliki banyak kemiripan (similitudes) dengan dewi-dewi Galia (déesses gauloises) lain dari mata air atau air panas, seperti Sirona dan Damona.
claims.quote: Segeta possède de nombreuses similitudes avec d'autres déesses gauloises des eaux de sources ou thermales, comme les déesses Sirona et Damona.

claims.statement: Other inscriptions (inscriptions) dedicated to Segeta were found at Bussy-Albieux and Feurs.
claims.statement_id: Prasasti (inscriptions) lain untuk Segeta ditemukan di Bussy-Albieux dan Feurs.
claims.quote: D'autres inscriptions dédiées à Segeta ont été trouvées à Bussy-Albieux, Feurs

claims.statement: The Gaulish goddess (déesse gauloise) Segeta is associated with waters (eaux) through the place names Aquae Segetae at Moingt; she was worshipped in Gaul.
claims.statement_id: Dewi Galia (déesse gauloise) Segeta dikaitkan dengan air (eaux) melalui nama tempat Aquae Segetae di Moingt; ia dipuja di Galia (Gaul).
claims.quote: La déesse gauloise Segeta est associée aux eaux avec les lieux-dits Aquae Segetae de Moingt

claims.statement: She may have been the principal goddess (déesse principale) of the Segusiavi (Ségusiaves), and her name may derive from Sego, 'force, victory' (force, victoire).
claims.statement_id: Ia mungkin dewi utama (déesse principale) suku Segusiavi (Ségusiaves), dan namanya diduga berasal dari Sego, 'kekuatan, kemenangan' (force, victoire).
claims.quote: elle a peut-être été la déesse principale chez les Ségusiaves et son nom dériverait de Sego, force, victoire.

claims.statement: It is customary to distinguish two goddesses (deux déesses): one is a Roman goddess (déesse romaine) Segetia whose cult is attested at Rome.
claims.statement_id: Biasanya dibedakan dua dewi (deux déesses): salah satunya dewi Romawi (déesse romaine) Segetia yang pemujaannya tercatat di Roma (Rome).
claims.quote: Rappelons qu'il est d'usage de distinguer deux déesses : — une déesse romaine Segetia dont le culte est attesté à Rome

claims.statement: Nony's aim is to bring the Segetia of the coin (monnaie) of Gallienus (Gallien) into the Gaulish pantheon (panthéon gaulois).
claims.statement_id: Tujuan Nony adalah memasukkan Segetia dari koin (monnaie) Gallienus (Gallien) ke dalam jajaran dewa Galia (panthéon gaulois).
claims.quote: Notre propos d'aujourd'hui est de faire entrer la Segetia de la monnaie de Gallien dans le panthéon gaulois

claims.statement: Since those goddesses were also prayed to alongside Apollo (Apollon), often honoured at thermal spas (stations thermales), Segeta may likewise have been associated (associée) with him.
claims.statement_id: Karena Sirona dan Damona juga dipuja bersama Apollo (Apollon), yang sering dihormati di pemandian air panas (stations thermales), ada kemungkinan Segeta juga dikaitkan (associée) dengan Apollo.
claims.quote: Ces dernières ayant été également priées seules ou conjointement avec Apollon, souvent honoré dans des stations thermales, il est possible que Segeta ait été pareillement associée à ce dernier

claims.statement: The Seileag (an Seileag) is a monster (ollphéist) thought to live in Loch Seile (Loch Shiel), Highland (Comhairle na Gàidhealtachd).
claims.statement_id: Seileag (an Seileag) adalah monster (ollphéist) yang dipercaya tinggal di Loch Seile (Loch Shiel), wilayah Highland (Comhairle na Gàidhealtachd).
claims.quote: Is ollphéist a cheaptar a bheith ina gcónaí i Loch Seile, Comhairle na Gàidhealtachd í Niseag nó an Seileag.

claims.statement: The list covers lochs in Scotland said to contain monsters in Scottish folklore.
claims.statement_id: Daftar ini memuat danau-danau di Skotlandia yang menurut cerita rakyat Skotlandia dihuni monster.
claims.quote: List of Scottish loch-monsters is a list of lochs in Scotland said to contain monsters in Scottish folklore.

claims.statement: The Loch Shiel monster, Seileag, is described as having three humps and being 70 ft long.
claims.statement_id: Monster Loch Shiel bernama Seileag digambarkan memiliki tiga punuk dan panjang 70 kaki (70 ft).
claims.quote: Loch Shiel Seileag three humps and 70 ft long

claims.statement: Loch Shiel (Scottish Gaelic: Loch Seile) is a deep freshwater loch 20 kilometres west of Fort William in Lochaber, Scotland.
claims.statement_id: Loch Shiel (bahasa Gael Skotlandia: Loch Seile) adalah danau air tawar yang dalam, sekitar 20 kilometer di sebelah barat Fort William di Lochaber, Skotlandia.
claims.quote: Loch Shiel (Scottish Gaelic: Loch Seile ... is a deep freshwater loch situated 20 kilometres (12 mi) west of Fort William in Lochaber, Scotland.

claims.statement: Loch Shiel is the longest loch to have retained a natural outflow without regulation of its water level, being 120 m deep.
claims.statement_id: Loch Shiel adalah danau terpanjang yang aliran keluarnya masih alami tanpa pengaturan muka air, dengan kedalaman 120 m.
claims.quote: is the longest to have retained a natural outflow without any regulation of its water level, being 120 m (393 ft) deep.

claims.statement: Its nature changes along its length: deep and enclosed by mountains in the north east, shallow and surrounded by bog and rough pasture in the south west.
claims.statement_id: Sifat danau ini berubah di sepanjang badannya: dalam dan diapit pegunungan di timur laut, dangkal dan dikelilingi rawa serta padang rumput kasar di barat daya.
claims.quote: Its nature changes considerably along its length, being deep and enclosed by mountains in the north east and shallow surrounded by bog and rough pasture in the south west

claims.statement: Eog Llyn Llyw is the oldest (hynaf) and wisest (doethaf) of the Oldest Animals (Anifeiliaid Hynaf) named in the tale (chwedl) Culhwch ac Olwen.
claims.statement_id: Eog Llyn Llyw adalah yang tertua (hynaf) dan terbijak (doethaf) di antara Hewan-Hewan Tertua (Anifeiliaid Hynaf) yang disebut dalam kisah (chwedl) Culhwch ac Olwen.
claims.quote: Eog Llyn Llyw yw'r hynaf a'r doethaf o'r Anifeiliaid Hynaf a nodir yn chwedl Culhwch ac Olwen.

claims.statement: One of the Anoethau (impossible tasks, tasgau amhosibl) set on the hero Culhwch by Ysbaddaden Bencawr in the tale is to free (rhyddhau) Mabon fab Modron from his prison (garchar).
claims.statement_id: Salah satu Anoethau (tugas mustahil, tasgau amhosibl) yang diberikan Ysbaddaden Bencawr kepada pahlawan Culhwch dalam kisah itu adalah membebaskan (rhyddhau) Mabon fab Modron dari penjaranya (garchar).
claims.quote: Un o'r Anoethau (tasgau amhosibl) a osodir ar yr arwr Culhwch gan Ysbaddaden Bencawr yn y chwedl yw rhyddhau Mabon fab Modron o'i garchar.

claims.statement: Eryr Gwern Abwy leads (tywys) them to Eog Llyn Llyw.
claims.statement_id: Eryr Gwern Abwy menuntun (tywys) mereka kepada Eog Llyn Llyw.
claims.quote: Mae Eryr Gwern Abwy yn eu tywys i Eog Llyn Llyw.

claims.statement: The Salmon (Eog) explains that it used to swim (nofio) along the river (afon) every night until it came to the walls of Caerloyw (Gloucester), where it heard terrible groaning from the castle tower.
claims.statement_id: Sang salmon (Eog) menjelaskan bahwa ia biasa berenang (nofio) menyusuri sungai (afon) setiap malam sampai ke tembok Caerloyw (Gloucester), tempat ia mendengar rintihan mengerikan dari menara kastel.
claims.quote: Mae'r Eog yn esbonio fel ei fod yn arfer nofio ar hyd yr afon bob nos hyd daw i furiau Caerloyw lle mae'n clywed griddfan ofnadwy yn dod o dŵr y castell.

claims.statement: It offers to carry (cludo) Gwrhyr and Eidoel on its shoulders (ysgwyddau) to see for themselves; they manage to speak with the prisoner (carcharor), who is none other than Mabon fab Modron.
claims.statement_id: Ia menawarkan untuk membawa (cludo) Gwrhyr dan Eidoel di atas bahunya (ysgwyddau) agar mereka melihat sendiri; mereka berhasil berbicara dengan tahanan (carcharor), yang tak lain adalah Mabon fab Modron.
claims.quote: Mae'n cynnig cludo Gwrhyr ac Eidoel ar ei ysgwyddau i weld drostynt eu hunain. Llwyddant i siarad â'r carcharor sydd neb llai na Mabon fab Modron.

claims.statement: Cei and Bedwyr go along the river (afon) on the shoulders (ysgwyddau) of Eog Llyn Llyw; they reach the tower on the river bank, and Cei tears down the walls (muriau) and frees (rhyddhau) Mabon.
claims.statement_id: Cei dan Bedwyr menyusuri sungai (afon) di atas bahu (ysgwyddau) Eog Llyn Llyw; mereka sampai ke menara di tepi sungai, dan Cei menjebol tembok (muriau) lalu membebaskan (rhyddhau) Mabon.
claims.quote: aiff Cei a Bedwyr ar hyd yr afon ar ysgwyddau Eog Llyn Llyw. Cyrhaeddent y tŵr ar lan yr afon ac mae Cei yn rhwygo'r muriau ac yn rhyddhau Mabon.

claims.statement: Eog Llyn Llyw can be classed with the many examples of supernatural salmon (eogiaid goruwchnaturiol) in the Celtic world (byd y Celtiaid); the salmon (eog) is associated with knowledge (gwybodaeth) and wisdom (doethineb).
claims.statement_id: Eog Llyn Llyw dapat digolongkan bersama banyak contoh salmon adikodrati (eogiaid goruwchnaturiol) di dunia Celtic (byd y Celtiaid); salmon (eog) dikaitkan dengan pengetahuan (gwybodaeth) dan kebijaksanaan (doethineb).
claims.quote: Gellir dosbarthu Eog Llyn Llyw gyda'r sawl enghraifft o eogiaid goruwchnaturiol ym myd y Celtiaid. Cysylltir yr eog â gwybodaeth a doethineb.

claims.statement: The Irish hero (arwr Gwyddelig) Finn mac Cumaill, for example, gains the gift of a prophet (proffwyd) and sage after putting his thumb in his mouth having touched a special salmon (eog).
claims.statement_id: Pahlawan Irlandia (arwr Gwyddelig) Finn mac Cumaill, misalnya, mendapat karunia nabi (proffwyd) dan orang bijak setelah memasukkan ibu jarinya ke mulut sesudah menyentuh salmon (eog) istimewa.
claims.quote: Mae'r arwr Gwyddelig Finn mac Cumaill er enghraifft yn cael dawn proffwyd a doethwr ar ôl rhoi ei fawd yn ei geg ar ôl cyffwrdd eog arbennig.

claims.statement: The location (lleoliad) of Llyn Llyw is uncertain (ansicr), but the fact that the Salmon (Eog) swims upriver to Caerloyw (Gaerloyw) suggests it lies around the lower part of Afon Hafren.
claims.statement_id: Letak (lleoliad) Llyn Llyw tidak pasti (ansicr), tetapi karena salmon (Eog) itu berenang ke hulu menuju Caerloyw (Gaerloyw), diduga tempat itu berada di sekitar bagian hilir Afon Hafren.
claims.quote: Mae lleoliad Llyn Llyw yn ansicr, ond mae'r ffaith fod yr Eog yn nofio i fyny'r afon i Gaerloyw yn awgrymu ei fod o gwmpas rhan isaf Afon Hafren.

claims.statement: The eagle tells how it went in search of food as far as Llyn Llyw and struck its talons into a salmon, but the salmon drew it into the deep and it was scarcely able to escape.
claims.statement_id: Sang elang bercerita bahwa ia mencari makanan sampai ke Llyn Llyw, mencengkeram seekor salmon dengan cakarnya, tetapi salmon itu menyeretnya ke dalam air dalam (the deep) sehingga ia nyaris tidak bisa lolos.
claims.quote: went in search of food as far as Llyn Llyw. And when I came there, I struck my talons into a salmon, thinking he would serve me as food for a long time. But he drew me into the deep, and I was scarcely able to escape from him.

claims.statement: The Hwch Ddu Gwta is a supernatural (goruwchnaturiol) sow in Welsh folklore (llên gwerin Cymru) associated with Nos Galan Gaeaf; in the south (De) she is called Hwch Ddu Gota.
claims.statement_id: Hwch Ddu Gwta adalah babi betina (hwch) gaib dalam cerita rakyat Wales (llên gwerin Cymru) yang dikaitkan dengan Nos Galan Gaeaf; di selatan (De) disebut Hwch Ddu Gota.
claims.quote: oruwchnaturiol yn llên gwerin Cymru a gysylltir â Nos Galan Gaeaf yw'r Hwch Ddu Gwta (Hwch Ddu Gota yn y De)

claims.statement: In Wales (Cymru) she is linked mainly with the north-west (gogledd-orllewin), especially Ynys Môn, but traditions about her are also found in Clwyd and Morgannwg.
claims.statement_id: Di Wales (Cymru) ia terutama dikaitkan dengan barat laut, khususnya Ynys Môn, tetapi tradisinya juga ada di Clwyd dan Morgannwg.
claims.quote: Yng Nghymru fe'i cysylltir yn bennaf â'r gogledd-orllewin, yn enwedig Ynys Môn, ond ceir traddodiadau amdani yng Nghlwyd a Morgannwg yn ogystal.

claims.statement: The Hwch Ddu Gwta was believed to take shape from the last sparks of the bonfire (coelcerth) and rush after the last (olaf) to leave in order to eat them.
claims.statement_id: Dipercaya Hwch Ddu Gwta menjelma dari percikan terakhir api unggun (coelcerth) dan memburu orang terakhir yang pergi untuk memakannya.
claims.quote: Credid bod yr Hwch Ddu Gwta yn ymrithio o wreichion olaf y goelcerth ac yn rhuthro ar ôl yr olaf i adael i'w bwyta.

claims.statement: In the Mynydd Hiraethog area of Clwyd, everyone would run home (adref) shouting.
claims.statement_id: Di daerah Mynydd Hiraethog, Clwyd, semua orang lari pulang (adref) sambil berteriak.
claims.quote: Yn ardal Mynydd Hiraethog, Clwyd, byddai pawb yn ei heglu hi adref gan weiddi,

claims.statement: The tradition (traddodiad) was especially strong in Môn, even in the first half of the 19th century (19g).
claims.statement_id: Tradisi (traddodiad) ini sangat kuat di Môn, bahkan pada paruh pertama abad ke-19 (19g).
claims.quote: Roedd y traddodiad yn arbennig o gryf ym Môn, hyd yn oed yn hanner cyntaf y 19g.

claims.statement: In Arfon and around, the Hwch Ddu Gwta was believed to sit on top of the stile (camfa) awaiting her chance.
claims.statement_id: Di Arfon dan sekitarnya dipercaya Hwch Ddu Gwta duduk di atas tangga pagar (camfa) menunggu kesempatan.
claims.quote: Yn Arfon a'r cylch credid bod yr Hwch Ddu Gwta yn eistedd ar ben y gamfa yn aros ei chyfle.

claims.statement: In the borderlands (y Gororau) she was also seen, with a round tail (cynffon gron), writhing on top of the stile.
claims.statement_id: Di daerah perbatasan (y Gororau) ia juga terlihat, dengan ekor bulat (cynffon gron), menggeliat di atas tangga pagar.
claims.quote: Ar y Gororau roedd hi i'w gweld hefyd, gyda chynffon gron, yn ymdroelli ar ben y gamfa.

claims.statement: The Nos Galan Gaeaf bonfire custom derives from the time of the Celts (Celtiaid) and rites linked to the festival of Samhain.
claims.statement_id: Kebiasaan api unggun Nos Galan Gaeaf berasal dari masa Kelt (Celtiaid) dan ritus yang terkait dengan perayaan Samhain.
claims.quote: Mae'n arfer sy'n deillio o gyfnod y Celtiaid a defodau sy'n gysylltiedig â gŵyl Samhain

claims.statement: On that night the ghosts of the dead were believed to be seen at midnight on every stile; in different parts of Wales these ghosts took different characters, one of the most common being the ladi wen (white lady).
claims.statement_id: Pada malam itu arwah orang mati dipercaya terlihat pada tengah malam di setiap tangga pagar; di berbagai bagian Wales wujudnya berbeda, dan salah satu yang paling umum adalah ladi wen (perempuan putih).
claims.quote: Not only were spirits said to roam freely but it was believed that the ghosts of the dead were to be seen at midnight on every stile. In different parts of Wales these ghosts took on different characters but two of the most common were the ladi wen [white lady]

claims.statement: Another common one, mainly in North Wales, was the tail-less black sow (hwch ddu gwta), associated with bonfires after dark; as the fire died down people feared the black sow's appearance.
claims.statement_id: Sosok umum lainnya, terutama di Wales Utara, adalah babi betina hitam tanpa ekor (hwch ddu gwta) yang dikaitkan dengan api unggun; saat api padam orang takut babi hitam itu muncul.
claims.quote: mainly in North Wales the tail-less black sow [hwch ddu gwta] and was associated with lighting bonfires after dark, as the fire died down they feared the appearance of the black sow

claims.statement: The rhyme urges being first at home, since the tail-less black sow is sure to roam.
claims.statement_id: Sajaknya mengingatkan agar menjadi yang pertama tiba di rumah karena babi betina hitam tanpa ekor pasti berkeliaran.
claims.quote: Be sure you are the first at home, the tail-less black sow is sure to roam.

claims.statement: Another rhyme says the black sow and headless white lady will try and catch the last to leave.
claims.statement_id: Sajak lain menyebut babi hitam dan perempuan putih tanpa kepala akan berusaha menangkap orang terakhir yang pergi.
claims.quote: The black sow and headless white lady, Will try and catch the last to leave

claims.statement: Eryr Gwern Abwy (the Eagle of Gwern Abwy) is one of the Oldest Animals (Anifeiliaid Hynaf) in the mythology of Wales (Cymru) and is mentioned in the tale Culhwch ac Olwen.
claims.statement_id: Eryr Gwern Abwy (elang Gwern Abwy) adalah salah satu Hewan Tertua (Anifeiliaid Hynaf) dalam mitologi Wales (Cymru) dan disebut dalam kisah Culhwch ac Olwen.
claims.quote: Un o'r Anifeiliaid Hynaf yn chwedloniaeth Cymru yw Eryr Gwern Abwy. Cyfeirir at yr eryr mytholegol hwn yn chwedl Culhwch ac Olwen.

claims.statement: The owl (tylluan) directs the envoys to Eryr Gwern Abwy; the eagle does not know, but guides them to Eog Llyn Llyw (the Salmon of Llyn Llyw).
claims.statement_id: Burung hantu (tylluan) mengarahkan para utusan kepada Eryr Gwern Abwy; elang itu tidak tahu, tetapi menuntun mereka kepada Eog Llyn Llyw (Salmon dari Llyn Llyw).
claims.quote: Cyfarwydda'r dylluan hwy at Eryr Gwern Abwy. Ni ŵyr yr eryr, ond mae'n eu tywys at Eog Llyn Llyw

claims.statement: In the Trioedd (Triads), the Tri Hynaif Byd (Three Oldest of the World) are named as Tylluan Cwm Cowlyd, Eryr Gwern Abwy and Mwyalchen Gelli Gadarn.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Trioedd (Triad), Tri Hynaif Byd (Tiga Tertua di Dunia) disebut sebagai Tylluan Cwm Cowlyd, Eryr Gwern Abwy, dan Mwyalchen Gelli Gadarn.
claims.quote: Yn y Trioedd, enwir Tri Hynaif Byd fel Tylluan Cwm Cowlyd, Eryr Gwern Abwy a Mwyalchen Gelli Gadarn.

claims.statement: The eagle (eryr) is an important bird in Celtic mythology (y Celtiaid) and is associated with the Sun (yr Haul).
claims.statement_id: Elang (eryr) adalah burung penting dalam mitologi bangsa Kelt (y Celtiaid) dan dikaitkan dengan Matahari (yr Haul).
claims.quote: Mae'r eryr yn aderyn pwysig ym mytholeg y Celtiaid. Fe'i cysylltir â'r Haul.

claims.statement: The location of Gwern Abwy is unknown (anhysbys).
claims.statement_id: Lokasi Gwern Abwy tidak diketahui (anhysbys).
claims.quote: Mae lleoliad Gwern Abwy yn anhysbys.

claims.statement: The owl guides the envoys to the oldest animal in this world, and the one that has travelled most, the Eagle of Gwern Abwy.
claims.statement_id: Burung hantu menuntun para utusan ke tempat hewan tertua di dunia ini, yang paling banyak mengembara, Elang Gwern Abwy.
claims.quote: the place where is the oldest animal in this world, and the one that has travelled most, the Eagle of Gwern Abwy.

claims.statement_id: Elang berkata saat pertama datang ada batu yang puncaknya ia patuk bintang-bintang setiap malam, dan kini batu itu tingginya tak sampai sejengkal.
claims.quote: when I first came hither there was a rock here, from the top of which I pecked at the stars every evening; and now it is not so much as a span high.

claims.statement: Fat Lips (Fatlips) is the name given to a legendary spirit dwelling in Dryburgh Abbey in Berwickshire, Scotland.
claims.statement_id: Fat Lips (Fatlips) adalah nama untuk roh legendaris yang menghuni Dryburgh Abbey di Berwickshire, Skotlandia.
claims.quote: Fat Lips (or Fatlips) is the name given to a legendary spirit dwelling in Dryburgh Abbey in Berwickshire, Scotland.

claims.statement: The spirit was associated with a homeless woman who moved into a vault beneath the ruins of the abbey some time after the 1745 Jacobite rising.
claims.statement_id: Roh ini dikaitkan dengan seorang perempuan tunawisma yang pindah ke sebuah ruang bawah tanah di bawah reruntuhan biara beberapa waktu setelah pemberontakan Jacobite 1745.
claims.quote: The spirit was associated with a homeless woman who moved into a vault beneath the ruins of the abbey some time after the 1745 Jacobite rising.

claims.statement: According to the woman, Fatlips was a little man who tidied the room while she was away and kept her cell dry by stamping moisture from the ground with his heavy iron boots.
claims.statement_id: Menurut perempuan itu, Fatlips adalah lelaki kecil yang merapikan ruangan saat ia pergi dan menjaga selnya tetap kering dengan menginjak-injak kelembapan dari tanah memakai sepatu bot besinya yang berat.
claims.quote: was a little man who tidied the room while she was away, and kept the cell she lived in dry by stamping moisture away from the ground with his heavy iron boots.

claims.statement: An unfortunate female wanderer lived in a dark vault among the ruins of Dryburgh Abbey, which she never left during the day.
claims.statement_id: Seorang perempuan pengembara yang malang tinggal di sebuah ruang bawah tanah yang gelap di antara reruntuhan Dryburgh Abbey dan tidak pernah meninggalkannya pada siang hari.
claims.quote: an unfortunate female wanderer took up her residence in a dark vault, among the ruins of Dryburgh Abbey, which during the day, she never quitted.

claims.statement: The woman said her dwelling was arranged by a spirit she named Fatlips, describing him as a little man in heavy iron shoes who trampled the clay floor of the vault to dispel the damps.
claims.statement_id: Perempuan itu mengatakan tempat tinggalnya ditata oleh sebuah roh yang ia beri nama Fatlips; ia menggambarkannya sebagai lelaki kecil bersepatu besi berat yang menginjak lantai tanah liat ruang bawah tanah itu untuk mengusir lembap.
claims.quote: her habitation was arranged by a spirit, to whom she gave the uncouth name of Fatlips, describing him as a little man, wearing heavy iron shoes, with which he trampled the clay floor of the vault, to dispel the damps.

claims.statement: Because of this, the well-informed regarded her with compassion as deranged in understanding, and the common people regarded her with some terror.
claims.statement_id: Karena hal ini, orang yang berpengetahuan memandangnya dengan iba sebagai orang yang terganggu akalnya, sedangkan orang awam memandangnya dengan rasa takut.
claims.quote: This circumstance caused her to be regarded, by the well-informed, with compassion, as deranged in her understanding; and by the vulgar, with some degree of terror.

claims.statement: Her way of life was believed to stem from a vow that, while the man to whom she was attached was away, she would never look upon the sun. Her lover never returned.
claims.statement_id: Cara hidupnya diyakini berasal dari sumpah bahwa selama lelaki yang dicintainya pergi, ia tidak akan memandang matahari. Kekasihnya tidak pernah kembali.
claims.quote: It was, however, believed to have been occasioned by a vow that, during the absence of a man to whom she was attached, she would never look upon the sun. Her lover never returned.

claims.statement: The lover fell during the civil war of 1745-46, and she never again beheld the light of day.
claims.statement_id: Kekasih itu gugur dalam perang saudara 1745–46, dan sejak itu ia tidak lagi melihat cahaya siang.
claims.quote: He fell during the civil war of 1745-46, and she never more would behold the light of day.

claims.statement: The vault where the woman lived and died still bears the name of the supernatural being with which, in the author's words, her disturbed imagination peopled its gloom, and few neighbouring peasants dare enter it by night.
claims.statement_id: Ruang bawah tanah tempat perempuan itu hidup dan meninggal masih dinamai menurut makhluk gaib yang menurut penulis dihuni oleh khayalannya yang terganggu, dan hanya sedikit petani sekitar yang berani memasukinya pada malam hari.
claims.quote: The vault, or rather dungeon, in which this unfortunate woman lived and died, passes still by the name of the supernatural being with which its gloom was tenanted by her disturbed imagination, and few of the neighbouring peasants dare enter it by night.

claims.statement: In Orkney folklore, Finfolk (sometimes Finnfolk) are sorcerous shapeshifters of the sea, the dark mysterious race from Finfolkaheem.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Orkney, Finfolk (kadang Finnfolk) adalah pengubah wujud penyihir dari laut, ras gelap dan misterius dari Finfolkaheem.
claims.quote: In Orkney folklore, Finfolk (sometimes Finnfolk) are sorcerous shapeshifters of the sea, the dark mysterious race from Finfolkaheem

claims.statement: The Finfolk (both Finman and Finwife) kidnap unsuspecting fishermen or frolicking youth near the shore and force them into lifelong servitude as a spouse.
claims.statement_id: Finfolk (baik Finman maupun Finwife) menculik nelayan yang lengah atau pemuda yang bermain dekat pantai dan memaksa mereka menjadi pasangan seumur hidup.
claims.quote: The Finfolk (both Finman and Finwife) kidnap unsuspecting fishermen, or frolicking youth, near the shore and force them into lifelong servitude as a spouse.

claims.statement: The Finman is said to have many magical powers, such as rowing between Norway and Orkney in seven oar-strokes, making his ship invisible and creating fleets of phantom boats.
claims.statement_id: Finman dikatakan punya banyak kekuatan gaib, seperti mendayung antara Norwegia dan Orkney dalam tujuh kayuhan, membuat kapalnya tak terlihat, dan menciptakan armada perahu hantu.
claims.quote: He is said to have many magical powers, such as rowing between Norway and Orkney in seven oar-strokes, making his ship invisible and creating fleets of phantom boats.

claims.statement: The Finman may sometimes be deterred by drawing a cross on the bottom of a craft with chalk or tar, for the Finfolk abhor the sign of the Christian cross.
claims.statement_id: Finman kadang dapat dihalau dengan menggambar salib di dasar perahu memakai kapur atau ter, karena Finfolk membenci tanda salib Kristen.
claims.quote: though he may sometimes be deterred by drawing a cross on the bottom of a craft with chalk or tar, for Finfolk abhor the sign of the Christian cross

claims.statement: The Finwife starts her life as a beautiful mermaid bent on acquiring a human husband.
claims.statement_id: Finwife memulai hidupnya sebagai putri duyung cantik yang bertekad mendapatkan suami manusia.
claims.quote: The Finwife starts her life as a beautiful mermaid bent on acquiring a human husband.

claims.statement: The Finfolk were said to have two homes: the magical underwater world of Finfolkaheem where they lived in the winter, and the island of Hildaland.
claims.statement_id: Finfolk dikatakan punya dua tempat tinggal: dunia bawah laut ajaib Finfolkaheem tempat mereka tinggal pada musim dingin, dan pulau Hildaland.
claims.quote: The Finfolk were said to have two homes: the magical underwater world of Finfolkaheem where they lived in the winter, and the island of Hildaland.

claims.statement: Hildaland is described as a paradisiacal island said to be invisible, hidden just underwater, or surrounded by magical fog.
claims.statement_id: Hildaland digambarkan sebagai pulau surgawi yang dikatakan tak terlihat, tersembunyi tepat di bawah air, atau diselimuti kabut gaib.
claims.quote: a paradisiacal island that was said to either be invisible, hidden just underwater, or surrounded by magical fog.

claims.statement: Besides their lust for humans, Finfolk have a weakness for silver; according to legend, a way to escape abduction is to toss silver coins away from oneself.
claims.statement_id: Selain nafsunya pada manusia, Finfolk lemah terhadap perak; menurut legenda, cara lolos dari penculikan ialah melempar koin perak menjauh dari diri.
claims.quote: Finfolk, in addition to their lust for humans, have a weakness for silver, including silver coins and jewelry. According to legend, a possible way to escape abduction is to exploit this Finfolk weakness by tossing silver coins away from oneself.

claims.statement: The Fin Folk are described as a mythological race unique to Orkney and Shetland.
claims.statement_id: Fin Folk disebut sebagai ras mitologis yang khas bagi Orkney dan Shetland.
claims.quote: One mythological race of beings which embodies all of the influences discussed above is the Fin Folk, who are unique to Orkney and Shetland.

claims.statement: The Fin Folk are an amphibious sea people who can step from the water onto land at will, and are described as both threatening and benevolent.
claims.statement_id: Fin Folk adalah bangsa laut amfibi yang dapat keluar dari air ke darat sesuka hati, dan digambarkan sekaligus mengancam dan baik hati.
claims.quote: their race is that of an amphibious sea people who can step out of the water onto land as they choose, and live comfortably between the two worlds. They are both threatening and benevolent.

claims.statement: Known as powerful sorcerers, Fin Folk can control the weather; they may reward fishermen with pleasant seas or punish them with treacherous storms.
claims.statement_id: Dikenal sebagai penyihir ampuh, Fin Folk dapat mengendalikan cuaca; mereka bisa memberi nelayan laut yang tenang atau menghukum dengan badai berbahaya.
claims.quote: Known as powerful sorcerers, Fin Folk can control the weather. They may reward fishermen with pleasant sea waters, or punish them with treacherous storms.

claims.statement: Fin Folk value silver greatly and are loath to part with it.
claims.statement_id: Fin Folk sangat menghargai perak dan enggan melepaskannya.
claims.quote: But never silver, for Fin Folk value silver greatly and are loathe parting with it.

claims.statement: Female Fin children are born with the fish tail of a mermaid, which they wear until maturity when the tail splits into legs.
claims.statement_id: Anak perempuan Fin lahir dengan ekor ikan putri duyung, yang mereka pakai sampai dewasa ketika ekor itu terbelah menjadi kaki.
claims.quote: Female Fin children, however, are born with the fish tail of a mermaid, which they wear until they reach maturity when their tail will split into legs.

claims.statement: Freybug is a monstrous Black Dog that is stated to come from medieval English folklore, specifically from Norfolk.
claims.statement_id: Freybug adalah Anjing Hitam yang mengerikan yang dinyatakan berasal dari cerita rakyat Inggris abad pertengahan, khususnya dari Norfolk.
claims.quote: Freybug is a monstrous Black Dog that is stated to come from medieval English folklore, specifically from Norfolk.

claims.statement: Like most supernatural black dogs, it was roughly the size of a calf and wandered country roads terrifying travelers.
claims.statement_id: Seperti kebanyakan anjing hitam gaib, ukurannya kira-kira sebesar anak sapi dan berkeliaran di jalan pedesaan menakuti para pelancong.
claims.quote: Like most supernatural black dogs, it was roughly the size of a calf, and wandered country roads terrifying travelers.

claims.statement: The English martyr Laurence Saunders mentioned Fray-bugs in his letters to his wife in 1555.
claims.statement_id: Martir Inggris Laurence Saunders menyebut Fray-bug dalam surat-suratnya kepada istrinya pada 1555.
claims.quote: The English martyr Laurence Saunders mentioned Fray-bugs in his letters to his wife in 1555.

claims.statement: The author John Brand suggested that the Fray-bug was a Black Dog similar to the Barghest.
claims.statement_id: John Brand menafsirkan bahwa Fray-bug adalah Anjing Hitam yang mirip Barghest.
claims.quote: suggested that the Fray-bug was a Black Dog similar to the Barghest.

claims.statement: The dictionary defines fray-bug as an object of fear, a bogy or spectre, and fray-boggard as a scarecrow.
claims.statement_id: Kamus mendefinisikan fray-bug sebagai objek yang ditakuti, hantu atau momok, dan fray-boggard sebagai orang-orangan sawah.
claims.quote: fray-boggard, a scarecrow; fray-bug, an object of fear; a bogy, spectre

claims.statement: The dictionary cites a 1555 writing of Saunders that reads "It fantasyeth forsooth much feare of fray bugges".
claims.statement_id: Kamus mengutip tulisan Saunders (1555) yang berbunyi "It fantasyeth forsooth much feare of fray bugges".
claims.quote: It fantasyeth forsooth much feare of *fray bugges.

claims.statement: Grant, or Gyant, is a creature of English folklore described in the medieval Latin work Otia Imperialia by Gervase of Tilbury.
claims.statement_id: Grant, atau Gyant, adalah makhluk dalam cerita rakyat Inggris yang dijelaskan dalam karya Latin abad pertengahan Otia Imperialia oleh Gervase dari Tilbury.
claims.quote: Grant, or Gyant, is a creature of English folklore described in the medieval Latin work Otia Imperialia by Gervase of Tilbury.

claims.statement: Gervase's account is the only known medieval source to name the creature.
claims.statement_id: Catatan Gervase adalah satu-satunya sumber abad pertengahan yang diketahui yang menyebut nama makhluk ini.
claims.quote: Gervase's account is the only known medieval source to name the creature.

claims.statement: Francis Young links the Grant to a wider motif in Britain and Ireland of horse-like bogies met by travellers on isolated roads, such as the púca, kelpie or shagfoal.
claims.statement_id: Francis Young mengaitkan Grant dengan motif yang lebih luas di Britania dan Irlandia tentang momok mirip kuda yang ditemui pelancong di jalan terpencil, seperti púca, kelpie, atau shagfoal.
claims.quote: Francis Young links the Grant to a wider motif in Britain and Ireland of horse-like bogies encountered on isolated roads by travellers, such as the púca, kelpie, or shagfoal

claims.statement: Joseph Pentangelo instead argues that it was probably a hare, and that the description in the Otia Imperialia may reflect embellishment by Gervase or his informant.
claims.statement_id: Joseph Pentangelo sebaliknya berpendapat bahwa makhluk itu mungkin seekor kelinci liar (hare), dan bahwa gambaran dalam Otia Imperialia mungkin hasil pemolesan oleh Gervase atau narasumbernya.
claims.quote: Joseph Pentangelo instead argues that it was probably a hare, and that the description in the Otia Imperialia may reflect embellishment by Gervase or his informant.

claims.statement: Gervase (as quoted by Keightley) writes that in England there is a certain kind of demon whom they call Grant in their language.
claims.statement_id: Gervase (dikutip Keightley) menulis bahwa di Inggris ada sejenis iblis (demon) yang dalam bahasa mereka disebut Grant.
claims.quote: in England a certain kind of demon whom in their language they call Grant

claims.statement: It looks like a yearling foal, erect on its hind legs, with sparkling eyes.
claims.statement_id: Ia berwujud seperti anak kuda berumur setahun, berdiri tegak dengan kaki belakang, bermata berkilau.
claims.quote: like a yearling foal, erect on its hind legs, with sparkling eyes.

claims.statement: If danger is impending the following day or night, it runs about the streets provoking the dogs to bark.
claims.statement_id: Bila ada bahaya yang mengancam pada hari atau malam berikutnya, ia berlari di jalan-jalan memancing anjing menggonggong.
claims.quote: If there is any danger impending on the following day or night, it runs about the streets provoking the dogs to bark

claims.statement: This illusion warns the inhabitants to beware of fire; the friendly demon terrifies those who see him but by his coming puts the ignorant on their guard.
claims.statement_id: Tipuan ini memperingatkan penduduk agar waspada terhadap api; iblis yang bersahabat itu menakuti orang yang melihatnya tetapi dengan kedatangannya membuat orang yang tidak tahu menjadi siaga.
claims.quote: This illusion warns the inhabitants to beware of fire, and the friendly demon, while he terrifies those who see him, puts by his coming the ignorant on their guard.

claims.statement: Gwedros Gawr (also Gwedraws or Gwaedros) was a giant (cawr) who, according to legend, lived at Caerwedros in Ceredigion.
claims.statement_id: Gwedros Gawr (juga Gwedraws atau Gwaedros) adalah raksasa (cawr) yang menurut legenda tinggal di Caerwedros di Ceredigion.
claims.quote: Cawr oedd Gwedros Gawr (hefyd, Gwedraws neu Gwaedros) a oedd, yn ôl chwedloniaeth, yn byw yng Nghaerwedros yng Ngheredigion.

claims.statement: Gwedros is named in the book of the 17th-century antiquarian Siôn Dafydd Rhys, which contains over fifty names of the giants (cewri) of Wales (Cymru).
claims.statement_id: Gwedros disebut dalam buku sang antikuaris abad ke-17 Siôn Dafydd Rhys, yang memuat lebih dari lima puluh nama raksasa (cewri) Wales (Cymru).
claims.quote: Mae Gwedros yn cael ei enwi yn llyfr yr hynafiaethydd o'r 17g Siôn Dafydd Rhys, sy'n cynnwys dros hanner cant o enwau cewri Cymru.

claims.statement: The book is part of the Peniarth Manuscripts collection (Peniarth 118) in the National Library of Wales (Llyfrgell Genedlaethol Cymru).
claims.statement_id: Buku itu bagian dari koleksi Naskah Peniarth (Peniarth 118) di Perpustakaan Nasional Wales (Llyfrgell Genedlaethol Cymru).
claims.quote: Mae'r llyfr yn rhan o gasgliad Llawysgrifau Peniarth (Peniarth 118) yn Llyfrgell Genedlaethol Cymru.

claims.statement: According to Rhys, in the land of Aberteifi and the parish of Llan Dyssiliaw is a place called Caer Wedros, named so because Gwedros Gawr once lived there.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Rhys, di negeri Aberteifi dan paroki Llan Dyssiliaw ada tempat bernama Caer Wedros, yang dinamai demikian karena Gwedros Gawr dahulu tinggal di sana.
claims.quote: In the land of Aberteifi and in the parish of Llan Dyssiliaw is a place called Caer Wedros. And that caer was called thus, and is still so called because Gwedros Gawr formerly lived there.

claims.statement: Caerwedros is a small village in western Ceredigion, Wales, in the community of Llandysiliogogo.
claims.statement_id: Caerwedros adalah desa kecil di Ceredigion barat, Wales, di komunitas Llandysiliogogo.
claims.quote: is a small village in western Ceredigion, Wales, in the community of Llandysiliogogo.

claims.statement: The site of Caerwedros Castle is today a mound of earth on the west side of the village.
