claims.quote: The site of Caerwedros Castle, is today a mound of earth on the west side of the village.

claims.statement: According to folklorist Wirt Sikes, the gwyllion are female fairies of frightful aspect who haunt lonely roads in the Welsh mountains and lead travellers astray.
claims.statement_id: Menurut folkloris Wirt Sikes, gwyllion adalah peri perempuan berwujud menakutkan yang menghantui jalan sepi di pegunungan Wales dan menyesatkan pengelana.
claims.quote: According to folklorist Wirt Sikes the gwyllion are female fairies of frightful aspect who haunt lonely roads in the Welsh mountains and lead travellers astray.

claims.statement: They are gloomy spirits more akin to hags or witches, as distinct from the Welsh ellyllon (elves), which are more benevolent.
claims.statement_id: Mereka roh muram yang lebih mirip hag atau penyihir, berbeda dari ellyllon (elf) Wales yang lebih baik hati.
claims.quote: They are gloomy spirits more akin to hags or witches, as distinct from the Welsh ellyllon (elves) that are more benevolent.

claims.statement: One gwyll in particular was known as the Old Woman of the Mountain who haunted Llanhyddel Mountain in Monmouthshire.
claims.statement_id: Satu gwyll yang khusus dikenal sebagai Old Woman of the Mountain (Perempuan Tua dari Gunung) menghantui Gunung Llanhyddel di Monmouthshire.
claims.quote: One gwyll in particular was known as the Old Woman of the Mountain who haunted Llanhyddel Mountain in Monmouthshire

claims.statement: Those who met them by night or on a misty day were sure to lose their way even if perfectly familiar with the road.
claims.statement_id: Orang yang bertemu mereka pada malam hari atau hari berkabut pasti tersesat, sekalipun sangat hafal jalannya.
claims.quote: Those who encountered them either by night or on a misty day would be sure to lose their way even if they were perfectly familiar with the road.

claims.statement: Welsh ghosts and fairies were afraid of knives and could be banished by them.
claims.statement_id: Hantu dan peri Wales takut pada pisau dan dapat diusir dengan pisau.
claims.quote: Welsh ghosts and fairies were afraid of knives and could be banished by them.

claims.statement: The Gwyllion appears as the main antagonist in the 2013 CGI animated film Barbie: Mariposa and the Fairy Princess.
claims.statement_id: Gwyllion tampil sebagai antagonis utama dalam film animasi CGI 2013 Barbie: Mariposa and the Fairy Princess.
claims.quote: The Gwyllion is featured as the main antagonist in the 2013 CGI animated film Barbie: Mariposa and the Fairy Princess.

claims.statement: The Gwyllion are female fairies of frightful characteristics who haunt lonely roads in the Welsh mountains and lead night-wanderers astray.
claims.statement_id: Gwyllion adalah peri perempuan berciri menakutkan yang menghantui jalan sepi di pegunungan Wales dan menyesatkan para pengembara malam.
claims.quote: The Gwyllion are female fairies of frightful characteristics, who haunt lonely roads in the Welsh mountains, and lead night-wanderers astray.

claims.statement: The Welsh word gwyll is variously used to signify gloom, shade, duskiness, a hag, a witch, a fairy and a goblin.
claims.statement_id: Kata Welsh gwyll dipakai dengan beragam arti: kemuraman, bayangan, kegelapan senja, hag, penyihir, peri, dan goblin.
claims.quote: The Welsh word gwyll is variously used to signify gloom, shade, duskiness, a hag, a witch, a fairy, and a goblin

claims.statement: Its special application is to these mountain fairies of gloomy and harmful habits, as distinct from the Ellyllon of the forest glades and dingles, which are more often beneficent.
claims.statement_id: Pemakaian khususnya ialah untuk peri-peri gunung yang berkebiasaan muram dan merugikan, berbeda dari Ellyllon di padang hutan dan lembah, yang lebih sering baik hati.
claims.quote: but its special application is to these mountain fairies of gloomy and harmful habits, as distinct from the Ellyllon of the forest glades and dingles, which are more often beneficent.

claims.statement: The Old Woman of the Mountain typifies all her kind.
claims.statement_id: Old Woman of the Mountain mewakili seluruh jenisnya.
claims.quote: and the Old Woman of the Mountain typifies all her kind.

claims.statement: The popular tradition in that district was that the Old Woman of the Mountain was the spirit of one Juan White, who lived time out of mind in those parts and was thought to be a witch.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi populer di daerah itu menyebut Old Woman of the Mountain adalah arwah seorang Juan White, yang hidup sejak dahulu kala di sana dan dianggap penyihir.
claims.quote: The popular tradition in that district was that the Old Woman of the Mountain was the spirit of one Juan White, who lived time out of mind in those parts, and was thought to be a witch

claims.statement: In Wales, according to Jones, the Gwyllion often came into the houses of the people at Aberystruth, especially in stormy weather.
claims.statement_id: Di Wales, menurut Jones, Gwyllion sering masuk ke rumah penduduk di Aberystruth, terutama saat cuaca badai.
claims.quote: In Wales, according to Jones, the Gwyllion often came into the houses of the people at Aberystruth, especially in stormy weather

claims.statement: Inmates welcomed them by providing clean water and taking care that no knife or cutting tool lay in the corner near the fire where the fairies sat.
claims.statement_id: Penghuni menyambut mereka dengan menyediakan air bersih dan memastikan tidak ada pisau atau alat pemotong di sudut dekat api tempat para peri duduk.
claims.quote: providing clean water for them, and taking especial care that no knife, or other cutting tool, should be in the corner near the fire, where the fairies would go to sit.

claims.statement: So he drew out his knife, and the fairies vanished directly.
claims.statement_id: Maka ia menghunus pisaunya, dan para peri langsung lenyap.
claims.quote: So he drew out his knife, and the fairies vanished directly.

claims.statement: A man tried to overtake her but she led him further astray, always out of reach, until he found himself in a marsh.
claims.statement_id: Seorang pria mencoba menyusulnya, tetapi ia justru menuntun pria itu semakin tersesat, selalu di luar jangkauan, sampai pria itu berada di rawa.
claims.quote: He tried to overtake her but she led him further astray, always out of reach, until he found himself in a marsh.

claims.statement: In Breton folklore the being is called Iannic-ann-ôd or Yannig an Aod.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Breton, makhluk ini disebut Iannic-ann-ôd atau Yannig an Aod.
claims.quote: In Breton folklore, Iannic-ann-ôd or Yannig an Aod

claims.statement: Iannic-ann-ôd are said to be the lost souls of those drowned at sea who were never recovered.
claims.statement_id: Iannic-ann-ôd dikatakan sebagai jiwa-jiwa tersesat orang-orang yang tenggelam di laut dan jasadnya tidak pernah ditemukan.
claims.quote: are said to be the lost souls of those drowned at sea and were never recovered.

claims.statement: The drowned (les noyés) whose bodies were not found and buried in sacred ground wander eternally along the coasts.
claims.statement_id: Orang tenggelam (les noyés) yang jasadnya tidak ditemukan dan dikubur di tanah suci mengembara selamanya menyusuri pantai.
claims.quote: Les noyés, dont le corps n’a pas été retrouvé et enseveli en terre sacrée, errent éternellement le long des côtes.

claims.statement: It is not rare to hear them cry out dismally in the night (crier, dans la nuit, lugubrement), with the call "Iou! Iou!".
claims.statement_id: Tidak jarang mereka terdengar menjerit pilu pada malam hari (crier, dans la nuit, lugubrement), dengan seruan "Iou! Iou!".
claims.quote: Il n’est pas rare qu’on les entende crier, dans la nuit, lugubrement :

claims.statement: The cry goes that Iannic-ann-ôd, "Petit-Jean de la grève" (Little John of the shore), is howling.
claims.statement_id: Di pelosok Cornouailles orang berseru bahwa Iannic-ann-ôd, "Petit-Jean de la grève" (Jean Kecil dari pantai), sedang melolong.
claims.quote: E-man-Iannic-ann-ôd o iouall ! (Voilà Iannic-ann-ôd, — Petit-Jean de la grève, — qui hurle !)

claims.statement: The phrase is spoken in the country of Cornouailles (pays de Cornouailles).
claims.statement_id: Ungkapan itu diucapkan di wilayah Cornouailles (pays de Cornouailles).
claims.quote: On dit alors, dans le pays de Cornouailles :

claims.statement: All these howling drowned are instinctively called Iannic-ann-ôd.
claims.statement_id: Semua orang tenggelam yang melolong itu secara naluriah disebut Iannic-ann-ôd.
claims.quote: Tous ces noyés hurleurs sont instinctivement appelés Iannic-ann-ôd.

claims.statement: Iannic-ann-ôd is not wicked (n'est pas méchant), provided one does not amuse oneself by sending back his sinister lament.
claims.statement_id: Iannic-ann-ôd tidak jahat (n'est pas méchant), asalkan orang tidak iseng membalas ratapannya yang suram.
claims.quote: Iannic-ann-ôd n’est pas méchant, pourvu qu’on ne s’amuse pas à lui renvoyer sa plainte sinistre.

claims.statement: If answered once he leaps half the distance toward you; a second time, half of the remainder; a third time, he breaks your neck (vous rompt le cou).
claims.statement_id: Jika dijawab sekali, ia melompat setengah jarak ke arah orang itu; jika dijawab kedua kali, setengah dari sisa jarak; jika dijawab ketiga kali, ia mematahkan leher orang itu (vous rompt le cou).
claims.quote: si vous répondez une première fois, Iannic-ann-ôd franchit d’un bon la moitié de la distance qui le sépare de vous ; si vous répondez une deuxième fois, il franchit la moitié de cette moitié ; si vous répondez une troisième fois, il vous rompt le cou.

claims.statement: In one tale a farm servant (domestique de ferme) was coming back from driving the animals to the fields one summer evening.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu cerita, seorang pelayan pertanian (domestique de ferme) pulang dari menggiring ternak ke ladang pada suatu malam musim panas.
claims.quote: Un domestique de ferme revenait de conduire les bêtes aux champs, un soir d’été, dans le temps où l’on commence à leur faire passer les nuits dehors.

claims.statement: The servant waited until he was close to the farm before answering the shrill "Iou" calls of the beach prowler (rôdeur de plages) behind him.
claims.statement_id: Pelayan itu menunggu sampai cukup dekat dengan pertanian sebelum menjawab seruan "Iou" yang nyaring dari sang pengembara pantai (rôdeur de plages) di belakangnya.
claims.quote: il attendit d’être assez près de la ferme, avant de répondre aux « Iou » stridents, que poussait derrière lui le rôdeur de plages.

claims.statement: After the third answer a tremendous blow struck the door from outside, as if it were flying to pieces (volait en éclats).
claims.statement_id: Setelah jawaban ketiga, sebuah pukulan dahsyat menghantam pintu dari luar hingga seakan pecah berkeping-keping (volait en éclats).
claims.quote: Un formidable coup s’abattit du dehors sur la porte ; on eût juré qu’elle volait en éclats.

claims.statement: The voice outside threatens: it will pass this once, but if the servant tries it again he will be made "un homme".
claims.statement_id: Suara di luar mengancam: kali ini dimaafkan, tetapi jika pelayan itu mengulanginya, ia akan dijadikan "un homme" (manusia, dalam nada ancaman).
claims.quote: Passe pour une fois : mais si tu y reviens, je ferai de toi un homme !

claims.statement: The Little People of the Pryor Mountains (known as Nirumbee or Awwakkulé in the Crow language) are a race of ferocious dwarfs in the folklore of the Crow Tribe, a Native American tribe.
claims.statement_id: Little People of the Pryor Mountains (disebut Nirumbee atau Awwakkulé dalam bahasa Crow) adalah ras kurcaci (dwarfs) ganas dalam cerita rakyat Suku Crow, suku asli Amerika.
claims.quote: The Little People of the Pryor Mountains (known as Nirumbee or Awwakkulé in the Crow language) are a race of ferocious dwarfs in the folklore of the Crow Tribe, a Native American tribe.

claims.statement: According to Crow folklore they live in the Pryor Mountains, a small mountain range in Carbon County and Bighorn County, Montana.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat Crow mereka tinggal di Pryor Mountains, pegunungan kecil di Carbon County dan Bighorn County, Montana.
claims.quote: live in the Pryor Mountains, a small mountain range in Carbon County, Montana and Bighorn County, Montana.

claims.statement: The Crow said petroglyphs on rocks in the mountains were made by these demon-like creatures, and because the Little People live there the mountains are sacred to the Crow.
claims.statement_id: Orang Crow mengatakan petroglif di bebatuan pegunungan itu dibuat oleh makhluk mirip iblis ini, dan karena mereka tinggal di sana, pegunungan itu suci bagi Crow.
claims.quote: Petroglyphs on rocks in the mountains, the Crow said, were made by these demon-like creatures. Because the Little People live there, the mountains are sacred to the Crow.

claims.statement: The Pryor Mountains Little People were also known for stealing children, food, medicine and tobacco.
claims.statement_id: Little People Pryor Mountains juga dikenal mencuri anak, makanan, obat, dan tembakau.
claims.quote: The Pryor Mountains Little People were also known for stealing children, food, medicine, and tobacco.

claims.statement: The Crow also believed the Little People made stone arrowheads, since the Crow themselves knew only how to make bone arrowheads.
claims.statement_id: Orang Crow juga percaya Little People membuat mata panah batu, karena Crow sendiri hanya bisa membuat mata panah tulang.
claims.quote: The Crow also believed that the Little People created stone arrowheads, for the Crow themselves only knew how to make bone arrowheads.

claims.statement: Generally the Crow would refuse to enter the Pryor Mountains because of their belief in the Little People.
claims.statement_id: Pada umumnya orang Crow enggan memasuki Pryor Mountains karena kepercayaan mereka pada Little People.
claims.quote: Generally speaking, the Crow would refuse to enter the Pryor Mountains due to their belief in the Little People.

claims.statement: Other offerings such as beads, cloth or tobacco could also be left to win safe passage through the mountains.
claims.statement_id: Persembahan lain seperti manik, kain, atau tembakau juga bisa ditinggalkan agar mendapat jalan aman melewati pegunungan itu.
claims.quote: However, other kinds of offerings, such as beads, cloth, or tobacco, could also be left in order to win safe passage through the mountains.

claims.statement: The Little People were also integral to the Crow practice of the Sun Dance.
claims.statement_id: Little People juga merupakan bagian penting dari praktik Sun Dance suku Crow.
claims.quote: The Little People also were integral to the Crow practice of the Sun Dance.

claims.statement: The Little People are said to be no more than 18 inches (46 cm), or knee, high.
claims.statement_id: Little People dikatakan tidak lebih tinggi dari 18 inci (46 cm), atau setinggi lutut.
claims.quote: The Little People are said to be no more than 18 inches (46 cm) (or knee) high.

claims.statement: They are described as incredibly strong but with short arms and legs and little or no neck.
claims.statement_id: Mereka digambarkan sangat kuat tetapi berlengan dan berkaki pendek, dan nyaris tanpa leher.
claims.quote: and incredibly strong but short arms and legs; and little or no neck.

claims.statement: In the vision the chief of the Little People also prophesied that Plenty Coups would become chief of his people if he used his wits.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penglihatan, kepala Little People juga menubuatkan bahwa Plenty Coups akan menjadi kepala suku jika menggunakan akalnya.
claims.quote: He also prophesied that Plenty Coups would become chief of his people, if he used his wits

claims.statement: Each year the Crow made an offering to the Little People at Medicine Rocks.
claims.statement_id: Setiap tahun orang Crow memberi persembahan kepada Little People di Medicine Rocks.
claims.quote: Each year, the Crow made an offering to the Little People at Medicine Rocks

claims.statement: The Little People of the Pryor Mountains have been known to the Crow for generations; to many they are spiritual guides and helpers, to others they are considered mischievous and to be avoided.
claims.statement_id: Little People Pryor Mountains telah dikenal orang Crow selama beberapa generasi; bagi banyak orang mereka pemandu spiritual dan penolong, bagi yang lain mereka dianggap jahil dan harus dihindari.
claims.quote: The Little People of the Pryor Mountains have been known to the Crow for generations; to many they are spiritual guides and helpers of the Crow, to others they are considered mischievous and are to be avoided.

claims.statement: However they are thought of, the Crow teach respect for these powerful beings, who are to be treated as Elders.
claims.statement_id: Apa pun anggapan orang, Crow mengajarkan hormat kepada makhluk-makhluk berkuasa ini; mereka harus diperlakukan sebagai Elders (tetua).
claims.quote: Regardless of how they are thought of, the Crow teach respect for these powerful beings; they are to be treated as Elders.

claims.statement: In one story the Little People adopted a Crow boy at a very young age when he was lost in the Pryor Mountains, separated from his Crow family.
claims.statement_id: Dalam salah satu kisah, Little People mengadopsi seorang anak lelaki Crow yang masih sangat kecil ketika ia tersesat di Pryor Mountains, terpisah dari keluarganya.
claims.quote: The Little People adopted a Crow boy at a very young age when he was lost in the Pryor Mountains, separated from his Crow family.

claims.statement: The Crow were told to shoot arrows at the face of the cliff as they passed for safe passage to their destination, giving the place the name Arrow Rock.
claims.statement_id: Orang Crow diminta menembakkan panah ke wajah tebing saat lewat demi jalan aman menuju tujuan, sehingga tempat itu dinamai Arrow Rock.
claims.quote: They were told to shoot arrows at the face of the cliff, giving the place the name Arrow Rock, as they passed by for safe passage to their final destination.

claims.statement: They were also instructed to pile rocks at the base of the cliff as prayer offerings, leave meat for the Little People to eat, and women were told to leave beads and jewelry for the Little Women to wear.
claims.statement_id: Mereka juga diperintahkan menumpuk batu di kaki tebing sebagai persembahan doa, meninggalkan daging untuk dimakan Little People, dan perempuan meninggalkan manik dan perhiasan untuk Little Women.
claims.quote: They were also instructed to pile rocks at the base of the cliff as prayer offerings, leave meat for the Little People to eat, and women were told to leave beads and jewelry for the Little Women to find and wear.

claims.statement: The Little People are described as dwarves that are both human and supernatural beings and can act as spiritual guides for the Crow Tribe.
claims.statement_id: Little People digambarkan sebagai kurcaci yang sekaligus manusia dan makhluk gaib dan dapat menjadi pemandu spiritual bagi Suku Crow.
claims.quote: The Little People are described as dwarves that are both human and supernatural beings that can act as spiritual guides for the Crow Tribe.

claims.statement: They have been described as between twenty inches and 4 feet in height and looking like miniature adults, hence the name Little People.
claims.statement_id: Mereka digambarkan setinggi antara dua puluh inci dan 4 kaki dan tampak seperti orang dewasa mini, sehingga dinamai Little People.
claims.quote: They have been described as being between twenty inches and 4 feet in height and look like adults in miniature size, hence the name Little People.

claims.statement: Based on Crow oral histories, Arrow Shot Into Rock is the place where the Crow first met the Little People.
claims.statement_id: Berdasarkan sejarah lisan Crow, Arrow Shot Into Rock adalah tempat orang Crow pertama kali bertemu Little People.
claims.quote: Based on Crow oral histories Arrow Shot Into Rock is the place where the Crow encountered the Little People for the first time.

claims.statement: In Irish folklore (folklore irlandais), the Lurikeen is a lutin (sprite) and familiar spirit of tinkers (itinerant tinsmiths), linked to misery and defeats.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Irlandia (folklore irlandais), Lurikeen adalah lutin (peri kecil) sekaligus roh pendamping para "tinker" (tukang kaleng keliling), dikaitkan dengan kesengsaraan dan kekalahan.
claims.quote: Dans le folklore irlandais ... le Lurikeen est un lutin et esprit familier des « tinkers » (ferblantiers itinérants), lié à la misère et aux défaites.

claims.statement: In the Kildare tale the Lurikeen is shown working like vengeance at a little old brogue only fit for the foot of a fairy.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Kildare, Lurikeen digambarkan duduk di bawah pohon hawthorn tua, bekerja keras memperbaiki sepatu kecil tua yang hanya pantas untuk kaki peri.
claims.quote: the Lurikeen, working like vengeance at a little old brogue only fit for the foot of a fairy like himself.

claims.statement: He bores his holes and jerks his waxed ends, wearing a little three-cornered hat with gold lace and knee-breeches, with a jug of beer at his side and a pipe in his mouth.
claims.statement_id: Ia melubangi sepatu dan menarik benang berlilin, memakai topi kecil bersudut tiga berhias renda emas, celana selutut, dengan kendi bir di sampingnya dan pipa di mulut.
claims.quote: There he was, boring his holes, and jerking his waxed ends, with his little three-cornered hat with gold lace, his knee-breeches, his jug of beer by his side, and his pipe in his mouth.

claims.statement: He was so busy at his work and so taken up singing an old ballad in Irish that he did not notice Breedheen until she had him by the scruff of the neck.
claims.statement_id: Ia begitu sibuk bekerja dan asyik menyanyikan balada lama dalam bahasa Irlandia sampai tidak menyadari Breedheen sudah menangkap tengkuknya.
claims.quote: He was so busy at his work, and so taken up with an old ballad he was singing in Irish, that he did not mind Breedheen till she had him by the scruff o' the neck

claims.statement: The girl demands the Lurikeen's money and refuses to take hand or eye from him until she has a fine lob of it.
claims.statement_id: Gadis itu menuntut uang Lurikeen dan menolak melepaskan tangan atau mata darinya sampai ia mendapat segenggam besar.
claims.quote: It's your money I want, and I won't take hand or eye from you till you put me in possession of a fine lob of it.

claims.statement: At the brow of the hill the Lurikeen looked over the ditch, gave a great screech and shouted as if a bugle horn were blown at her ears, crying that Castle Carberry was afire.
claims.statement_id: Di puncak bukit kecil, Lurikeen menengok ke atas parit dan menjerit keras seperti bunyi terompet di telinga gadis itu, berseru bahwa Castle Carberry terbakar.
claims.quote: he looked up over the ditch, gave a great screetch, and shouted just as if a bugle horn was blew at her ears

claims.statement: The moment she turned to the castle she lost the weight of the Lurikeen, and he vanished without a trace, as if it had all been a dream.
claims.statement_id: Saat gadis itu menoleh ke kastil, ia kehilangan bobot Lurikeen di tangannya dan makhluk itu lenyap tanpa jejak, seakan semuanya mimpi.
claims.quote: The same moment she missed the weight of the Lurikeen, and when her eyes fell where he was a moment before, there was no more sign of him than if everything that passed was a dream.

claims.statement: The only instance of a Wexford Lurikeen the author can recall differs only slightly from this Kildare tale.
claims.statement_id: Satu-satunya contoh Lurikeen dari Wexford yang diingat penulis hanya berbeda sedikit dari kisah Kildare ini.
claims.quote: The only instance of a Wexford Lurikeen that we can recall, differs only slightly from this.

claims.statement: Wexford Molly was as vigilant as Kildare Biddy and did not take eye or hand off him until he pointed out the very stalk of booliaun bui under which the treasure lay.
claims.statement_id: Molly dari Wexford sama waspadanya dengan Biddy dari Kildare dan tidak melepaskan tangan atau mata sampai Lurikeen menunjukkan batang booliaun bui tempat harta terkubur.
claims.quote: Wexford Molly was as vigilant as Kildare Biddy, and never took eye or hand off him till he pointed out the very stalk of booliaun bui under which the treasure lay.

claims.statement: When Molly returned half an hour later with her father and brothers carrying spades and picks, the whole spot was as thick with booliauns as a plantation of young trees.
claims.statement_id: Ketika Molly kembali setengah jam kemudian bersama ayah dan saudara-saudaranya membawa sekop dan beliung, seluruh area itu sudah penuh booliaun seperti kebun pohon muda.
claims.quote: when Molly returned in half an hour, attended by father and brothers with spades and picks, all round the spot, to a considerable distance, was as thick with booliauns as a plantation with young trees.

claims.statement: Maelor Gawr is an early Celtic king and giant of Welsh mythology.
claims.statement_id: Maelor Gawr adalah raja Kelt awal sekaligus raksasa dalam mitologi Wales.
claims.quote: Maelor Gawr is an early Celtic king and giant of Welsh mythology

claims.statement: The tale of Maelor and his three sons, Cornippyn, Crygyn and Bwba, is recorded in a late sixteenth-century Welsh text.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Maelor dan ketiga putranya, Cornippyn, Crygyn, dan Bwba, tercatat dalam teks Wales akhir abad ke-16.
claims.quote: The tale of Maelor and his three sons, Cornippyn, Crygyn and Bwba, is recorded in the late sixteenth century Welsh text

claims.statement: The older text uses the antiquarian spelling Maylor Gawr.
claims.statement_id: Teks lama menulis namanya dengan ejaan antikuaris Maylor Gawr.
claims.quote: with the antiquarian spelling Maylor Gawr

claims.statement: On the third blast the intensity of the sound caused the horn to break into small pieces.
claims.statement_id: Pada tiupan ketiga, kerasnya bunyi membuat tanduk itu pecah berkeping-keping.
claims.quote: On the third blast of his horn the intensity of the force of the sound caused the horn to be broken into small pieces.

claims.statement: The other sons, Crygyn and Bwba, lived in Llanilar and Llanbadarn Fawr respectively and murdered any man who approached their stronghold.
claims.statement_id: Putra lainnya, Crygyn dan Bwba, tinggal masing-masing di Llanilar dan Llanbadarn Fawr dan membunuh siapa pun yang mendekati benteng mereka.
claims.quote: The other sons, Crygyn and Bwba, lived in Llanilar and Llanbadarn Fawr respectively, and murdered any man who approached their stronghold.

claims.statement: Contemporary stories still tell of one of the more unusual residents of Penparcau village, the headless dog of the son of King Maelor.
claims.statement_id: Cerita masa kini masih mengisahkan salah satu penghuni Penparcau yang tak biasa, anjing tanpa kepala milik putra Raja Maelor.
claims.quote: Contemporary stories still relate to one of the more unusual residents of Penparcau village, the headless dog of King Maelor

claims.statement: According to Rhys, in the country of Aberteifi before Brutus came to this island there lived Maylor Gawr, and his dwelling is still called Castell Maylor.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Rhys, di negeri Aberteifi sebelum kedatangan Brutus ke pulau ini pernah tinggal Maylor Gawr, dan tempat tinggalnya masih disebut Castell Maylor.
claims.quote: And in the country of Aberteifi, before the coming of Brutus to this island, there formerly lived Maylor Gawr, and the place where he lived is still called Castell Maylor

claims.statement: Maylor Gawr had three sons: Cornippin Gawr, Crygyn Gawr and Bwba Gawr.
claims.statement_id: Maylor Gawr memiliki tiga putra: Cornippin Gawr, Crygyn Gawr, dan Bwba Gawr.
claims.quote: To this Maylor Gawr were three sons, namely, Cornippin Gawr, and Crygyn Gawr, and Bwba Gawr.

claims.statement: Maylor Gawr was taken prisoner at a place called Cyfeilog, about twelve miles from his own castle.
claims.statement_id: Maylor Gawr ditawan di tempat bernama Cyfeilog, sekitar dua belas mil dari kastilnya sendiri.
claims.quote: And it came to pass that Maylor Gawr was taken prisoner in a place called Cyfeilog, about twelve miles from his own castle

claims.statement: When about to be put to death he begged his enemies to let him blow his horn three times.
claims.statement_id: Saat hendak dihukum mati, ia memohon kepada musuhnya agar boleh meniup tanduknya tiga kali.
claims.quote: he begged of his enemies to permit him to blow his horn three times before suffering death

claims.statement: On the second blast, so great was the force of the sound that all his finger and toe-nails fell off.
claims.statement_id: Pada tiupan kedua, kekuatan bunyinya begitu besar hingga semua kuku jari tangan dan kakinya rontok.
claims.quote: And on the second blast of his horn, so great was the strength and force of the sounding that all his finger and toe-nails fell off completely.

claims.statement: Cornippin rode with such haste and swiftness that he tore the head of his hound from its body.
claims.statement_id: Cornippin menunggang dengan begitu tergesa dan cepat hingga kepala anjing pemburunya terlepas dari tubuhnya.
claims.quote: in riding with such haste and swiftness, he tore the head of his hound off its body

claims.statement: He spurred his steed until the horse leapt in a single bound over the Ystwyth River.
claims.statement_id: Ia memacu kudanya sampai kuda itu melompat dalam satu lompatan melewati Sungai Ystwyth.
claims.quote: he spurred his steed until the horse leapt at one bound over the Ystwyth River

claims.statement: Cornippin reached his father and, after fighting, was also killed.
claims.statement_id: Cornippin sampai ke ayahnya, dan setelah bertarung ia pun terbunuh.
claims.quote: Cornippin came up to his father, where after fighting he also was killed.

claims.statement: These giants lived in Wales before Brutus came to this island, and their custom was to kill whatever men came to lodge within their strongholds.
claims.statement_id: Raksasa-raksasa ini hidup di Wales sebelum Brutus datang ke pulau ini, dan kebiasaan mereka ialah membunuh siapa saja yang datang menginap di benteng mereka.
claims.quote: These giants lived in Wales before Brutus came to this island, and their custom while they lived was to kill whatever men should come to lodge within their strongholds

claims.statement: Petticoat Loose is the spirit or ghost (taibhse) of a woman who features in the folklore (béaloideas) of Munster (Mumhan).
claims.statement_id: Petticoat Loose adalah roh atau hantu (taibhse) seorang perempuan yang menjadi tokoh cerita dalam cerita rakyat (béaloideas) Munster (Mumhan).
claims.quote: Is éard atá i gceist le Petticoat Loose ná sprid nó taibhse mná agus í ina hábhar scéalta i mbéaloideas na Mumhan.

claims.statement: Petticoat Loose is believed to attack travellers (taistealaithe) at night, frightening and tormenting them.
claims.statement_id: Dipercaya Petticoat Loose menyerang para pelancong (taistealaithe) pada malam hari, menakut-nakuti dan menyiksa mereka.
claims.quote: Mar a chreidtear, bíonn Petticoat Loose ag ionsaí taistealaithe istoíche, á n-imeaglú agus á gcrá.

claims.statement: Béal Locha in County Waterford (Contae Phort Láirge) is named as her home place, though some say she was from Coilleagán in the same county, and folklore says she can be seen throughout Munster.
claims.statement_id: Béal Locha di Contae Phort Láirge (County Waterford) disebut tempat asalnya, meski ada yang mengatakan dari Coilleagán di county yang sama, dan cerita rakyat menyebut ia terlihat di seluruh Munster.
claims.quote: Is é Béal Locha, Contae Phort Láirge, is áit dúchais do Phetticoat (ach deirtear freisin gurb as Coilleagán sa chontae chéanna di), ach deir an béaloideas go mbíonn sí le feiceáil fud fad na Mumhan.

claims.statement: According to folklore Petticoat's name was Cáit (or Máire) Ní Annagáin, and she was married to a man surnamed Ó Scanláin.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat, nama Petticoat adalah Cáit (atau Máire) Ní Annagáin, dan ia menikah dengan seorang pria bermarga Ó Scanláin.
claims.quote: De réir an bhéaloidis is é an t-ainm agus an sloinne a bhí ar Phetticoat ná Cáit (nó Máire) Ní Annagáin, agus bhí sí pósta ar fhear dar shloinne Ó Scanláin.

claims.statement: Among the reasons given for her becoming a ghost: she was wild and angry and struck her own mother, and she killed an unbaptised child (leanbh gan bhaiste).
claims.statement_id: Sebab ia menjadi hantu antara lain: ia ganas dan pemarah serta memukul ibunya sendiri, dan ia membunuh seorang bayi yang belum dibaptis (leanbh gan bhaiste).
claims.quote: Bhí sí fiain feargach, agus bhuaileadh sí a máthair féin. Mharaigh sí leanbh gan bhaiste.

claims.statement: In one version her name comes from a night of entertainment when her skirt (sciorta) caught on a nail in the wall; she danced wildly until the skirt tore and only the petticoat was left.
claims.statement_id: Menurut satu versi, namanya berasal dari malam hiburan ketika roknya (sciorta) tersangkut paku di dinding; ia menari liar sampai rok itu robek dan hanya petticoat yang tersisa.
claims.quote: nuair a ghreamaigh a sciorta de thairne sa bhalla. Thosaigh sí ag damhsa go fiain, agus ansin réabadh an sciorta di, ionas nár fágadh ach an peireacót uirthi.

claims.statement: The Irish dramatist M. J. Molloy wrote a play titled Petticoat Loose in 1979.
claims.statement_id: Dramawan Irlandia M. J. Molloy menulis sebuah drama berjudul Petticoat Loose pada 1979.
claims.quote: Scríobh an drámadóir Éireannach M. J. Molloy dráma faoin teideal Petticoat Loose sa bhliain 1979.

claims.statement: In the dúchas.ie Schools' Collection, Petticoat Loose was an unfortunate woman killed on the road to Co. Kilkenny who then haunted it and would not let a car pass.
claims.statement_id: Dalam arsip Sekolah dúchas.ie, Petticoat Loose adalah perempuan malang yang dibunuh di jalan menuju Co. Kilkenny lalu menghantui jalan itu dan tidak membiarkan kereta lewat.
claims.quote: Petticoat Loose was an unfortunate woman. She was killed on the road to Co. Kilkenny, and then she haunted it. She would not let a car pass.

claims.statement: She told the priest she had killed her own child without baptism, and the priest said that was what damned her.
claims.statement_id: Perempuan itu mengaku telah membunuh anaknya sendiri tanpa baptis, dan pastor berkata itulah yang membuatnya terkutuk.
claims.quote: Then she told him that she had killed her own child without baptism, and the priest said that that was what damned her.

claims.statement: The priest said he would banish her to the Red Sea; she replied that if he did she would let no ship or steamer pass without drowning it.
claims.statement_id: Pastor berkata akan mengusirnya ke Laut Merah; ia menjawab bila itu dilakukan ia tidak akan membiarkan kapal atau kapal uap lewat tanpa tenggelam.
claims.quote: The priest said that he would banish her to the Red Sea. She said if he would she would not leave a ship or a steamer pass but she would drown.

claims.statement: Portunes, or Neptunes, are creatures of English folklore described only in the medieval Latin work Otia Imperialia by Gervase of Tilbury.
claims.statement_id: Portunes, atau Neptunes, adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Inggris yang hanya dijelaskan dalam karya Latin abad pertengahan Otia Imperialia oleh Gervase dari Tilbury.
claims.quote: Portunes, or Neptunes, are creatures of English folklore described only in the medieval Latin work Otia Imperialia by Gervase of Tilbury.

claims.statement: In Gervase's account Portunes enter peasant houses at night, warm themselves by the fire, and roast small frogs which they carry in their pockets.
claims.statement_id: Dalam catatan Gervase, Portunes memasuki rumah petani pada malam hari, menghangatkan diri di dekat api, dan memanggang katak kecil yang mereka bawa di saku.
claims.quote: Portunes enter peasant houses at night, warm themselves by the fire, and roast small frogs which they carry in their pockets.

claims.statement: K. M. Briggs classes them as a type of fairy, arguing that Gervase's account was the first description of small English fairies.
claims.statement_id: K. M. Briggs menggolongkan mereka sebagai sejenis peri dan berpendapat catatan Gervase adalah gambaran pertama tentang peri-peri kecil Inggris.
claims.quote: K. M. Briggs classes them as a type of fairy, arguing that Gervase's account was the first description of small English fairies.

claims.statement: C. C. Oman argues that the description of the size of the Portunes is corrupted because their size is incompatible with the housework they do.
claims.statement_id: C. C. Oman berpendapat bahwa keterangan ukuran Portunes keliru karena ukuran itu tidak sesuai dengan pekerjaan rumah yang mereka lakukan.
claims.quote: C. C. Oman argues that the description of the size of the Portunes is corrupted because the size of the creatures is incompatible with the housework they do

claims.statement: S. E. Banks and J. W. Binns dispute this, arguing that the manuscripts agree and Gervase clearly meant to describe them as very small.
claims.statement_id: S. E. Banks dan J. W. Binns membantahnya, dengan alasan naskah-naskah sepakat dan Gervase jelas bermaksud menggambarkan mereka sangat kecil.
claims.quote: S. E. Banks and J. W. Binns dispute this, arguing that the manuscripts are in agreement and Gervase clearly intended to describe them as very small.

claims.statement: Young considers a link between the English name and the Roman god Portunus but argues a direct relationship is unlikely because there is no evidence for a cult of Portunus in Roman Britain.
claims.statement_id: Young mempertimbangkan kaitan antara nama Inggris itu dan dewa Romawi Portunus, tetapi menilai hubungan langsung tidak mungkin karena tidak ada bukti pemujaan Portunus di Britania Romawi.
claims.quote: Young also considers a link between the English name and the Roman god Portunus, but argues that a direct relationship is unlikely because there is no evidence for a cult of Portunus in Roman Britain

claims.statement: Gervase (as quoted by Keightley) writes that in England there are certain demons, though he doubts whether to call them demons or figures of a secret and unknown generation, which the French call Neptunes and the English Portunes.
claims.statement_id: Gervase (dikutip Keightley) menulis bahwa di Inggris ada semacam iblis (demons), meski ia ragu apakah harus menyebutnya iblis atau sosok yang asal-usulnya rahasia dan tak diketahui; orang Prancis menyebutnya Neptunes, orang Inggris Portunes.
claims.quote: They have in England certain demons, though I know not whether I should call them demons or figures of a secret and unknown generation, which the French call Neptunes, the English Portunes.

claims.statement: It is their nature to embrace the simple life of comfortable farmers.
claims.statement_id: Sudah menjadi sifat mereka untuk menjalani hidup sederhana para petani yang berkecukupan.
claims.quote: It is their nature to embrace the simple life of comfortable farmers

claims.statement: They have the countenance of old men with wrinkled cheeks and are of very small stature, not quite half-an-inch high.
claims.statement_id: Mereka berwajah lelaki tua dengan pipi berkerut dan bertubuh sangat kecil, tingginya tidak sampai setengah inci.
claims.quote: They have the countenance of old men, with wrinkled cheeks, and they are of a very small stature, not being quite half-an-inch high.

claims.statement: If anything is to be carried into the house or any laborious work done, they lend a hand and finish it sooner than any man could; their nature is to have the power to serve but not to injure.
claims.statement_id: Bila ada barang yang harus dibawa ke rumah atau pekerjaan berat yang harus dilakukan, mereka membantu dan menyelesaikannya lebih cepat daripada manusia mana pun; sifat mereka berkuasa melayani tetapi tidak mencelakai.
claims.quote: if anything is to be carried into the house, or any laborious work to be done, they lend a hand, and finish it sooner than any man could. It is their nature to have the power to serve, but not to injure.

claims.statement: The Portune sometimes invisibly joins a lone horseman, at last takes the reins and leads the horse into a slough, then goes off with a loud laugh once the horse is floundering in it.
claims.statement_id: Portune kadang bergabung tanpa terlihat dengan penunggang kuda yang sendirian, akhirnya mengambil kendali dan menuntun kuda ke lumpur, lalu pergi dengan tawa keras ketika kuda itu terperosok.
claims.quote: the Portune sometimes invisibly joins the horseman; and when he has accompanied him a good while, he at last takes the reins, and leads the horse into a neighbouring slough; and when he is fixed and floundering in it, the Portune goes off with a loud laugh

claims.statement: Pyewacket was said to be one of the familiar spirits of a convicted witch accused by the self-styled Witchfinder General Matthew Hopkins in March 1644 in the town of Manningtree, Essex, England.
claims.statement_id: Pyewacket dikatakan salah satu roh pendamping (familiar) seorang penyihir terpidana yang dituduh oleh Matthew Hopkins, yang mengaku sebagai Witchfinder General, pada Maret 1644 di kota Manningtree, Essex, Inggris.
claims.quote: Pyewacket was said to be one of the familiar spirits of a convicted witch accused by the claimed Witchfinder General Matthew Hopkins in March 1644 in the town of Manningtree, Essex, England.

claims.statement: Hopkins claimed he spied on the witches as they held their meeting close by his house and heard them mention the name of a local woman.
claims.statement_id: Hopkins mengaku memata-matai para penyihir yang bertemu di dekat rumahnya dan mendengar mereka menyebut nama seorang perempuan setempat.
claims.quote: Hopkins claimed he spied on the witches as they held their meeting close by his house, and heard them mention the name of a local woman.

claims.statement: The woman was arrested and deprived of sleep for four nights, at the end of which she confessed and called out the names of her familiars, describing the forms in which they should appear.
claims.statement_id: Perempuan itu ditangkap dan dicegah tidur selama empat malam; pada akhirnya ia mengaku dan menyebut nama roh pendampingnya serta bentuk yang akan mereka ambil.
claims.quote: She was arrested and deprived of sleep for four nights, at the end of which she confessed and called out the names of her familiars, describing the forms in which they should appear.

claims.statement: Elemanzer, Pyewacket, Peck in the Crown and Grizzel Greedigut are listed as imps.
claims.statement_id: Wikipedia menyebut Elemanzer, Pyewacket, Peck in the Crown, dan Grizzel Greedigut sebagai imp (roh kecil).
claims.quote: Elemanzer, Pyewacket, Peck in the Crown, Grizzel Greedigut, described as imps

claims.statement: In the Hollywood film Bell, Book and Candle (1958), Pyewacket is the name of the brown sealpoint Siamese cat and familiar of Gillian Holroyd, a witch played by Kim Novak.
claims.statement_id: Dalam film Hollywood Bell, Book and Candle (1958), Pyewacket adalah nama kucing Siam cokelat sealpoint yang menjadi familiar Gillian Holroyd, penyihir yang diperankan Kim Novak.
claims.quote: In the Hollywood film Bell, Book and Candle (1958), Pyewacket is the name of the brown sealpoint Siamese cat / familiar of Gillian Holroyd, a witch played by Kim Novak.

claims.statement: Pyewacket is the title of a 2017 horror film.
claims.statement_id: Pyewacket adalah judul sebuah film horor 2017.
claims.quote: Pyewacket is a 2017 horror film.

claims.statement: Hopkins writes that in March 1644 some seven or eight witches lived in the town where he lived, a town in Essex called Maningtree.
claims.statement_id: Hopkins menulis bahwa pada Maret 1644 ada tujuh atau delapan penyihir tinggal di kotanya, sebuah kota di Essex bernama Maningtree.
claims.quote: in March 1644 he had some seven or eight of that horrible sect of Witches living in the Towne where he lived, a Towne in Essex called Maningtree

claims.statement: On the fourth night she called them in by their several names and told them what shapes to take, a quarter of an hour before they came in, ten of them being in the room.
claims.statement_id: Pada malam keempat perempuan itu memanggil roh-roh itu dengan nama masing-masing dan memberitahu bentuk yang akan mereka ambil seperempat jam sebelum masuk, dengan sepuluh orang hadir di ruangan.
claims.quote: which the fourth night she called in by their severall names, and told them what shapes, a quarter of an houre before they came in, there being ten of us in the roome

claims.statement: Immediately after, the witch confessed several other witches and named the imps' names, as Elemanzer, Pyewacket, Peckin the Crown, Grizzel, Greedigut, and so on.
claims.statement_id: Segera setelah itu penyihir tersebut mengaku adanya beberapa penyihir lain dan menyebut nama imp-imp, antara lain Elemanzer, Pyewacket, Peckin the Crown, Grizzel, Greedigut, dan seterusnya.
claims.quote: Immediately after this Witch confessed severall other Witches, from whom she had her Imps, and named to divers women where their marks were, the number of their Marks, and Imps, and Imps names, as Elemanzer, Pyewacket, Peckin the Crown, Grizzel, Greedigut, &c.

claims.statement: A stray sod is a clump of grass enchanted by faeries.
claims.statement_id: Stray sod adalah gumpalan rumput yang disihir oleh peri (faerie).
claims.quote: a stray sod is a clump of grass enchanted by faeries.

claims.statement: A person who steps on one becomes disoriented and lost, even in familiar surroundings.
claims.statement_id: Orang yang menginjaknya akan bingung dan tersesat, bahkan di tempat yang dikenalnya.
claims.quote: If a person steps on one, they will become disoriented and lost, even in familiar surroundings.

claims.statement: Wearing an item of clothing inside-out breaks the enchantment, allowing the person to find their way again.
claims.statement_id: Mengenakan pakaian terbalik memutus sihir itu sehingga orang bisa menemukan jalan lagi.
claims.quote: Wearing an item of clothing inside-out breaks the enchantment, allowing the person to find their way again.

claims.statement: The concept and phrase appear to originate in ancient Celtic mythology, specifically Irish folklore.
claims.statement_id: Konsep dan frasa ini tampaknya berasal dari mitologi Kelt kuno, khususnya cerita rakyat Irlandia.
claims.quote: The concept and phrase appear to originate in ancient Celtic mythology, specifically Irish folklore.

claims.statement: In more modern Christianized interpretations, the source of the enchantment may not be fairies.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tafsiran modern yang dikristenkan, sumber sihir itu mungkin bukan peri.
claims.quote: In more modern Christianized interpretations, the source of the enchantment may not be fairies.

claims.statement: Stray sods appear in the series The Spiderwick Chronicles, disorienting travelers.
claims.statement_id: Stray sod muncul dalam serial The Spiderwick Chronicles, membuat para pengelana tersesat.
claims.quote: Stray sods appear in the series The Spiderwick Chronicles, disorienting travelers.

claims.statement: The dúchas.ie Schools' Collection says there is a stray sod in Tom Lee's hill in Derreen, and several people went astray on it.
claims.statement_id: Dalam arsip Sekolah dúchas.ie dikatakan ada stray sod di bukit Tom Lee di Derreen, dan beberapa orang tersesat di atasnya.
claims.quote: There is said to be a stray sod in Tom Lee's hill in Derreen. Several people went astray on it.

claims.statement: One night Mick Winters was coming home late and went astray on it.
claims.statement_id: Suatu malam Mick Winters pulang larut dan tersesat di atasnya.
claims.quote: One night Mick Winters was coming home late and he went astray on it.

claims.statement: When he sat down a crowd of little red men came and got him to play cards.
claims.statement_id: Ketika ia duduk, sekumpulan lelaki kecil berpakaian merah datang dan mengajaknya bermain kartu.
claims.quote: And when he did so a crowd of little red men came and got him to play cards.

claims.statement: He said he must have walked on a fairies' pass.
claims.statement_id: Ia berkata mungkin ia telah berjalan di jalur peri (fairies pass).
claims.quote: He said he must have walked on a fairies pass.

claims.statement: The Black Dog of Newgate is a legend concerning the haunting of the former Newgate Prison of London, which stood next to the Old Bailey.
claims.statement_id: Black Dog of Newgate adalah legenda tentang hantu di bekas Penjara Newgate, London, yang terletak di sebelah Old Bailey.
claims.quote: The Black Dog of Newgate is a legend concerning the haunting of the former Newgate Prison of London, which was located next to the Old Bailey

claims.statement: The account is an example of the English Black Dog category of supernatural manifestations, featuring a spectral hound of ill omen or malicious intent.
claims.statement_id: Kisah ini contoh kategori Black Dog Inggris, yang menampilkan anjing pemburu hantu pertanda buruk atau berniat jahat.
claims.quote: is an example of the English Black Dog category of supernatural manifestations, featuring a spectral hound of ill-omen or malicious intent

claims.statement: The earliest recorded account of the legend dates from 1596 and is credited to a prison inmate called Luke Hutton.
claims.statement_id: Catatan tertua legenda ini berasal dari 1596 dan dikreditkan kepada narapidana bernama Luke Hutton.
claims.quote: the earliest recorded account of the legend dates from 1596, and is credited to a prison inmate called Luke Hutton.

claims.statement: In the story, during a famine in the reign of King Henry III of England, a scholar with the reputation of being a sorcerer was incarcerated in Newgate Prison.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita, saat kelaparan pada masa Raja Henry III dari Inggris, seorang cendekiawan yang dikenal sebagai penyihir dipenjara di Newgate.
claims.quote: during a famine in the reign of King Henry III of England, a scholar was incarcerated in Newgate Prison who had the reputation of being a sorcerer

claims.statement: Shortly after the crime, the inmates guilty of his death reportedly began seeing the spectre of a monstrous black dog walking up and down the prison.
claims.statement_id: Tak lama setelah kejahatan itu, para narapidana yang bersalah konon mulai melihat sosok hantu anjing hitam raksasa berjalan hilir mudik di penjara.
claims.quote: Shortly after this crime was committed, the inmates guilty of his death reportedly began seeing the spectre of a monstrous black dog walking up and down the Prison

claims.statement: This being reportedly killed and consumed those responsible one by one, until the last survivors, driven mad by fear, broke out of the gaol and escaped.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu konon membunuh dan memakan para pelaku satu per satu, sampai penyintas terakhir, gila karena takut, kabur dari penjara.
claims.quote: This being reportedly killed and consumed those responsible one by one, until the last survivors, driven mad by fear, broke out of the gaol and escaped.

claims.statement: Towards the end of the narrative the unnamed stranger claims the tale of the spiritual dog is untrue and that the only Black Dog he has heard of is a great blacke Stone standing in the dungeon.
claims.statement_id: Menjelang akhir narasi, orang asing tak bernama itu mengaku kisah anjing roh tidak benar, dan satu-satunya Black Dog yang ia dengar adalah batu hitam besar (great blacke Stone) di ruang bawah tanah.
claims.quote: Towards the end of the narrative the unnamed stranger claims that the tale of the spiritual dog is untrue, and that the only Black Dog he has heard any account of is a great blacke Stone standing in the dungeon called

claims.statement: The story was intended as a morality tale preaching against the low behaviour and base living of the prison's inmates.
claims.statement_id: Kisah ini dimaksudkan sebagai cerita moral yang menentang perilaku rendah dan hidup nista para narapidana.
claims.quote: Intended as a morality tale preaching against the low behaviour and base living of the inmates of the prison

claims.statement: There is some speculation whether this haunting is also connected to nearby Amen Court.
claims.statement_id: Ada spekulasi apakah hantu Black Dog of Newgate juga berkaitan dengan Amen Court di dekatnya.
claims.quote: There is some speculation as to whether this haunting of the Black Dog of Newgate is also connected to nearby Amen Court

claims.statement: This sinister legend is said to have originated in 1596 when a man was thrown into Newgate for dabbling in sorcery.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini dikatakan bermula pada 1596 ketika seorang lelaki dijebloskan ke Newgate karena bermain sihir.
claims.quote: This sinister legend is said to have originated in 1596 when a chap was thrown into Newgate for dabbling in sorcery.

claims.statement: Starving to death, some prisoners within Newgate had turned to cannibalism.
claims.statement_id: Karena kelaparan, sebagian narapidana di Newgate beralih ke kanibalisme.
claims.quote: Starving to death, some prisoners within Newgate had turned to cannibalism

claims.statement: Amen Court is said to be haunted by the dog, with many accounts describing a shapeless black form slithering along walls and giving off a hideous odour.
claims.statement_id: Amen Court dikatakan dihantui anjing itu; banyak laporan menyebut hantunya berupa bentuk hitam tak berbentuk yang menyelinap di dinding dan mengeluarkan bau menjijikkan.
claims.quote: It is said that Amen Court is haunted by the dog, with numerous accounts reporting that its ghost appears as a shapeless, black form, slithering along walls and giving off a hideous odour.

claims.statement: Witnesses often state that the apparition is accompanied by the sound of dragging footsteps.
claims.statement_id: Saksi sering menyatakan kemunculan itu disertai bunyi langkah diseret.
claims.quote: Whenever this apparition appears, witnesses often state that the visitation is accompanied by the sound of dragging footsteps.

claims.statement: Tiddy Mun was a legendary bog spirit in England believed able to control the waters and mists of the Fens of South Lincolnshire, the Carrs of North Lincolnshire and the fens of the Isle of Ely.
claims.statement_id: Tiddy Mun adalah roh rawa legendaris di Inggris yang dipercaya mampu mengendalikan air dan kabut di rawa-rawa South Lincolnshire, The Carrs di North Lincolnshire, dan rawa Isle of Ely.
claims.quote: Tiddy Mun was a legendary bog spirit in England, who was believed to have the ability to control the waters and mists of The Fens of South Lincolnshire, The Carrs of North Lincolnshire and fens of the Isle of Ely.

claims.statement: The belief in Tiddy Mun was first documented in June 1891 in an article by M. C. Balfour in the Folklore Society journal Folk-Lore.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan akan Tiddy Mun pertama kali didokumentasikan pada Juni 1891 dalam artikel M. C. Balfour di jurnal Folklore Society, Folk-Lore.
claims.quote: The belief in Tiddy Mun was first documented in June 1891 in an article by M. C. Balfour in the Folklore Society journal Folk-Lore.

claims.statement: In the article she recalls a story, collected in the Ancholme Valley, told to her by an older person.
claims.statement_id: Dalam artikel itu Balfour mengisahkan cerita yang dikumpulkan di Lembah Ancholme dan diceritakan oleh seorang yang lebih tua.
claims.quote: In the article she recalls a story, collected in the Ancholme Valley, told to her by an older person

claims.statement: In the story Tiddy Mun cast a curse of pestilence upon a village, angered at the draining of the Fens by the Dutch led by Cornelius Vermuyden in the seventeenth century.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita itu, Tiddy Mun menjatuhkan kutukan wabah pada sebuah desa karena marah atas pengeringan Fens oleh orang Belanda di bawah Cornelius Vermuyden pada abad ke-17.
claims.quote: a curse of pestilence that had been cast upon his village by the Tiddy Mun, who was angered at the draining of the Fens by the Dutch, led by Cornelius Vermuyden, in the seventeenth century.

claims.statement: According to the story Tiddy Mun was eventually placated after the villagers gathered at twilight at the new moon, poured buckets of water into the dyke and apologised for the damage caused.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita, Tiddy Mun akhirnya reda setelah penduduk berkumpul senja saat bulan baru, menuang ember air ke parit, dan meminta maaf atas kerusakan yang terjadi.
claims.quote: According to the story the Tiddy Mun was eventually placated after the villagers gathered at twilight at the time of the new moon, poured buckets of water into the dyke and apologised for the damage caused.

claims.statement: He was not exclusively malevolent: if the Fens flooded and the waters reached the villages, people would go out at night and call Tiddy Mun.
claims.statement_id: Ia tidak sepenuhnya jahat: bila Fens banjir dan air mencapai desa, orang keluar malam hari dan memanggil Tiddy Mun.
claims.quote: He was not exclusively malevolent; if the Fens flooded and the waters reached the villages, people would go out at night and call Tiddy Mun

claims.statement: Balfour in 1891 described Tiddy Mun as no bigger than a three-year-old child but looking like an old man with long, tangled white hair and a matted white beard.
claims.statement_id: Balfour pada 1891 menggambarkan Tiddy Mun tidak lebih besar daripada anak tiga tahun tetapi berpenampilan seperti lelaki tua berambut putih panjang kusut dan berjanggut putih kusut.
claims.quote: The Tiddy Mun was described, by folklorist M.C. Balfour in 1891, as being no bigger than a three-year-old child, but looking like an old man with long, tangled white hair and a matted white beard.

claims.statement: He is said to have worn a grey gown so that at dusk he was difficult to see, and his laughter was said to resemble the call of the peewit.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikatakan mengenakan jubah abu-abu sehingga sulit terlihat saat senja, dan tawanya konon menyerupai panggilan burung peewit.
claims.quote: He is said to have worn a grey gown so that at dusk he was difficult to see. His laughter was said to resemble the call of the peewit.

claims.statement: Writing in 1955, E. H. Rudkin records another Ancholme Valley belief in an imp-like race generally considered mischievous but benevolent.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1955 E. H. Rudkin mencatat kepercayaan Lembah Ancholme lain tentang ras makhluk mirip imp yang umumnya dianggap nakal tetapi baik hati.
claims.quote: Writing in 1955, folklorist E. H. Rudkin also records another Ancholme Valley belief of an imp-like race of beings who were generally considered mischievous but benevolent.

claims.statement: The Tiddy people would dance by moonlight on large flat stones known as Strangers Stones.
claims.statement_id: Orang Tiddy menari di bawah cahaya bulan di atas batu datar besar yang disebut Strangers Stones.
claims.quote: The Tiddy people would dance, by moonlight, on large flat stones, known as Strangers Stones, found in the area.

claims.statement: Darwin Horn argues that Tiddy Mun's curses may be connected to misfortune and disease brought about by the draining of the fenland.
claims.statement_id: Darwin Horn berpendapat kutukan-kutukan Tiddy Mun dapat dikaitkan dengan kemalangan dan penyakit akibat pengeringan lahan rawa.
claims.quote: may be connected to misfortune and disease brought about by the effect of draining the fenland.

claims.statement: In Balfour's dialect text Tiddy Mun dwelt in the water-holes (watter-holes), and the Dutch (Dutchies) were emptying them out.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks dialek Balfour, Tiddy Mun tinggal di lubang-lubang air (watter-holes), dan orang Belanda (Dutchies) sedang mengosongkannya.
claims.quote: Tiddy Mun dwelt i' tha watter-holes, an' noo tha Dutchies wor a emptyin' 'em out

claims.statement: He was called Tiddy Mun because he was none bigger than a three-year-old child (three year's bairn), but had no real name.
claims.statement_id: Ia disebut Tiddy Mun karena tidak lebih besar daripada anak berumur tiga tahun (three year's bairn), tetapi sebenarnya tidak punya nama.
claims.quote: for a wor none bigger 'n a three year's bairn, but a hadn't rightly no sort of a name

claims.statement: The old teller claims to have seen him limping by in the fog, all grey and white and screeching like the pyewipe (peewit).
claims.statement_id: Si penutur lama mengaku pernah melihatnya berjalan pincang di kabut, abu-abu dan putih, menjerit seperti burung pyewipe (peewit).
claims.quote: a've seen un mysel, limpin' by i' tha fog, all grey an' white an' screechin' like tha pyewipe

claims.statement: At every new moon people poured water into the dyke crying to Tiddy Mun without a name: "Here's watter for thee!" (here is water for thee).
claims.statement_id: Setiap bulan baru orang menuang air ke parit sambil berseru kepada Tiddy Mun tanpa nama: "Here's watter for thee!" (ini air untukmu).
claims.quote: Tiddy Mun wi-out a name Here's watter for thee !

claims.statement: The teller guesses Tiddy Mun has been frightened away by all the new ways and gear, so folk no longer know him.
claims.statement_id: Penutur menduga Tiddy Mun telah ketakutan dan pergi oleh cara-cara dan perkakas baru sehingga orang tak lagi mengenalnya.
claims.quote: Tiddy Mun 's bin' frighted away wi' a' tha new ways an' gear, for folk dinna ken un no more

issues.message: Diusulkan dilewati: Identitas 'Мойви (Moivi), roh air yang menenggelamkan pelaut dalam legenda Inggris' tidak dapat dipastikan. Satu-satunya artikel Wikipedia (bg: Мойви) ditandai pengelolanya sendiri sebagai tanpa sumber dan mungkin tidak lengkap, tidak akurat, atau seluruhnya keliru; isinya (kulit hijau, rambut seperti ganggang, 'gelombang kematian') tidak ditemukan di sumber lain mana pun. Pencarian web tidak menemukan tokoh bernama Moivi dalam cerita rakyat Inggris; ciri yang disebut mirip Jenny Greenteeth, tetapi menyamakannya adalah dugaan tanpa sumber. claims.statement: Yallery Brown is a mischievous fairy-like nature spirit in an old Lincolnshire folk tale from England, which is itself usually named after the creature.
claims.statement_id: Yallery Brown adalah roh alam jahil mirip peri dalam dongeng lama Lincolnshire di Inggris, yang dongengnya sendiri biasanya dinamai menurut makhluk itu.
claims.quote: Yallery Brown is a mischievous fairy-like nature spirit in an old Lincolnshire folk tale from England, which itself is usually named after the creature.

claims.statement: The story was first cited by M. C. Balfour in 1891 within a set of stories collected in the Ancholme Valley of North Lincolnshire and published in the Folklore Society journal Folklore.
claims.statement_id: Kisah ini pertama kali dikutip M. C. Balfour pada 1891 dalam kumpulan cerita dari Lembah Ancholme di North Lincolnshire, dan terbit di jurnal Folklore Society, Folklore.
claims.quote: This story was first cited by M C Balfour in 1891 within a set of stories collected in the Ancholme Valley of North Lincolnshire, and published in the Folklore Society journal Folklore

claims.statement: The story was also sent to Joseph Jacobs and included in his More English Fairy Tales.
claims.statement_id: Kisah itu juga dikirim kepada Joseph Jacobs dan dimuat dalam More English Fairy Tales.
claims.quote: The story was also sent to Joseph Jacobs and included in his More English Fairy tales.

claims.statement: In Balfour's version the teller speaks in the first person.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Balfour, penutur bercerita dengan sudut pandang orang pertama.
claims.quote: Balfour's tale has the teller speaking in first person.

claims.statement: In Jacobs's version, a young lad of eighteen or so named Tom Tiver worked on the Hall Farm.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Jacobs, ada seorang pemuda delapan belas tahun bernama Tom Tiver yang bekerja di Hall Farm.
claims.quote: there was a young lad of eighteen or so named Tom Tiver working on the Hall Farm.

claims.statement: After the stone is lifted, a tiddy thing lies on its back in the hole, blinking up at the moon and at Tom.
claims.statement_id: Setelah batu diangkat, di dalam lubang terbaring makhluk mungil (tiddy thing) telentang, berkedip menatap bulan dan Tom.
claims.quote: And there in the hole lay a tiddy thing on its back, blinking up at the moon and at him.

claims.statement: It had long matted hair and beard twisted round its body so that its clothes could not be seen.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu berambut dan berjanggut panjang kusut yang melilit tubuhnya sehingga pakaiannya tak terlihat.
claims.quote: but it had long cotted hair and beard, twisted round and round its body so that you couldn't see its clothes

claims.statement: Its skin was the colour of freshly turned earth in spring, brown as brown could be.
claims.statement_id: Kulitnya berwarna seperti tanah yang baru dibalik di musim semi, cokelat sekali.
claims.quote: the skin was the colour of the fresh turned earth in the spring—brown as brown could be

claims.statement: The creature himself tells Tom to call him Yallery Brown, "'t is my nature", and says it will do as a name like any other.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu sendiri menyuruh Tom menyebutnya Yallery Brown, "karena begitulah sifatku", dan menyebut nama itu cukup sebagai nama seperti yang lain.
claims.quote: Yallery Brown thou mayst call me, Yallery Brown; 't is my nature seest thou, and as for a name 't will do as any other.

claims.statement: Yallery Brown agrees to help but warns that if Tom ever thanks him, Tom will never see him more.
claims.statement_id: Yallery Brown bersedia membantu, tetapi bila Tom pernah berterima kasih kepadanya, Tom tidak akan melihatnya lagi.
claims.quote: I'll help thee and welcome, but if ever thou sayest that to me—if ever thou thankest me, see'st thou, thou 'lt never see me more.

claims.statement: Day after day all Tom's work was done by Yallery Brown, and better than Tom could have done it himself.
claims.statement_id: Hari demi hari semua pekerjaan Tom dikerjakan Yallery Brown, bahkan lebih baik daripada jika Tom mengerjakannya sendiri.
claims.quote: And so it went on day after day, all the work done by Yallery Brown, and better done, too, than he could have done it himself.

claims.statement: If Tom's work was done for him, the other lads' work was undone; his buckets were filled while theirs were upset.
claims.statement_id: Bila pekerjaan Tom dikerjakan, pekerjaan rekan-rekannya dirusak: ember Tom terisi, ember mereka ditumpahkan.
claims.quote: If the work was done for Tom, 't was undone for the other lads; if his buckets were filled, theirs were upset

claims.statement: Tom never saw Yallery Brown in daylight; only in the dark did he see him hopping about like a Will-o-th'-wyke without his lantern.
claims.statement_id: Tom tidak pernah melihat Yallery Brown pada siang hari; hanya dalam gelap ia melihatnya melompat-lompat seperti Will-o-th'-wyke tanpa lenteranya.
claims.quote: For he never saw Yallery Brown in daylight; only in the darklins he saw him hopping about, like a Will-o-th'-wyke without his lanthorn.

claims.statement: After Tom thanks him, the creature says he was safe under the stone and could do no harm, but Tom let him out himself and cannot put him back.
claims.statement_id: Setelah Tom berterima kasih, makhluk itu berkata ia dulu aman di bawah batu dan tak bisa mencelakai, tetapi Tom sendiri yang melepaskannya dan tak bisa menyimpannya kembali.
claims.quote: I was nice and safe under the stone, Tom, and could do no harm; but thou let me out thyself, and thou can't put me back again!

claims.statement: The curse came true: the children died, the crops rotted, the beasts never fattened, and nothing ever did well with Tom.
claims.statement_id: Kutukan itu terwujud: anak-anak meninggal, tanaman membusuk, ternak tak pernah gemuk, dan tak ada yang berhasil bagi Tom.
claims.quote: And the children died, and the crops rotted—the beasts never fatted, and nothing ever did well with him
